features.name: OpenAI Codex sessions
features.purpose: Run a session's turns on an OpenAI model through the codex CLI: device-code account login, the app-server engine, and the per-provider capability table every UI gate reads.
businessRules: $CODEX_HOME/auth.json is the only store of OpenAI secrets; Lines writes it exactly once at login and never again, because OpenAI rotates the refresh token on every refresh

reading that file is allowed and writing it twice is not — the usage poller reads the access token per request, never caches it, and a stale token empties the chip (no data until codex refreshes it) rather than being refreshed here
CODEX_HOME shadows the user's own ~/.codex/config.toml, so their terminal codex configuration does not apply inside Lines

a cross-provider setModel is refused once a session has run: nothing carries a conversation between a claudeSessionId and a codexThreadId; SessionManager.switchProvider is the deliberate way past that refusal (see cross-provider-model-switching)
workflow steps run on Claude models only, refused on both the client pickers and the server validator

Lines' own workflow tools are read-only in a codex session: a codex call reaches the bridge as a plain HTTP request on POST /lines-mcp with no permission card on its path, so that route serves LINES_READ_ONLY_MANIFEST and dispatches with createMcpDispatcher(ctx, undefined, { allowWrites: false }); a Claude session keeps the writes, each behind its card (allowWrites: true)
output_tokens means exactly what the provider called output; reasoning tokens ride beside it and the spend accumulator adds them explicitly

codex reports tokens and never a price; a codex spend row now shows an estimated $ instead, computed from a static price table and always marked with a ~ so it can never look like a provider-reported figure (see usage-and-cost)
a stopped codex turn settles as stopped, never as a failure with a Retry

a session-scoped helper query (autoName, summarizeTurn, consolidateStepOutput) prefers that session's own provider and falls back to the other when the preferred one is absent or answers null; a helper with no session (the MCP judge) stays Claude-first

auto-naming never strands a session on 'New session': a null or thrown helper answer still writes a localSessionName(prompt) fallback title, and the session retries on its next prompt until a real summary lands

every helper query (auto-name, turn summary, step consolidation, provider-switch hand-off) runs in an empty scratch directory (helperCwd()), never the session's own cwd, so a project's auto-memory or AGENTS.md cannot leak into an answer meant to describe one narrow thing
architecturalRules: codex notifications are normalized into Claude SDK message shapes on the bridge, not given a transcript kind of their own — the settle pass and every turn scan are keyed to those shapes
the worker forwards notifications verbatim and interprets nothing, so changing how a codex item renders cannot restart the worker and kill every live turn
streamed deltas must wear the stream_event envelope: isDroppable and the client's supersede rule both key off it
UI gates ask shared/providers.ts about a capability, never about a vendor
engine dispatch is the first thing handleBridgeMessage does, because the Claude control cases would throw a synchronous TypeError on a codex session
protocol types are generated by the installed CLI and never hand-written; codexAppServer.contract.test.ts is the drift canary
nothing in shared/ may import a server dependency — the protocol types are export-type only, so the browser bundle pays nothing
relatedDecisions: Claude's message shape is the internal model deliberately; a neutral event model is deferred until a third provider is real
device code rather than a redirect, because the browser finishing a login is frequently not on the bridge's machine
acceptForSession is never sent to codex — Lines keeps the one allowlist the user can actually see
helper queries stay on codex exec: they are one-shot, so the app-server would mean a long-lived child on the bridge for no gain

provider selection for a helper query is a preference, not a hard route: a session-scoped call passes its own provider, and the other one is still tried when the preferred provider is disconnected or answers null
a manual provider switch is a second, deliberate entry point past setModel's refusal, not a loophole in it (cross-provider-model-switching)

features.name: Model selector
features.purpose: Pick which Claude model a session or workflow step runs with, shown with a one-line description per option.
businessRules: description is optional on ModelOption; missing description renders label-only

a step/session keeps a retired model id in storage (no migration); resolveModelId() substitutes the mapped replacement at query time so it still runs, and a warning badge on the step card flags it for the user to update
an unmapped unknown model id passes through resolveModelId() unchanged rather than being forced to a default

picking the other provider's model on a session that has already run opens a confirm dialog (switchProvider) rather than disabling the option; only providerSwitchBlock's own reasons (a workflow step consolidating, a pending advance, queued messages) and a missing CLI/account still disable it
Overrides never mutate stored steps.
Claude-only overrides: the run modal offers Anthropic models only.
architecturalRules: all model Selects must use modelSelectData()/renderModelOption instead of inlining data mapping
modelSelectData() takes the current stored id as ensureId so a stale/unknown id renders disabled instead of leaving the Select blank
legacy-model resolution is a static explicit map (LEGACY_MODEL_MAP), not a tier-prefix heuristic or live Models-API lookup

modelSelectData()'s unavailable and warn options both disable an option, but only warn marks it warningActionable — describedOptionRenderer overrides Mantine's disabled-option opacity (describedOptionStyles) so a warning icon still stands out on a dimmed row, and only an actionable one is a click-through to Settings -> Updates

features.name: Permissions and plan mode
features.purpose: What decides whether a tool call runs, who decided it, and how plan mode's deliverable is written and reviewed: mode pickers, resolution provenance, the synced auto-mode allowlist (what an entry covers, and the exact entry "Always allow" saves), symlink-aware path checks, files that run code later always asking, plan-file auto-approval, the reopenable plan card, and a typed reply counting as "keep planning".
entryPoints: Selecting text inside the plan card (PlanApproval / CommentablePlan)
businessRules: all five PermissionMode values stay in PERMISSION_MODES and selectable in the workflow step Selects, including acceptEdits, because preset workflows ship steps with permissionMode: 'acceptEdits'; the composer/settings segmented controls only show three (Plan, Assist, Full Auto) and default/acceptEdits have no pill
'default' displays as Manual; the stored value is unchanged (used for the workflow step badge and any session outside the three pill values)

the shipped new-session default is 'auto' (Assist), and a session lands on 'auto' rather than 'default' after a plan is approved on every path that used to reset it, all routed through setPermissionMode so the worker is told rather than only the stored meta changing; where 'auto' would be the target, a session carrying permissionCeiling (it runs someone else's recipe) resumes in 'default' instead
ExitPlanMode and AskUserQuestion always resolve to an explicit 'ask' from the hook, in every permission mode, never a bare continue: true a mode or settings entry could pre-empt
a second answer to an already-resolved permission request is dropped; it never re-emits a resolution event or re-triggers recoverOrphanedPermission's injected prompt

a resend after a bridge restart replays a stored ALWAYS_ASK_TOOLS resolution only when it was produced by a human (resolvedBy is 'user', 'plan-reply', or absent/legacy); any server-synthesized resolution is re-asked instead
a model-initiated EnterPlanMode sets meta.permissionMode = 'plan' immediately, so a subsequent worker/bridge restart resumes still gated
every resolution logs one [permission] line (session, tool, allow/deny, source)
a remote allowlist is never applied automatically; divergence is shown as an explicit added/removed diff the user accepts or rejects
divergence is detected as a set difference between local and remote entries, never by comparing updatedAt
pushing the local list to storage is suppressed while a review is pending
rejecting a review keeps the local list, pushes it back over the remote row, and is remembered by the remote's content so the same proposal is never re-asked
ALWAYS_ASK_TOOLS (AskUserQuestion, ExitPlanMode) can never be allowlisted

a hand-typed Bash prefix is whitespace-collapsed and may not contain &, |, ; or a line break: a line is split on &&, ||, ; and line breaks, and a command still carrying | or & is never covered by an entry, so such a prefix could never match

an entry covers a chained command only when it is a plain simple command: one carrying a pipe, &, a redirect, a backtick, $( or a line break (UNSAFE_SEGMENT) meets every rule whatever its prefix; each command is read through ruleText (${IFS}, escaped spaces, quotes and backslashes) so no spelling slips past a rule written for the plain one

a prefix that is dangerous on its own (one a BASH_RULES rule already matches, a COMMAND_RUNNERS shell/interpreter/launcher or RUNNER_SUBCOMMANDS pair, or only NAME=value assignments) covers only that exact command, never what follows it, whoever saved the entry and whenever

"Always allow" saves exactly the entry the card showed (alwaysAllowEntry, decided when the card was raised) and nothing when it showed none: none for an always-ask tool, a file tool or Monitor, a line writing a persistent file, a flagged command that pipes/redirects/substitutes, flagged commands needing two entries, or a dangerous prefix; for Bash the entry is the first two words (after assignments) of the command a rule flagged, never of the line's first command

a write to a file that runs code later (PERSISTENT_FILES: Claude Code settings/hooks, MCP configs, git hooks/config, shell startup files, ssh) always reaches the user in every permission mode but bypassPermissions, wherever the file is; in auto mode no allowlist entry disarms it, and it covers Bash writes (redirects, tee, cp/mv/ln/install/rsync/scp, dd, sed -i, perl -i, curl -o, wget -O) plus git config writes and program-running one-off git -c/--config-env/GIT_CONFIG_* settings; reading those files is untouched

a file path auto-approves only when it is inside a root both as written and once every symlink is followed; a path that climbs with .. or runs through a link that can't be followed never does, and a blanket file-tool entry does not cover such a write either

an approval never changes the call it approves: resolvePermission ignores the client's updatedInput, except an AskUserQuestion card's answers, rebuilt against the recorded card (its own questions only, strings only, 10,000 characters each) and persisted as rebuilt

a guest's Always allow and Allow as read are dropped server-side (permissionAnswerFor) and never shown (useIsGuestOnSession): both write the host's allowlist, which is the owner's setting; a guest's click is the one-off approval
non-Bash entries never carry a prefix; one given is silently dropped rather than rejected

plan-directory reads and writes (~/.claude/plans/** or <cwd>/.claude/plans/**) auto-approve in every permission mode, judged as written and once symlinks are followed, with neither plans directory allowed to be a link elsewhere, and never for a persistent file inside one
ExitPlanMode and AskUserQuestion always still prompt the user regardless of target path
credential paths (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env) always escalate even if nested under a plans directory, checked on the path as written and on where a link leads
any other out-of-root file access still escalates — out of root as written or once symlinks are followed, so a link inside the project is judged by the file it reaches

/file (and by extension /tree/find) can read any plan directory reachable from isPlanPath, not just the requesting session's own plan file — a deliberate widening of a route previously confined to project/session roots, scoped to plan directories only, and to the owner (a guest's resolve never takes the plans exception)
a resolved plan card renders collapsed by default but is always reopenable via its header
action buttons never render once a request is resolved, in the inline card or the fullscreen modal
fullscreen focus mode opens read-only for a resolved plan
when the harness passes no inline plan argument, the card falls back to the turn's last plan-file write, reconstructing Edit-revised plans from the file snapshot
a plan card is live (chevron + Focus enabled) whenever a plan path is known, even with no resolvable inline/snapshot text
opening a plan card re-reads its plan file from disk, so the card (pending or resolved) always shows the plan's current text, not a frozen snapshot
a resolved card whose live text differs from what was captured shows an 'updated since approval' hint

a typed composer reply while an ExitPlanMode card is pending is treated as "keep planning": it denies that one request with the user's text as the reason, unblocking the query instead of queueing behind a promise nothing can resolve; it only fires for a pending ExitPlanMode, never another tool

no attachments: the deny reason is KEEP_PLANNING_MESSAGE plus the user's raw text and nothing else is queued; with attachments: the reason is a note only and the real text/attachments are queued, but not delivered until the turn genuinely settles (idle/done/error) since a keep-planning deny is a tool_result inside the live turn and never emits an SDK result

Keep planning (button) folds the leading run of queued messages authored by the clicker into the same deny reason via takeQueuedPlanReply, since that deny never settles the turn either and the row would otherwise strand until final approval; a paused queue and a foreign-authored row are never folded; an attachments row keeps its place with its text/mentions/draft cleared
the plan card's badge shows 'kept planning' (not 'denied') for a denied ExitPlanMode request
the card's two actions only relabel and only send planComments when at least one comment is attached; with zero comments the wire message and labels are unchanged
a plan comment is a {quote, note} pair, never a character offset
a workflow-gated plan step folds its comments into the gate's deny message and never interjects
plan comments require the prompt capability in addition to approvePermissions, and are dropped for an actor with promptNeedsApproval
a comment's quote is never editable, only its note
a quote that no longer matches the live plan text silently drops its highlight; the comment itself is unaffected
hovering a comment row or a highlighted passage never scrolls the plan; only clicking a comment row scrolls its passage into view (visible copy only)

plan mode auto-approves read-only Bash, web reads, subagent/skill calls and read-shaped MCP tools (isSafePlanModeRead), fail-closed and skipped for codex sessions; BASH_RULES still wins over the allowlist

plan mode matches BASH_RULES per command and only on commands that aren't reads, so grep pattern text can't trigger a rejection; scratch writes under a temp dir ask instead of being rejected; Monitor commands are classified like Bash

'Allow as read' on a plan-mode card records a Bash prefix with scope 'plan-read' (prefix taken from the bridge's record of the card); plan-read entries only extend the plan-mode classifier, never the auto-mode guard, and BASH_RULES, credential paths and recognised writes still win over them

the 'Auto-reject writes in plan mode' setting (planModeRejectWrites) denies only a plan-mode call planModeVerdict recognises as a write, with the reason in the deny message; an unrecognised call (node -e, a heredoc, an unknown tool) still reaches a card ('ask' from the hook); checked in both handlePreToolUse (so a settings.json permissions.allow can't pre-empt it) and handleCanUseTool (fail-closed backstop); codex sessions reject every non-read call; off by default, never touches ALWAYS_ASK_TOOLS, and rejects Lines MCP writes too; auto-denies are recorded with resolvedBy: 'plan-readonly' and stay visible in the transcript
architecturalRules: single shared PERMISSION_MODES list — no component defines its own label/description array; PERMISSION_MODE_SEGMENTS is a three-item, independently-ordered subset (plan, auto, bypassPermissions) built by mapping over that subset, not by filtering PERMISSION_MODES

SegmentedControl has no per-segment tooltip prop, so per-item tooltips wrap each segment's label in a Tooltip-wrapped full-width span; the composer's control-level Tooltip only renders when the session is disabled (a Codex session), not generically, so it never fights the per-pill tooltips
resolvedBy is optional and every reader treats a missing value as 'user'
findPermissionResolution scans backwards (newest wins), matching the existing convention in exitPlanRequestId
the workflow plan-step gate's recorded resolution: 'allow' was already not a record of the SDK's tool result; resolvedBy: 'workflow-advance' makes that legible rather than changing it
validators live in shared/types.ts so the web client runs the exact same rules as the bridge before sending an entry
allowlist edits are dedicated addGuardAllow/removeGuardAllow/reviewGuardAllowlist intent messages, not folded into the whole-blob UserUiSettings save
the web store never caches the allowlist in localStorage; it is server-authoritative and arrives on every hello
removing an entry has no confirmation modal since it only narrows the guard and fails safe
the review modal is mounted at the app root, not inside Settings, so a divergence reaches the user without requiring a gear click

assessToolCall's self-worker-source check (isSelfWorkerSource) runs before the blanket tool allowlist short-circuit — the first guard verdict an allowlist entry cannot disarm; keep it ordered first in any refactor; the persistent-file check (persistentFileReason) sits right after it on the same side, and the Bash branch runs persistentShellWrite ahead of segmentAllowed, so no entry disarms a write that outlives the turn

isPlanPath anchors containment to real directories via isRealInside (as written and once symlinks are followed, a climbing .. never counting), not a substring match on the plan-dir marker, so neither path traversal nor a link planted in a plans directory passes as a plan path

containment follows symlinks everywhere it gates something, through one implementation: realPathOf/isRealInside, exported from autoGuard.ts so resolveWorkspacePath, the file routes, find-in-files and guestCwdAllowed reuse it; a path whose real location can't be worked out counts as outside

the entry "Always allow" saves is decided by the bridge when the card is raised and recorded on it (alwaysAllowEntry), never re-derived after the click or computed by the client, which only renders it; allowEntryFor is deprecated and uncalled

resolvePermission treats its own record of the card as the source of truth for what was approved (its input, alwaysAllowEntry, planRead.prefix) and the wire only for the decision, plus question answers and plan comments, each narrowed server-side
auto-approved plan writes remain visible as tool_use blocks in the transcript, but the auto-approval permission event is filtered from the UI like other auto-approved calls
PLAN_DIR_MARKER/isPlanFilePath live in shared/types.ts, not autoGuard.ts, so the web client can reuse the same plan-path hint without importing server code

resolveWorkspacePath/workspaceRoots/resolveWorkspaceParam live in server/src/workspacePaths.ts, not server/src/index.ts, so they're importable by their own test — index.ts starts listening as a side effect of being imported

~/.claude/plans is per-OS-user, not per-app-user: under AUTH_ENABLED every signed-in app user on the same machine shares that directory, so this exception can cross app-user boundaries — accepted for now

the plan-file fallback builds data.input.plan/planPath from the transcript alone; the rendered card layers a live filesystem read (useFileContent against /file) on top whenever it's open, falling back to the transcript-only text before that fetch resolves or on failure
the plan-file write is tracked turn-scoped (lastPlanWrite) for text stitching, with a non-reset session-wide fallback (sessionPlanWrite) only consulted when the turn-scoped write is absent
expanded (inline collapse) and focus (fullscreen) are independent state; an effect keyed only on resolution forces both closed once a request resolves
the card's live read means a resolved card can show text the user never approved; the 'updated since approval' hint is the mitigation, not a faithful-approval guarantee

the plan-reply path picks the request id via a single backwards scan (same shape as findPermissionRequest/findPermissionResolution), never a bulk deny-everything-pending pass, so a concurrent unrelated permission card is never touched

the no-attachments plan-reply path never emits a 'user' transcript event or calls prompt() directly — both would open a new turn boundary and corrupt turn-scoped bookkeeping (collectTurns, permissionWaitMs)
the wording of a commented plan decision lives solely in formatPlanComments
on a deny, the server always rebuilds denyMessage from the comments and discards the client's
pushIntoLiveTurn is the pushTurnSafely(..., {intoLiveTurn:true}) call extracted out of interjectQueued so the plan-comments approval path can reuse it

the keep-planning wording has exactly one builder, keepPlanningReason (paired with PLAN_REPLY_MARKER) in shared/types.ts, shared by the build side (server) and the parse side (web's planReplyText) so the two can never drift
plan-comment drafts follow the composer-draft localStorage pattern, keyed by session id and requestId
the highlight paint uses the CSS Custom Highlight API rather than DOM mutation, since the plan markdown re-renders on mount and on every live re-read of the plan file

features.name: Usage and cost
features.purpose: Plan-usage chip, spend split by model, per-session cost/token/duration in the sidebar, and per-step spend in the workflow stepper — all fed by one accumulate-on-result pass.
businessRules: settled cost is always Claude Code's own reported cost (total_cost_usd/modelUsage); a computed figure only stands in mid-turn and for a provider that reports none

total_cost_usd is Claude Code's running total: a result is billed as its reading less the reading it continues from, chosen by the counters alone (CostLineage) — a closed or restarted query usually carries the total on, a new session_id starts from zero however high it climbs, and a resume can continue an older save; nothing about the bridge's view of the process is trusted

historical totals billed by the earlier rules are wrong in both directions and never self-correct; server/scripts/repair-spend.ts is a one-time, per-machine, dry-run-by-default rebuild of totals, costByModel and workflow step costs from transcripts and rewind sidecars

no login, no chip - enforced server-side (poller never fetches, logout nulls snapshot) and client-side (auth.loggedIn gate); logged in with no reading shows an empty chip with an explanation, never hidden
{type: 'usage', usage: null} means auth is gone (logout or revoked/expired OAuth session), nothing else

a stale snapshot survives transient fetch failures; staleness is shown via 'Updated Xm ago', never by hiding the chip; with no snapshot at all (usage null or zero windows while logged in) the client renders an empty chip, wire meaning unchanged
hello may carry usage: null before the poller's first fetch completes (e.g. after a server restart); a logged-in client keeps its previously held snapshot instead of clearing it

rows are keyed by the model that spent the money — resolveModelId of the CLI's canonicalModel or modelUsage key, falling back to meta.model without per-model counters — so subagent and CLI-internal spend sits on its own model's row
helper-query spend (autoName, summarizeTurn, step-output consolidation) is excluded — the table is chat-turn spend only, not full account spend
costByModel is additive; only the repair script rebuilds it
the global rollup is derived client-side from the sessions the store already holds, so deleting a session removes its spend
a result carrying neither cost nor usage opens no row
cost rendered as $X.XX, hidden when totalCostUsd is unset
token icon/tooltip hidden when totalTokens is unset
date rendered en-GB (dd/mm/yyyy) instead of browser-default locale
hovering a badge-state row swaps the status badge for date/cost/tokens meta; row min-height is fixed to prevent layout jump
duration rendered via formatDuration, hidden when totalDurationMs is unset; excludes idle wait between turns and permission-prompt approval wait within a turn
cost rendered as $X.XX next to the step name, hidden when that step's accumulated cost is zero or unset
token icon with a tooltip ('N tokens spent') shown next to the cost label, hidden when that step's accumulated tokens are zero or unset

retries and auto-advance turns on the same step add onto the same array slot rather than overwriting it; a step's cost and tokens include every attempt of a re-driven turn and every result landing while it is parked, and a turn ending with no result charges nothing
duration shown next to the token icon via formatDuration, hidden when that step's accumulated duration is zero or unset; excludes permission-prompt approval wait within the turn
a turn transparently re-driven by turn-recovery (a rejected token, an overloaded API) accumulates spend for every attempt, not just the one that finally settles

usage-history period totals (day/week/month/year) are computed from this bridge's own spend-history.json and are not synced, covering only turns run on this machine; the all-time rollup is derived from synced sessions and spans every machine, so a period figure can read lower than all-time for the same window
All time is the default and first entry in the period picker, since it is the only figure that is not machine-scoped and the number the card already showed before period browsing existed

day keys (YYYY-MM-DD) are stamped in the bridge's local timezone at write time and frozen; the blob's tz field records the zone in effect, and a mismatch against the browser's zone is surfaced as a note rather than corrected
the ledger is additive only; nothing rewrites an existing day row except the one-time backfill script, which replaces the whole file

server/scripts/backfill-spend-history.ts is best-effort: a session whose transcript was deleted contributes nothing and cannot be recovered (a rewind's cut tail survives in its sidecar and is read); both scripts refuse --write while a bridge is up, the desktop app's included (bridge.lock)
the period picker's menu re-anchors on today whenever granularity changes, so switching grains never leaves the user viewing an unrelated period

a turn on a provider whose capability table says cost: false is priced from ModelOption.price via estimateSpendUsd instead of left uncosted; the gate is the provider's capability, not whether a particular result happens to be missing a cost, so a Claude turn with no cost stays uncosted
estimateSpendUsd returns undefined (never 0) for a model with no price entry, since a zero would render as "this turn was free" rather than "we cannot say"

every figure derived from an estimate is marked with a ~ prefix (formatSpendUsd) rather than a dimmed style or a tooltip, decided once per spend surface (section/session/step) rather than per row, since each surface is already narrowed to one provider
every spend readout renders through formatSpendUsd, which always formats to 2 decimals; no call site can pick its own precision

WorkflowState.stepModels[i] records the model id a step's turns actually ran on, because a provider-crossing workflow stays inside one SessionMeta and the session's current model cannot answer for an earlier step; absent on a step run before this field existed, which falls back to the session-level hasEstimatedSpend reading

server/scripts/repair-spend.ts and server/scripts/backfill-spend-history.ts replay spend through spendReplay.ts — the live lineage, attribution, estimator and capability gate — so a rebuilt figure agrees with what a live turn would record

the live in-flight spend estimate is never persisted and never enters totalCostUsd/lastCostUsd/costByModel/the ledger/the cost lineage; it is replaced by Claude Code's reported cost at settle, and anything shown that includes it is ~-marked (an unpriced call shows no live figure, never $0.00)

the live Claude figure is priced per API call at the call's own model with Anthropic's conventions (estimateClaudeCallUsd: uncached input, 1.25x/2x cache writes), with the final output count from message_delta; subagent calls are included and the broadcast is throttled to about 1s per session
a transcript turn card shows that result's own billed cost (CostLineage over every result in seq order, compaction-hidden ones included), never the raw total_cost_usd
a codex turn's usage is the growth of the thread's running total across all its tokenUsage notifications (codexUsageStep), not the last request's usage alone
lastCostUsd/lastTokens are the turn's own: emptied as a turn starts (resetTurnFigures) and added to by every result it settles
architecturalRules: reuses the existing accumulate-on-result pass in server/src/sessions.ts that already owns totalCostUsd/totalTokens, instead of a new tracking mechanism
no new persistence and no new ws message — costByModel travels inside the existing SessionMeta blob
totalTokens and totalDurationMs accumulate on the SDK result message the same way totalCostUsd already does, rather than introducing a separate tracking mechanism
duration is sourced from the SDK result event's duration_ms, not clock math against turnStartedAt, so it excludes idle time by construction

permission-wait time is deducted via LiveState.permissionWaitMs (measured from askPermission call to resolution) rather than switching to the SDK's duration_api_ms, which would also strip genuine tool-execution time
workflow step spend is charged from the session's unreported spend (takeUnreportedSpend) on every settle, not read off lastCostUsd for a workflow turn only
tokens mirror the same pattern via a new SessionMeta.lastTokens field rather than a separate tracking mechanism
permission-wait time is deducted via LiveState.permissionWaitMs rather than the SDK's duration_api_ms, which would also strip genuine tool-execution time

the rule choosing a reading's base lives in shared/resultSpend.ts and reads only the readings themselves, so the live accumulator, the transcript's turn cards and the scripts share it and cannot diverge
repair-spend.ts is a throwaway script, not startup migration code, following the bridge-running guard / dry-run-default / JSON-backup pattern established by server/scripts/migrate-user.ts

the spend-history ledger lives in its own store file (spend-history.json), not on SessionMeta, because that blob is synced last-write-wins under a hard push cap and a day-by-day record is exactly the per-turn data it must stay free of
spend history is deliberately not cloud-synced in v1 (no Prisma migration, no new sync route); a synced ledger table is the stated follow-up
a day's spend rides its own {type: 'spendDay'} message rather than the nullable {type: 'usage'} broadcast, since usage: null has one fixed meaning (auth is gone) unrelated to spend history
the ledger write sits beside each addSpend call for costByModel, with the identical resolved model id, cost and tokens, so the ledger and costByModel can never disagree about what counted
spendDay broadcasts and the hello snapshot carry the whole day row, not a delta, so a dropped message self-heals on the next turn instead of leaving a permanent gap

the web store's hello merge and spendDay handler are both gated on fromPrimary, mirroring updateStatus/bridge/claudeCli, so a second machine's hello cannot overwrite or blend into the primary's ledger
the period picker is plain useState lifted only as far as UsageIndicator, not zustand state, since it is ephemeral view state shared only between the two provider chips
the period-picker menu renders with withinPortal={false} because a portaled dropdown would render outside the HoverCard's DOM subtree and dismiss it on pointer move
estimation is kept out of shared/resultSpend.ts, which subtracts running totals; an estimate is per-turn, so shared/estimateSpend.ts is its own module, called only when the lineage bills nothing

shared/estimateSpend.ts and shared/types.ts form a deliberate import cycle (the estimator reads priceFor/DEFAULT_MODELS; types.ts re-exports the estimator) safe only because the estimator reads those bindings inside function bodies, never at its own top level

the live estimate is an ephemeral session-scoped {type: 'turnSpend'} message rather than an upsert, because upsert bumps the LWW updatedAt, persists sessions.json and broadcasts the whole meta; null means the turn settled and the figure is dropped
the bridge's cost lineage is rebuilt lazily from the transcript, not persisted, and dropped on a rewind truncation — the transcript is the one record server and client both bill from

features.name: Workflow step versioning
features.purpose: Shared diff-popover UI for warning that a pinned step is stale and for browsing, re-pinning, or restoring any past step version, plus the rules deciding which workflow the editor draft reflects.
businessRules: newest-first, gap-tolerant version list

own steps show full history; foreign steps show published versions only, with the exact pinned version unioned in whenever the bridge holds it — for someone else's unpublished version, only a copy cached while it was still visible

POST /steps/resolve answers only the caller's own versions and anyone's published ones; another user's private version comes back exactly as a missing one does — a pin is not a grant, and unpublishing revokes other users' pins, which then park as unresolved
addStepVersions adopts only the requested step's history and resolveSteps only the requested ownerId/stepId/version triples, since a version is filed under the owner it names
pin/restore is disabled for the currently active version; restore is also disabled for a version that needs review, since the restored head is signed by this machine

a held-back workflow or step version is kept and badged but refused by assertRunnable, attach and runStep until reviewed; approving echoes the shown digest (a stale one is refused); edits and copies (Duplicate, Make an editable copy) never clear a mark
the review dialog (UntrustedReviewModal) freezes what it shows when it opens, so content that changes while it is open is refused by the bridge rather than confirmed unseen
workflow re-pin changes only which immutable version a ref points to; step-library restore creates a brand-new head version with old content — history is never rewritten
both popovers fetch history on open, not on mount, and re-fetch on every reopen
diff list scrolls independently (ScrollArea.Autosize, mah 280) once it exceeds popover height, so the Update button stays reachable regardless of diff length
Update all re-pins every outdated ref step directly, skipping the per-field diff review
a workflows/sharedWorkflows length change while the modal is already open with a live draft must not re-trigger the pick-a-workflow fallback
loadFrom selects no step of the loaded workflow (the pane shows the workflow overview); a step opens only via explicit selection, one at a time

own beats shared: an id/step present in both the own and shared maps is owned, editable, and never rendered under "Shared by others"; a StepRef.ownerId drifted from the bridge's own id is healed on re-pin/update and on WorkflowEngine.save(), plus once at boot
every version of one step reports the same createdAt (the lineage's, not the version's); a content change or a publish-toggle-only save both keep it, and it only ever moves earlier, never later

contentOf is the single StepContent field list for loading, saving, publishing and duplicating steps in both the workflow editor and step library, so no field (reasoningEffort, routing) is dropped on any path
architecturalRules: immutable step versions are never deleted or edited, on disk or in storage — only the head list and published flag change
storage enforces the foreign-publish filter server-side on both the version-history route and POST /steps/resolve; client-side version union never bypasses it

the resolve visibility rule lives in storage/src/stepRows.ts so it is testable without a Clerk token; refs are type-checked before the Prisma where (a filter object in place of a string would match every owner) and capped at RESOLVE_MAX_REFS
cross-user step rows are keyed by the row, never the blob: storage sets ownerId (and id on the history route) from the row, and the bridge also drops anything it did not ask for
trust is read off the saved workflow the bridge sent, never the draft; a copied mark rides DraftWorkflow.heldMark, sent once with the next save and then dropped
setSharedSteps keeps the reviewed content of a version its author rewrote in place, and an unverified copy never displaces a trusted version of the same number — the number is what a workflow pins

init effect tracks the open transition via a prevOpened ref and skips its workflows[0] fallback whenever a draft already exists and this isn't the open transition, to avoid racing the id-reconciliation effect after a new-workflow save
new-workflow id reconciliation matches by name plus deep step equality, not step count alone

features.name: Workflow step lifecycle
features.purpose: How a running workflow step's turn settles into advance, park, or stall; the manual escape hatches for a stuck or stalled step; the bounded consolidation of a step's output before it is handed on; and the sidebar checkmark for a fully-finished workflow.
businessRules: plain Stop during a running workflow step always parks it at waiting-approval; it never advances
a user prompt sent after a force-advance but before the interrupted turn settles clears the 'interrupted' flag and its step stamp
step output hand-off after a force-advance goes through the same (now-bounded) consolidation as a normal advance
a step configured with autoAdvance: true still parks after Stop — Stop overrides the step's own configuration
a plan-approval advance already pending when Stop is pressed is discarded, not delayed: both the flag and its step stamp are cleared

a failed turn (is_error result or a crashed query) also never autoAdvances — it parks the step with stepFailure: 'turn' instead, keeping the error status alive for Retry; a turn the user stopped is excluded even though the SDK can report it in the identical is_error shape — that settle reports failed: false and takes the ordinary Stop park, with no stepFailure and no error status

a parked step (waiting-approval, or error for a failed step) can run a manual context compaction without leaving that state; approve/force-advance/retry/prompt are all held for the duration and a typed prompt queues instead of iterating, draining into the same step (never advancing) once the compaction settles — see context-window
the affordance only ever targets the workflow's current step; other steps show no hover state
confirmation copy differs by state: a running step warns its turn is stopped and the last-said text becomes the output; the last step's copy says the workflow finishes
one click on Mark as completed always ends with the workflow on the next step (or done), via a normal settle or the watchdog
each affordance only ever targets the workflow current step, and only while it is genuinely stalled
starting a stalled pending step runs it exactly as a normal advance would — same fresh-start behavior, same hand-off
resuming a stalled done step re-runs its consolidation, so the outputs entry the dead advance never published is filled in first
resuming needs no confirmation dialog — the step is already done, so nothing is being overridden
the last step reading done is a finished workflow, never a stall; it gets no affordance
the Approve button shows a loader and is disabled for the entire consolidation window, not just until the next step's status arrives
the button is also disabled while disconnected, since a dropped WS message would otherwise leave the click looking like it did nothing
the card's copy switches to an in-progress message while advancing
the consolidation window is bounded, so even a hung query or token refresh cannot hold advancing open forever
consolidation only fires when a step ran more than one turn; single-turn steps incur no extra query or latency
on query failure, empty result, or a timeout (consolidateTimeoutMs), falls back to lastAssistantText (per-step-scoped) rather than blocking the workflow
an empty consolidated output is never published, so it cannot overwrite a previously captured value
consolidation is scoped to the stepIndex that just finished, not merely the newest started marker

a step whose template references an {outputs.<name>} that is absent or blank parks at waiting-approval via failTurn (stepFailure: 'pre-run') with a marker naming the missing outputs, instead of running with a silently blank substitution
a step deliverable captured during plan mode comes from the ExitPlanMode plan (inline argument or written plan file), not the turn's trailing chat text
outputs are strictly per-session (WorkflowState.outputs); there is no cross-session write path
prompt tokens are honoured only where the step author wrote them: a token occurring inside substituted content (a step output, the diff, the task text) stays literal instead of being re-expanded
the working-tree diff handed to a fresh-start step is capped with a truncation marker (MAX_DIFF_CHARS) so a large dirty tree degrades the hand-off rather than failing the turn

a plan revised by Edit after the deliverable-producing Write still contributes its current on-disk text to the hand-off, via collectTurns reading the plan file (gated by isPlanPath) instead of the last captured Write content
icon precedence: session.completed -> outline check, status running -> Loader, status.actionable -> pulsing dot, isWorkflowFinished -> filled check, otherwise plain dot
actionable states always win over the finished checkmark so a session needing the user is never masked as done
force-advance (mark last running step completed) also sets the last step done, so a force-finished workflow shows the filled check too

clicking a step in the stepper still jumps the transcript to that step's start marker, but the marker may not be mounted (Transcript.tsx windows a long transcript to its tail): the click asks revealWorkflowStep() to scroll directly if the marker exists, otherwise it fires an event the transcript handles by dropping its window and scrolling once the marker mounts

the parked state is a one-line strip rather than a card, and does not repeat the step's name: it is on screen for as long as a step is parked (most of a workflow's life) and the stepper directly above already shows that name in bold

a hidden step is display:none and never unmounted, because Transcript counts [data-progress-fill] elements in DOM order to learn the step count — dropping or reordering one renumbers the workflow's scroll segments

a desktop shows the whole workflow across the row however many steps it has; a phone shows the current step alone with n/total and a chevron, since one step is all that fits at 390px with its name readable

the chevron opens the other steps as a bottom sheet rather than an in-place expansion — the stepper sits above the transcript, so expanding in place pushes the conversation down every time the user checks where they are

that sheet renders no [data-progress-fill] elements, because Transcript counts them to learn the workflow's length and a second set would double it; per-step progress stays on the row behind the sheet
tapping a step in the sheet reveals it in the transcript and closes the sheet; a pending step has nothing to jump to and is inert

a non-last step's settle (done while its step still reads running) raises no Task complete alert or push — isAlertTransition suppresses it because an advance follows and a park re-alerts as waiting-approval; only the last step's done alerts; see web-push-notifications
Per-run overrides never mutate stored steps; runStep merges WorkflowState.stepOverrides over the step's model and effort.
Only pending steps accept override edits; running and done steps keep what they ran on.
Overrides are Claude-only: a non-Anthropic model or unknown effort is dropped by sanitizeStepOverrides.

a parked step re-opens to running when a main-thread event proves a turn is live on it that the bridge did not start (a background-task notification turn) and parks again on that turn's result; a pre-run failure, an in-flight advance, a Stop in progress and any bridge-started turn never re-open it
a closed query is final: nothing it emits afterwards reaches the session, and a workflow advance holds prompts and queue flushes until it finishes
architecturalRules: interrupt() stays intent-free — no caller may infer "advance" from "stop"
only forceAdvance sets advanceOnComplete (+ advanceOnCompleteStep); a plain Stop leaves it unset and arms no watchdog
whether a settle may consume advanceOnComplete is decided by the advanceOnCompleteStep stamp matching the current step index, not by turnSource
an interrupted settle always parks unless it is also the forced (stamped force-advance) exception, overriding both autoAdvance and a pending plan-approval advance
never advance synchronously under a live turn — flag advanceOnComplete and wait for the turn to settle, with a watchdog as the only fallback
the handleWorkerEnded settle fallback must stay gated on the interrupting set (routine non-error ended events exist)

never call advance() directly on a running step while its turn is active — set advanceOnComplete (+ advanceOnCompleteStep) then call SessionManager.interrupt(); interrupt() no longer implies an advance
the advanceOnCompleteStep stamp, not turnSource, decides whether a settle or the watchdog may consume a pending flag
the watchdog clears turnSource when it fires, so a late arrival from the abandoned turn is ignored by the stamp check
both recoveries are guarded no-ops the user must trigger — the engine never self-heals a stalled step automatically
reuses runStep step-entry behavior (pending) and advance() (done) rather than duplicating hand-off or consolidation logic
a done-at-current-index recovery keys off advancing, never isSessionActive — advance() sets no session status, so the leftover status says nothing about whether an advance is live
advance() must persist the stepIndex bump itself; leaving it to a later broadcast makes the unrecoverable done-at-current-index shape the durable state for the whole consolidation window
the in-flight flag is server-owned broadcast state, never local optimistic UI state
clearing the flag rides the next status broadcast rather than issuing its own — no await may be inserted between the clear and that broadcast
cleared on process restart (constructor load loop) and on hand-off (adoptSynced), never in reconcileWithWorker, which runs far more often and would falsely clear a live advance
runStep's silent early returns now persistMeta before returning, so the cleared flag and bumped stepIndex always reach the client
advance() persists the stepIndex bump immediately rather than letting it ride runStep later broadcast
reuses the transcript-walking pattern from lastAssistantText/summarizeTurn and the one-shot non-agentic query shape from summarizeTurn/autoName
advance() is async; callers fire it with void this.advance(sessionId)
all prompt tokens are filled in one pass over the template (substituteTokens) rather than by chained replaceAll calls; a new token is added to that pass, never appended as another pass
isWorkflowFinished is kept separate from sessionRowMeta's { color, label, actionable } return since projectStatusMeta and alerts.ts consume that shape and workflow-done is not actionable
isWorkflowFinished mirrors workflows.ts advance(): the last step is set done with no further stepIndex bump, so all-done is the only reliable signal

features.name: Turn recovery
features.purpose: Everything that gets a turn back on its feet: detecting and resuming turns that died with the app, a working Retry for every recoverable failure, in-turn recovery from a rejected OAuth token, and the rule that a turn never runs on the unrefreshable ambient ~/.claude login.
businessRules: a turn the user stopped is not classified as a failure: no dropFailedQuery, no red banner, no Retry — the stopped result is recorded verbatim but the turn settles clean
auto-continue only resumes sessions flagged by the reconcile that is running; a stale flag keeps its banner
autoContinueInterrupted is on unless explicitly false; absent (or no settings.json) means enabled
a resume that throws is contained per session: logged, session put back into the flagged state, later sessions still resume
settings pulled from the storage server are merged field-wise so an older client cannot erase a newer setting by omitting it
interruptedAt clears on prompt, result, markTurnLive and archive/complete, but never on ackSession

the blind-clear timer fires only when no worker ever answered and it never saw an incompatible version; a mismatch is instead surfaced immediately via WorkerStatus.mismatch, not by this timer or the lost deadline
the sidebar row shows the same yellow interrupted dot/badge as the banner via sessionRowMeta, reusing the banner's exact guard, and persists through ackSession the same way
the socket may be down for WORKER_LOST_MS (20s) before it's treated as a real outage, well past an ordinary tsx-watch reconnect (~1-2s)
the worker-lost path flags sessions but never auto-continues them, even with autoContinueInterrupted on; the next real hello resumes them

reconcileWithWorker skips a session that has neither live state nor a local on-disk transcript (SessionManager.ranHere) — it only exists here because storage sync (adoptSynced) adopted it from another machine, and demoting/restamping/auto-continuing it would broadcast and cloud-push a turn this machine never ran; a session with an actual worker report for this pass is still fully reconciled even with no local transcript, since a live report is itself evidence

a session demoted by reconcileWithWorker whose current workflow step already reads waiting-approval re-parks at waiting-approval instead of idle (the only turn that runs on an already-parked step is a manual compaction) — no interruptedAt is stamped and it is not added to flagged, so auto-continue's nudge cannot read as an approval nobody gave; see workflow-step-lifecycle
a cold-start protocol mismatch never sets everConnected, so the outage clock never starts; it's surfaced by WorkerStatus.mismatch instead

exactly one of ConnectionBanner/SkewBanner/WorkerBanner/StorageBanner/UpdateBanner renders at a time; bridge-down outranks contract skew outranks worker-down outranks storage-down outranks update-available; scoped to the primary machine only (see multi-machine-client)
every recoverable failure ends on a failure row with a working Retry, in a plain session and inside a running workflow alike
a failed turn never autoAdvances; it parks the step as failed instead, unless an explicit stamped force-advance is already pending
Retry re-runs the right thing: a step that never got a prompt is re-rendered from WorkflowState ('pre-run'); a step whose turn failed is re-sent as a follow-up on the same conversation ('turn')
no auto-retry or backoff — a transient failure (e.g. a 529) is an ordinary failed turn with a manual button
stepFailure is persisted, so a reload while parked in the failed state still shows Retry

an auth-classified turn failure attempts exactly one token refresh, then always rewrites the banner to name the next action (Retry, Sign in, or check your connection) instead of leaving raw CLI text with only Retry
errorKind: 'auth' is set only for the signed-out outcome; refreshed/refresh-failed clear it
the login modal opens off the existing authStatus broadcast, not a new message type, and unlike the hello auto-open it is not deduped

no bulk resume on a login event: a sign-in completing later, or from another device, must never fire N queued turns across sessions; a transparent recovery is anchored to one in-flight turn's own result, never to an authStatus broadcast, so this still holds even though a rejected-token turn is now silently re-driven within its own attempt budget
errorKind is never set when no AuthManager is wired (ambient-token mode)
every query crash (auth-related or not) still writes a synthetic result event with the raw CLI text preserved verbatim, even after the banner is revised
a clean ended (no error) writes no synthetic result
a signed-in user's turn never runs on ambient ~/.claude credentials; with no app token the turn is refused, since a visible failure with Retry beats a silent 401 loop
a refusal caused by being logged out re-broadcasts the logged-out authStatus so a dismissed login modal reopens; a refusal from a transient refresh failure does not
the bridge-side helper queries (autoName, summarizeTurn, consolidateStepOutput) are best-effort: no token means skip the query, never fall back and never fail the surrounding turn
compactContext still returns a synchronous { ok: true }; an auth refusal after that point surfaces through failTurn, not the { ok: false, code, reason } union
a transiently failed proactive refresh retries on a 60s-doubling ladder capped at 15 minutes; a dead refresh token logs out instead, stopping the chain
accessToken: null in buildQueryOptions is reachable only when no AuthManager is wired at all (tests / embedding), never for a real signed-in user

UserUiSettings.compressResponses gates COMPRESS_RESPONSES_PROMPT directly in buildQueryOptions — on means the ruleset is in systemPrompt.append, off means neither it nor a plugins key is present; one user-level setting rather than a per-session one, read from the store on every push so a Settings flip lands on each session's next query with nothing cached on the meta; on unless explicitly false

logins are tracked per OAuth state, so two started at once each keep their own PKCE verifier; completing one clears the rest, unfinished ones expire after 30 minutes, and a paste with no #state falls back to the newest

a content-filter, context-overflow or invalid-request failure never implies an automatic retry, backoff, or step advance; an overloaded/rate-limited failure is the one exception, transparently re-driven up to its attempt budget before it ever reaches this class of banner (see architecturalRules)
auth wins outright when a failure text matches both an auth pattern and a turnFailureKind pattern
the retry hint rides only the re-sent prompt text, never the stored transcript event for the original failed turn
Skip step and the stepper's Approve button send the identical workflowApprove message under the identical gate
a query the bridge cannot vouch for (e.g. no queryTokens entry after a bridge restart) is recycled, not reused
any failed turn drops that session's query, recognised or not, so a single Retry cannot reuse the child that just failed
a failed attempt inside a transparent recovery still bills its spend (totalCostUsd/totalTokens/costByModel), and never appends a second 'user' transcript event
a transparent recovery holds no query for the length of its backoff/refresh; reconcileWithWorker must not read that absence as a dead turn

a closed query never reaches the session again: its events, ended and pending RPC results are dropped, close kills the CLI child, and a Stop settling under it is settled by the bridge (skipped while the session is already in a newer turn, and for a deleted session)
warmQuery and recycleIdleQueries never close a query that is mid-turn, owns a background task or is held for auth (queryInUse)
architecturalRules: SessionManager.interrupting is the only authoritative Stop signal; the SDK's terminal_reason is unpublished and never consulted
adding a field to LiveSessionInfo is not a protocol bump; busy is optional so an old worker stays demote-only instead of losing its socket mid-turn
reconcileWithWorker is the only place that stamps interruptedAt
a result for a flagged session means the flag was wrong (buffered result lands after reconcile) — clear it there rather than adding handshake ordering
onStatusChange (UI health) is kept separate from onWorkerLost (session reconcile) rather than merged
isSelfWorkerSource's check runs before the guard's blanket tool allowlist short-circuit, not after
isSelfWorkerSource is self-locating (import.meta.dirname) rather than threading session/bridge identity into assessToolCall
failTurn is the single funnel for every failure the SDK never reports as a result; public so WorkflowEngine can call it for pre-run failures
the retry router idiom mirrors case 'prompt': WorkflowEngine.retryIfFailed gets first refusal, only false falls through to SessionManager.retryTurn; no new ClientMessage type
lastPromptForRetry is the single source both retryTurn and retryIfFailed read from
the failed park skips setStatus (which clears errorMessage on every transition) and calls persistMeta instead, so the error banner and Retry stay live while the step shows waiting-approval
the client's backward scan for retryKey may only skip 'workflow' and 'context-compact' items; every other kind ends the scan
classification happens at exactly two points: failTurn (covers every funnel caller) and the result branch of handleWorkerEvent, which bypasses failTurn by design
the revision guard (status === 'error' && errorMessage === error) is the entire don't-clobber mechanism, relying on the workflow failed-park path using persistMeta not setStatus
authRecoveryMessage's strings avoid every word AUTH_FAILURE_PATTERNS matches, so a re-failure cannot re-classify itself into a loop
a successful refresh() still does not call emitChange(); the revised banner is the visible signal, not an auth-status broadcast
handleTokenRejected goes through the single-flight refresh() rather than logout() directly, so N simultaneous failures cause one token request and concurrent callers all resolve 'refreshed'
the synthetic result is emitted via emitEvent directly, never routed through handleWorkerEvent, so it cannot re-run turn-settle bookkeeping
SDK/CLI error wording is not a published contract; isAuthFailureMessage can silently stop matching after an upstream change
known limitation: in Compact view the failed row sits inside a collapsed AgentTurn, so SessionView's alert is the always-visible affordance (pre-existing, out of scope)

the never-fall-back guarantee lives in pushTurn, which refuses before reaching buildQueryOptions; there is deliberately no second options builder, which would duplicate the whole option set for one differing key
both turn-start call sites go through pushTurnSafely rather than void this.pushTurn(...), so one place guarantees no unhandled rejection
ownerToken() awaits ensureFreshToken() rather than reading getAccessTokenSync(), so helper queries get the same refresh-on-margin treatment as a real turn
the no-AuthManager branch of pushTurn returns before the first await, keeping that path synchronous for tests that assert an immediate push
the proactive backoff computes its first rung explicitly (null ? RETRY : min(x*2, CAP)) rather than doubling a default, which would skip the 60s rung
getAccessTokenSync() remains on AuthManager but has no production caller; it is kept for the sync-status shape tests rely on

the no-local-history skip is narrow and scoped to reconcileWithWorker only — it does not change adoptSynced or what counts as this instance owning a session; it exists because a flapping worker or duplicate bridge (see hosted-machine-access) turned every reconcile pass into a broadcast/cloud-push storm across sessions this machine never actually ran, feeding the very kind of loop this feature exists to break rather than amplify

queryTokens is bridge-memory only and never persisted, while the worker's live queries outlive a bridge restart — the same asymmetry already documented for interrupted-turn recovery, and why the recycle guard must fail closed on an unknown entry

ensureFreshToken joins an in-flight recovery refresh (refreshInFlight) rather than only checking expiresAt, since expiresAt alone cannot distinguish a merely-unexpired token from one just revoked server-side

the transparent-recovery verdict (recoveryKindFor) is decided and stamped (recovering: true) at the same point and for the same reason as the stopped stamp: the transcript store only appends, so a verdict decided after emitEvent persists the result could never reach the durable record

LiveState.recovery is live-only, like compactResume and turnBaselines — a bridge restart mid-recovery falls through to the ordinary interrupted-turn path rather than growing its own crash-recovery mechanism

settleTurnFailed mirrors handleWorkerEnded's error branch, not failTurn — failTurn re-enters classifyFailure/recoverAuthFailure, which would attempt a redundant refresh and could overwrite an already-decided errorKind: 'auth'

cancelRecovery is called from every path that can take a turn away from a recovery in flight (interrupt, prompt, rewindSession, archive/delete, failTurn) rather than relying solely on the epoch/turnStartedAt ownership check, which is the backstop for work already awaited

promptContent is extracted side-effect-free (no stageAttachments, no events) so a silent re-push can build the same content the original 'user' event already staged, without re-staging and duplicating attachment files on disk
accumulateResultSpend is extracted so the deferred-settle and real-settle paths share the identical cost/token/costByModel accumulation

AuthManager.lastRefreshAt is a plain timestamp memo (not a promise cache) so a second concurrent handleTokenRejected() within RECENT_REFRESH_MS skips a redundant refresh-token rotation instead of joining refreshInFlight, which is already resolved by then

features.name: Session and project UI
features.purpose: The shell around a session: persisted unsent drafts, focus on a new session, which session a project switch opens (preferring the project's remembered last-selected session before falling back to latest-created), the project tab's actionable-status dot, and the tool-aware waiting-permission badge.
businessRules: persisted text draft is the full MentionValue (text + ranges), not plain text, so restored pills/expansions stay intact
staged attachments persist too, in IndexedDB rather than localStorage (base64 file data can run tens of MB)
an empty text draft or attachment list is deleted from storage rather than stored empty

Composer's focus effect is keyed on focusComposerFor === session.id rather than session.createdAt age; focusComposerFor is set by the sessionUpsert reducer in the same claim branch that grants pendingCreate the selection (see session-create-auto-select below), so focus and selection now share one create-intent signal instead of independently comparing clocks
switching to an older existing session does not steal focus
auto-selection always excludes archived sessions; completed needs no separate check since the server always archives alongside it
a project whose sessions are all archived auto-selects nothing (empty state) rather than opening an archived one
an explicit selection already in the target project, including an archived session, is never overridden by a tab switch

a project switch prefers the project's remembered last-selected session (lines.lastSessionByProject) over latestSessionIn; latestSessionIn (top non-archived session under the user's sidebar sort) remains the fallback when nothing is remembered or the remembered session is gone/archived; the same pick also runs after the primary machine's hello when a cold launch left nothing selected and no create is pending

the three sidebar groups (Sessions, Shared-with-me, Archived) and the project tab dot describe one machine's sessions only (sessionsOnMachine, see multi-machine-client) — the store still holds every linked machine's sessions, but the list is a display scope switched by the header's MachineSwitcher, not a merge

Shared-with-me holds a session only when no project tab covers it — sessionsInProject checked against every tab, not just the active one — so a session belonging to another open tab never appears here just because a different tab is active

the sidebar session list order is user-selectable via lines.sessionSort (persisted localStorage), applied to all three groups (Sessions, Shared-with-me, Archived): Status (default) ranks running first, then the tab-dot urgency order (plan ready > needs answer > needs approval > needs permission > interrupted > error), then background work, then done, then idle, tie-broken by lastActivityAt descending; Last active sorts by lastActivityAt descending; Created sorts by createdAt descending (the sidebar's pre-existing behavior)
a session status label missing from SESSION_SORT_RANK sorts last rather than being guessed at, same rule projectStatusMeta applies by skipping

the archived group's sort key changed from archivedAt ?? createdAt to the same compareSessions comparator the other two groups use: Status/Last-active mode still puts the most-recently-archived session first since archiving is an upsert that bumps updatedAt, but Created mode now means creation order, not archive order
priority highest first: plan ready (violet) > needs answer (teal) > needs approval (cyan) > needs permission (yellow) > interrupted (yellow) > error (red)
running/done/idle sessions never show a dot
archived sessions are excluded; completed sessions are always archived too, so no separate guard is needed
the active project's tab always shows the plain folder icon, suppressed at render time
opening a project marks its actionable sessions seen; a tab stays quiet until a session reaches a status not yet seen, and a resolved-then-relapsed session counts as new again
seenSessionStatus is in-memory only, so already-seen dots can reappear once after a page reload
ExitPlanMode -> label 'plan ready', violet badge
AskUserQuestion -> label 'needs answer', teal badge
any other tool -> label 'needs permission', yellow badge (unchanged default)
notification body mirrors the sidebar label (capitalized) for waiting-permission sessions

a sessionUpsert only takes the selection when pendingCreate is true AND the session id is not already in seenSessionIds — replaces a comparison of session.createdAt (stamped on the bridge machine) against Date.now() (the browser's clock): hosted, those are different machines, and even a slightly-ahead bridge clock made every upsert look 'just created' forever, so any session re-entering the map stole the selection

pendingCreate is set by markSessionCreatePending() (called by every createSession sender: the sidebar's New session button/menu, and the recipe-run path already selects explicitly via its own sessionId and does not need it) and expires on its own after 15s if no matching upsert ever arrives

seenSessionIds is maintained by both the hello reducer and sessionUpsert, so a session that leaves and re-enters the map — deleted then resurrected, or replayed by a duplicate hello — is never treated as new again

a repeated hello (same session/project signature as the last one applied) is inert: sessions, transcriptLoaded and contextBreakdowns are left untouched, while every other field (usage, worker/storage health, auth) still applies as normal — an older relay replayed open (and its full hello) for every live channel on any bridge attach or takeover, and wholesale-replacing state on each one is what turned two alternating bridge snapshots into a self-sustaining flicker loop across sessions and transcript reloads

send() (ws.ts) returns false when the socket is not open and the message is not a prompt (prompts alone queue for replay); the caller sets actionError so a dropped control message — e.g. a delete sent while disconnected — is visible instead of a console.warn nobody saw; automatic traffic callers resend on their own (BACKGROUND_TYPES: presence, loadTranscript, mcpServerStatus, contextBreakdown, stepVersions, recipeVersions) drops silently with a console.warn only and never sets actionError — a reconnect must not raise a banner nobody triggered

deleting a session shows a loading state on its own row and leaves the row in place until the sessionDeleted echo removes it — no optimistic removal, so a delete that silently failed to send is never mistaken for one that worked

archived sessions in the sidebar render 20 at a time behind a 'Show N more' button instead of the full archived list, since lines.showArchived defaults to on and a long-lived project can accumulate hundreds of them
architecturalRules: text drafts use a single lines.drafts JSON map keyed by session id, following the existing store.ts convention (e.g. lines.openFiles) rather than one key per session
attachment drafts use IndexedDB (db lines-drafts, store attachments, keyed by session id) instead of localStorage, since size is the reason attachments are staged as raw base64 in the first place
focus reuses the same sessionUpsert claim branch that decides selection (focusComposerFor set alongside selectedSessionId) instead of a second, independent is-new flag
membership check reuses sessionsInProject rather than an inline cwd comparison, so it stays key-aware like every other project-scoped scan
format.ts never imports store.ts; projectStatusMeta takes plain SessionMeta[] plus a seen map to keep that dependency edge one-way
the priority table is built from the same waitingPermissionMeta/STATUS_META entries sessionRowMeta uses, so a tab dot can never drift from the sidebar dot it points at
seenSessionStatus is maintained in a single store subscription rather than at each mutation site that could change what counts as seen
pendingPermissionTool rides the existing sessionUpsert broadcast, no new message type
cleared centrally in setStatus for any non-waiting-permission status, plus the worker-reconcile and sync-adopt paths that can force waiting-permission back to idle out from under a live turn
concurrent permission asks on the same session: last askPermission call wins the label/color, consistent with pre-existing status-overwrite behavior

sessionRowMeta is the single row-presentation entry point: archived sessions first (non-actionable green completed, stored status untouched so unarchive restores it), then waitingPermissionMeta, then the interrupted-turn-recovery yellow state, then the plain per-status table (moved into format.ts from Sidebar.tsx)

helloSignature is a cheap string (each session's id:updatedAt joined, plus project paths) rather than a hash of the whole hello payload, precisely so volatile fields (usage, worker/storage health) stay outside it and keep applying on every hello regardless of the short-circuit

store changes here (the hello short-circuit, pendingCreate/seenSessionIds) are pure reducer logic with no web test harness backing them (web/ has no test runner) — the highest-risk, least-covered part of this feature; verified manually

SessionRow is memoized — selecting a different session or any sessions-map update (e.g. a live turn ticking status) otherwise re-rendered every row in the list regardless of the size of the session being switched to; the memo relies on `session` keeping its object identity when unchanged, which sessionUpsert already guarantees by only replacing the entry that changed

compareSessions follows the same format.ts-never-imports-store.ts rule as projectStatusMeta: it takes plain SessionMeta and returns a comparator, so Sidebar.tsx and the store's latestSessionIn (via a validated readSessionSort of the shared SESSION_SORT_KEY) are the only places it is applied

SESSION_SORT_ORDER is built from STATUS_META.running, PROJECT_STATUS_ORDER, BACKGROUND_WORK_META, STATUS_META.done, ARCHIVED_META, STATUS_META.idle rather than a second hand-written urgency table, so the sidebar list order can never drift from the tab dot it points at

lines.lastSessionByProject follows the same single-JSON-map-under-one-key convention as lines.drafts/lines.openFiles, keyed by project path; written by one store subscription keyed on selectedSessionId rather than at each selection call site

features.name: Transcript rendering
features.purpose: How the transcript is drawn: one shared markdown renderer with a bubble only for user prompts (whose images render as never-loaded placeholders), structured per-tool field lists instead of raw JSON, subagent runs nested under their spawning card, a backgrounded call's state living on its own launching card instead of a duplicate row, and an EPHEMERAL_SYSTEM_SUBTYPES filter that keeps roughly half of every transcript file's lines off disk.
businessRules: user and agent text render markdown instead of plain preformatted text; single newlines collapse and raw HTML tags are dropped

a markdown image is never fetched, not on render and not on click: it renders as a placeholder showing its alt text and where it points (a URL's host, a file's path); clicking opens an http(s) URL in a new tab (noopener noreferrer) or a file path in the file preview; no source is exempt, this app's own origin included
an image inside a link is that link's label: the link stays the one action and the image is an inert chip inside it, never a second nested anchor
code blocks wrap long lines (white-space: pre-wrap, overflow-wrap: anywhere) instead of scrolling horizontally
only the user prompt renders as a bubble (right-aligned, capped at 80% column width); agent output is unwrapped and flush-left with nesting shown by order/expand affordance, not indentation
every tool's expanded body shows a structured field list, never raw JSON by default; raw JSON is one toggle away for every tool with no exceptions

a tool call already fully explained elsewhere in the row loses its expand affordance instead of showing an empty/redundant body: a successful edit (diff button covers it) loses only the chevron; a settled (answered, non-error) AskUserQuestion loses the row too and renders as just the always-open review

every AskUserQuestion call is isolated into its own single-tool group and treated as a foldAgentTurns boundary (like a pending ExitPlanMode), so it always renders as its own top-level transcript item regardless of tool-grouping level or Compact folding
an AskUserQuestion call's answer is read from its tool result's prose, not its input — the input only ever contains the questions asked

a subagent's assistant text and tool calls are never counted as main-agent output: workflow step output, the turn summary, and the live context-usage reading are all derived from main-agent messages only
a subagent's tool calls and text nest under its spawning card, never inline in the main transcript or folded into the main agent's tool group
a subagent cannot itself spawn another subagent (harness restriction), so nesting is one level deep in practice, though the data model is recursive
a message whose parent_tool_use_id names a spawn block not present in the transcript falls back to the main sink instead of being dropped
a spawn card leads with description, not the tool name; an unmapped or plugin-scoped subagent_type degrades to a generic agent badge (never hidden, never a crash)
the main agent and a subagent share the same badge icon but never the same color, so who is running reads from color alone before any label
in the interactive OptionCard, the checkbox/radio is a non-interactive indicator; the wrapping button is the sole click target, so onChange must not be added back to the control itself

code-block syntax highlighting (rehype-highlight) is deferred: first paint renders without it, then an idle callback (2s timeout fallback) upgrades the document in place — the highlighter only adds classes inside an already-laid-out <pre>, so it cannot reflow the transcript; a document with no code block skips the deferral and renders with the full plugin set immediately

a backgrounded call's transcript state lives on its own launching tool card (ToolBlock.background), never as a second row, whenever task_started names that card by tool_use_id; only a genuine orphan still renders the standalone dimmed row, capped to one line since task_notification.summary can be an entire shell script
a background subagent's stream_event deltas never drive the shared ActivityRow state — only a foreground agent's do

a system event whose subtype nothing renders or derives state from is still broadcast live but no longer written to the transcript file, except a status event carrying a compact_result, which is the authoritative compaction verdict
a pending QuestionPrompt card claims keyboard focus once per request (its first option) unless focus is already in a text-entry element elsewhere on the page, which outranks it
within a question, arrows move a roving-tabindex cursor across option cards; single-select clamps both ends, multiSelect clamps at top but ArrowDown off the last option advances to the next question

Enter on an unselected single-select option selects it, Enter again advances; Enter on a multiSelect option always toggles and never advances, since advancing would end the question after only one of several intended picks
a mouse click mirrors this: single-select click selects and advances, multiSelect click only toggles; nothing but an explicit Enter or the Send button can submit — a click can never submit by itself

re-picking an already-answered question does not move the view if the next question is also already answered (nothing to advance to); it still advances when the revised question's successor is unanswered

advancing to a new question smooth-scrolls that question's header to the top of the transcript (prefers-reduced-motion respected) rather than only revealing the newly focused option; moving within one question stays an instant nearest-scroll

the focused option card draws a visible outline from tracked focus state, not the browser's default :focus-visible ring, since a mouse click can also move focus (advancing) and that move must be visible
"Other…" never advances on selection (its text input autofocuses instead); a bare Enter inside that input advances once non-empty, and arrow keys keep native caret behaviour there

a system/init row only renders when the model actually differs from the previous init the transcript saw, not once per turn (the CLI process restarts every turn); the first init in a transcript always renders ("session started · model"), a later one only on a genuine model change and reads "model set to model" instead — a cross-provider switch is a separate ProviderSwitchItem marker and is unaffected
