a successful turn's cost and duration render as chips on the turn's header (Compact level) rather than their own centered row; a turn with no header card (text-only, or Full/Grouped level) shows them as a small right-aligned dimmed meta line instead — a failed, stopped, or recovering turn keeps its centered row, error text, and Retry affordance unchanged

only three workflow-marker events render in the transcript: started, a failure park (waiting-approval with failed or missingOutputs), and workflow-done; a clean park, an approve, a retry, and an interrupt leave no transcript trace since the stepper and the approve card already show that state live, and the emitted/stored event set is unchanged

buildTranscript may see a suffix-only event list until paged backfill completes; cross-turn derivations (CostLineage, sessionPlanWrite fallback, lastInitModel de-duplication, background tasks opened in older history) are transient until then
architecturalRules: user and agent transcript text share one markdown renderer instead of separate text-rendering paths; ColorizedText.tsx deleted as dead code
user bubble Paper needs minWidth: 0 alongside maxWidth: '80%' so wide content (e.g. a code block or one long unbroken token) can't win over max-width via min-content sizing
compact markdown rhythm overrides Mantine spacing variables scoped to .md-body rather than CSS selectors, because Typography's list rule outranks a .md-body ul selector override on specificity
collapsible transcript rows (agent turns, tool groups, tool calls) share one borderless .tx-row convention: no Paper/border, CSS-only hover, and no accumulating indentation

a collapsed row's body unmounts instead of only being CSS-hidden, so per-row state that must survive collapse/expand lives in a module-scope sticky map, not component state; sub-toggles inside an already-expanded body (a spawn card's prompt disclosure, every tool card's raw-input toggle) are deliberately plain useState, not sticky, since resetting on close is expected there.

react-window (or similar list virtualization) is still rejected — it would break updateProgress's workflow-step-marker scan, the scrollHeight-based auto-pin/ResizeObserver, and find-in-page; a simple tail window (last ~40 top-level items, growing on idle backfill or scroll-to-top) supersedes lazy-mounted bodies alone once a real session's markdown mount cost dominates — see transcript-performance.md

toolFields degrades instead of failing: an unclassifiable value becomes a capped json field rather than throwing or being skipped, since tool input shapes (especially MCP tools) are not controlled by this code
OptionCard gained a readOnly prop instead of being duplicated into a second component, so a settled answer looks exactly like the choice that produced it
the raw-input toggle shows even for an empty ({}) input, unlike PermissionPrompt's equivalent guard — consistency across every tool card was chosen over hiding a no-op toggle
existing transcripts already carry parent_tool_use_id on disk (persisted verbatim by the worker), so this feature is a pure read-side reinterpretation with no new capture and no migration
no agents option was added to buildQueryOptions; subagent definitions are inherited via settingSources, the same mechanism that already inherits the rest of the preset

the spawn tool's name is not a stable literal: the harness emits 'Agent', the SDK's own AgentInput type and docs call it 'Task', and both appear in persisted transcripts, so every consumer matches via isAgentTool() rather than one string
agentMeta/MAIN_AGENT_META is the single source of truth for agent icon/color, read by both the settled card and the live ActivityRow so they cannot drift apart

parseTaskInput never throws and never assumes a field is present, since AgentInput gains fields the map won't know about (effort is the live example) — this is why the raw-input toggle stays reachable behind every spawn card
nested rendering is threaded down as a renderNested callback rather than a new shared module, since ToolCallCard cannot import Transcript.tsx's Item without an import cycle

reconcileItems (transcript.ts) hands a rebuilt item back its previous object identity when every field buildTranscript can later mutate in place is unchanged (ToolBlock.result/isError/snapshot/children, permission .resolution/.data, ResultItem.summary, streaming/assistant text) — this is what lets memo on Item/AgentTurn/ToolGroup/ToolCallCard skip work and what lets the toolDiffCache WeakMap survive a rebuild instead of recomputing every whole-file diff per event; missing a mutated field here means a changed row silently keeps rendering its old content

the renderNested callback threaded from Transcript into ToolGroup/ToolCallCard must stay referentially stable across renders (a useCallback keyed on sessionId, reached through a ref so it can call itself for a nested subagent transcript) — a fresh closure every render defeats those components' memo silently, with nothing erroring

the workflow progress bar (updateProgress) reads which steps have started from the item list itself (a 'workflow' item with event 'started'), not from rendered [data-workflow-step] DOM marker positions, since the tail window can clip an early marker out of the DOM entirely; a clipped-but-started step's segment reports as fully filled rather than 0% filled; clicking a stepper step whose marker isn't mounted goes through revealWorkflowStep()/REVEAL_STEP_EVENT (web/src/lib/workflowReveal.ts) instead of a direct querySelector

QuestionPrompt's keyboard cursor (activeIdx) trails real DOM focus via onFocus rather than driving it through an effect — an effect keyed on the cursor that called .focus() would re-assert focus on every unrelated transcript re-render

Enter's handler calls preventDefault() unconditionally before branching, since UnstyledButton is a real <button> and Enter's default action already fires a click; Space is left un-intercepted on purpose so it inherits native click semantics instead of Enter's

the set of requests that already auto-focused is a module-scope Set keyed by requestId, not a useRef, because Transcript windows/backfills its item list and this component can genuinely remount for a still-pending request
the mouse and keyboard paths both fold through one advance() function; the click path passes canSubmit: false so clicking the last unanswered option can move focus but never itself fires the WS send

markdown images are placeholders because an image fetches on render with nobody clicking, so a prompt-injected agent could exfiltrate data just by writing an image URL; links wait for a click and are left alone; the deployed CSP is now enforcing and its img-src admits no arbitrary host, the same channel closed one layer down (see production-deployment)
markdownImageTarget is pure (web/src/lib, no React) so the server's test runner covers it; a protocol-relative //host URL is classed as remote via isExternalHref, never as a local path

features.name: Agent memory sync
features.purpose: Sync ~/.claude agent memory (user CLAUDE.md and per-project auto-memory) across a user's machines via the storage server, keeping disk as the SDK-facing cache and Postgres as the cross-machine source of truth.
businessRules: only ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/** are synced; cwd-local CLAUDE.md/.claude, settings.json, and credentials are never touched
per-file entry cap 256 KB; full-snapshot push additionally caps total payload at ~1.5 MB, dropping largest files first
server prunes tombstones older than ~30 days
conflict resolution is per-file last-write-wins by file mtime; the losing side's edit is silently dropped
architecturalRules: reuses the existing StorageSyncClient debounce-and-push pattern and syncNow pull-then-push cycle instead of a new sync mechanism
push is triggered from the SessionManager result-sniffing callback in userContext.ts, not sessions.ts or worker.ts, keeping the worker thin
project-scoped files are keyed by the machine-independent ProjectKeyRegistry key, falling back to a raw slug key when unresolved
the ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/ layout and path-to-slug derivation are Claude CLI/SDK-internal, not a published contract

features.name: Cloud sync: session push budgeting and delete tombstones
features.purpose: Push a user's SessionMeta list to the storage server without re-sending rows it already has and without exceeding the storage server's request body limit, and make a session delete stick across every machine syncing that account rather than being silently re-pushed by whichever one hasn't heard about it yet.
businessRules: a bulk push filters out sessions whose updatedAt/createdAt is not newer than the last accepted push, since storage rows are LWW upserts and re-sending unchanged rows is pure waste
a meta with neither updatedAt nor createdAt is always pushed
a single session whose own JSON exceeds the push budget is dropped from the cloud push (with a one-time warning), never blocking its siblings; its local copy is untouched
a rejected chunk's sessions are retried on the next flush, not dropped
a storage 413 (entity.too.large) answers JSON {error: 'payload too large'} instead of a generic 500 HTML page

a session delete is a soft delete (Session.deletedAt) in storage, never a hard delete — a hard delete leaves peers nothing to adopt, so whichever machine still holds the row pushes it right back on its next sync

DELETE is idempotent: a repeat keeps the original deletedAt stamp rather than advancing it, since the bridge retries a delete until storage confirms it and moving the tombstone forward each retry would re-notify every peer
GET /sessions serves tombstoned rows inside the ordinary delta window (carrying deletedAt in ms) — that is the only way a peer learns about a delete at all
PUT (bulk or single) refuses to resurrect a row whose deletedAt is at or after the pushed updatedAt; a write genuinely newer than the delete does bring the row back and clears the tombstone
the bridge keeps its own tombstone map (id -> deletedAt ms), persisted alongside sessions.json and pruned past ~30 days on load

adoptSynced returns early when a pulled session's stamp does not beat an existing local tombstone — the branch the ordinary LWW check never reached before, since that check only ran when a local copy of the session already existed
applyRemoteDelete records a tombstone even for a session this machine never held, so a slower third machine's later push can't resurrect it here either
a delete issued while pulled state is being applied, or before there is a token to send it with, is queued (pendingDeletes) rather than dropped, and rides the next flush/sync instead of being lost
a bulk push (reconnect) filters out any session whose delete is still unconfirmed, so the whole-list push can't undo a delete that raced it

a synced session is a display artifact plus resumable history, not a work order: adoptSynced never takes queued from a row and never lets one raise permissionMode (bypassPermissions is clamped to default for a session first seen here)

permissionCeiling is never synced: sessionForSync strips it from the copy a push sends (the live meta keeps it) and adoptSynced ignores it on pull, so a row can neither lift a foreign recipe run's ceiling nor bring one

an embedded workflow (workflow.def) from storage is display-only unless its runnableDigest matches the def this machine already holds for that session; otherwise it is marked unsigned and runStep refuses every step of it, strict sync or not; for a run this machine holds (same workflowId), its own task/outputs/lastStepOutput stand over the row's
architecturalRules: SESSIONS_PUSH_MAX_BYTES (1.5MB) mirrors the same headroom-under-2mb constant style as TOTAL_MAX_BYTES in server/src/memory.ts
chunk sends are sequential inside the debounce timer callback, not parallel, so one failure doesn't strand the rest silently
pushSessions owns the dedup filter; userContext.ts's syncNow still hands it the full session list — sync.ts keeps sole ownership of what actually goes on the wire
the real growth driver (WorkflowState.outputs/lastStepOutput, uncapped in server/src/workflows.ts) is not capped by this change — deferred as a follow-up

the row-level rules (LWW upsert, soft delete, resurrect guard, wire shape) live in storage/src/sessionRows.ts rather than inline in the /sessions routes, so they're unit-testable without a Clerk token — /sessions itself stays Clerk-gated and just calls through
flushSessions re-checks pendingDeletes per chunk, after the batch was drained but before each chunk's own await, so a delete issued while an earlier chunk is in flight is not undone by a later one
SessionManager's sessions map and tombstone map are always written together (a single writeState), so they can never desync on disk
deleteSession and applyRemoteDelete share a private forget() that only tears down live state that actually exists, so a remote tombstone for a session this machine never ran costs nothing

session rows carry no signature, so every field that would become an instruction here (queued, permissionMode, permissionCeiling, workflow.def, task/outputs/lastStepOutput) is held at this machine's own value or marked on adopt; a marked snapshot is refused at runStep, the gate every way into a step passes, and does not seed the session's model or permission mode

features.name: Storage availability banner
features.purpose: Classify why the bridge's storage-server link is down, wait out a routine expired-token 401 instead of raising the "cloud sync unavailable" banner, actively re-probe once down so recovery is noticed within seconds, and persist a bounded failure log a user can read and copy from Settings without a bridge console.
businessRules: a single auth (401/403) failure does not raise the banner; only AUTH_GRACE_MS (90s) of continuous auth failures does, and any 2xx/304 resets that clock
while down, a GET /settings probe fires every PROBE_INTERVAL_MS (15s) so recovery is reflected within seconds instead of waiting for the next incidental pull/push
the probe targets /settings, not /health, since /health sits above storage's Clerk gate and would falsely clear an auth-caused outage
sync-log.jsonl only grows on a failed request or an availability transition, capped at ~256 KB and trimmed to its newer half on overflow
a soft-error request still marks the link available and never touches the auth-grace clock, since a soft 401 is not evidence the token is good

a relayed token while down triggers an immediate probe (owner only), from either source: the in-channel auth handler calls ctx.sync.retryNow() after setting ctx.clerkToken, and the relay's onToken does the same
the banner's Dismiss is per-tab, keyed by the outage's status.since; a new outage shows again
only a refused signature verdict appends a fail row and warns; an accepted unsigned blob (mixed-fleet rollout) applies silently, no log row
desktop's main window runs with backgroundThrottling: false so the 50s token-relay timer isn't throttled while hidden
architecturalRules: classifyStatus/classifyError are pure exported functions, unit-testable without constructing a client
appendLog is injected with the same shape and default (() => {}) as the existing persistMarks parameter, so sync.ts still imports no fs
the probe timer is unref()'d like every other StorageSyncClient timer, started only on the down transition and stopped only on the up transition
no storage-server change: no Prisma migration, no storage/ deploy coupling

features.name: App data root
features.purpose: Machine-global directory (~/.lines-app) holding all server-side app state.
businessRules: app data root is ~/.lines-app
'local' user uses the flat root; real user ids live under ~/.lines-app/users/{id}

no machine-wide asset lives under the root any more; ~/.lines-app/plugins/ is a legacy directory an older build git-cloned into, left in place on upgrade rather than deleted, and nothing reads or writes it
architecturalRules: all persistent paths derive from APP_ROOT / userStoreRoot; never hardcode the home-directory path elsewhere

createStore keeps an in-memory, per-user transcript cache (raw lines + lazily-parsed events) revalidated by statSync mtime/size and bounded by count and byte size; it assumes this process is the sole writer of transcripts/*.jsonl
sessions.json writes are compact (not pretty-printed) and debounced via SessionManager.persist/flushPersist, coalescing a burst of status transitions into one write without delaying the broadcast

the sole-writer assumption is enforced, not just assumed: ~/.lines-app/bridge.lock is claimed by every bridge unconditionally (relaying or not), so a second bridge process refuses to start rather than becoming that second writer — see hosted-machine-access.md

features.name: @mention support in prompts
features.purpose: Reference a documented feature or project file inline in the composer prompt via @mention, expanded to context text at send time.
businessRules: mentions are expanded into plain prompt text client-side before send; server and worker never resolve mentions[], only the sidecar for display
a stale feature/file reference degrades to a harmless stale text block rather than blocking send

the find project file search excludes gitignored files by default (includeIgnored opts back in, see file-quick-open); dotfiles and dot-directories are always candidates; falls back to a bounded walk outside a repo, capped at 20000 files
a queued prompt's draft (pre-expansion MentionValue) is stored only when it has mentions; QueuedMessages.tsx re-edits it via a second MentionInput mount

file-match ranking is tiered (basename-prefix, basename-substring, path-substring, basename-subsequence, path-subsequence); a query's whitespace is stripped and a backslash is read as a path separator before matching
architecturalRules: new mention kinds are added as one more MentionProvider entry, no switch-over-kind elsewhere
pill ranges are a derived view synced to the authoritative plain-text string by prefix/suffix diffing, not a second source of truth
no contenteditable/rich-text dependency; pills are a cosmetic mirror-div overlay behind a plain textarea

/find, /file, /tree share one corsFor() helper and one resolveWorkspacePath() root restriction (now in server/src/workspacePaths.ts), which also allows a plan-directory path outside every root (isPlanPath)

features.name: Workflow task attachments
features.purpose: Carry image attachments sent with a workflow's task description into step 0's prompt instead of silently dropping them.
businessRules: attachments ride the entry step (step 0) only; later steps do not re-carry the original file
a non-fresh later step inherits the image for free via the live conversation; a freshStart step gets only the compact previous/diff hand-off, never the original attachment
mentions[] stay out of scope: display-only and already expanded into prompt text client-side
a step 0 that parks (waiting-approval) drops the attachment with no transcript trace; the user must re-attach
architecturalRules: attachment handling stays entirely in SessionManager.prompt; worker.ts does no attachment handling

features.name: Local dev orchestration (Tilt)
features.purpose: Run local development with independently owned worker and bridge runners, coordinated idle-boundary reload, startup rollback, and bounded process-tree shutdown.
businessRules: tilt up gates only storage on .env completeness (DATABASE_URL/DIRECT_URL/CLERK_SECRET_KEY); bridge/worker/web stay reachable even when storage config is missing
web is excluded from the freeze options since Vite HMR never restarts the dev server
a pull that changes only package-lock.json triggers nothing; run tilt trigger install by hand

pair-device (npm run pair -w server) is always declared but never auto_init - triggered by hand when a code expires or a machine is revoked, not part of bringing the stack up; idempotent, prints 'already paired' and exits 0 on a claimed device
desktop-package (npm run package -w desktop) is the same shape as pair-device - manual, never part of tilt up - and exists so the DMG build is discoverable from Tilt at all

RELAY_URL set without STORAGE_URL warns rather than failing preflight - the bridge would dial a hosted relay while syncing to the local storage default, splitting one machine's data across two databases

when RELAY_URL in .env points at a non-loopback host and ~/.lines-app/bridge.lock names a live process, preflight warns (naming the tray app if instance:'desktop', or naming any other holder as one that will refuse with exit 78) rather than failing; a stale/absent/unparseable lock is silent

LINES_INSTANCE is not set anywhere in this Tiltfile despite older comments claiming Tilt sets it to 'dev' — web/vite.config.ts resolves /__bridge from the same variable, so pinning it for the bridge alone would break dev-server discovery
source changes build an immutable local code generation; both backend processes reload only after confirmed idle
Freeze and Resume change supervisor policy without restarting a process
failed candidate startup restores the last healthy generation
explicit shutdown ends active work and reaps only the resource-owned process tree

restart-backend (a manual Tilt resource plus a button on worker/bridge) rebuilds and cycles the pair without waiting for idle, for the case the automatic path can be blocked on indefinitely (a workflow step parked at waiting-approval anywhere on the machine); the control route answers with a 'restarted: true' handshake so a supervisor predating the route cannot report false success on its plain 200

enable-all (tilt enable --all, plus a button living on preflight specifically because that resource is never disabled) is the way back from a disabled Tilt resource, whose own buttons disappear along with it
a forced restart pauses the supervisor's crash recovery and retries a previously rejected build; a restart that rolls back fails with the rejection reason instead of reporting success

the bridge binds 127.0.0.1 under Tilt as everywhere, so its readiness probe and status link name 127.0.0.1 rather than localhost (which may resolve to ::1 first), and web/src/ws.ts dials 127.0.0.1 from a page served on loopback

Vite listens on every interface (host: true), but a phone on the LAN gets the page and no machine: the bridge admits only this machine's own page origins; LAN testing is opt-in via LINES_BRIDGE_HOST=0.0.0.0 plus the page's LAN origin in LINES_BRIDGE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, after which anyone on that network who can load the origin can drive the bridge

both runners set LINES_DEV_SUPERVISED=1 on their children, which is also the one switch that lets the bridge's single-tenant 'local' context accept a storage token — the dev relay with auth off (--with-relay without --relay-auth) binds every browser to 'local' and forwards its token; a desktop install never sets it
architecturalRules: PORT is injected per resource via serve_env, never a shared env block
preflight reads .env key names only, never values, into any Tilt spec/log/UI button
no resource watches a file its own cmd writes — install's deps list the five workspace manifests but omit package-lock.json, which npm install itself rewrites and would retrigger the resource forever
resource_deps gates only the first build after tilt up; a later re-run of install does not cascade to prisma-generate or the four service resources

whether the bridge talks to a hosted install is not a Tilt flag - it follows RELAY_URL in .env, read by the bridge's own dotenv; STORAGE_URL is injected into serve_env only as a default, so an explicit .env value is never overridden
the worker runner coordinates source watching and IPC admission; Tilt independently owns the worker and bridge runners
external installed dependencies are shared and are not covered by source rollback

features.name: Context window
features.purpose: Live context-window occupancy in the composer with a per-category breakdown, plus manual compaction, a near-limit warning, and readable transcript events for both manual and CLI auto-compaction.
businessRules: occupancy is sourced from the SDK's /context control request (getContextUsage()) when a live query exists, never from result.usage, which is cumulative across every API call in the turn rather than a point-in-time reading
the ContextUsage fallback (derived from the last assistant message's usage) is used only when no live query is available
no reading yet means no chip, in both fallback and SDK modes
unknown model context window shows raw token counts with no ring rather than guessing a denominator
category/component rows must sum to the shown total; any SDK-reported vs component-sum mismatch is surfaced as an explicit residual row instead of hidden
deferred categories are excluded from the total and from free space, and shown with no percentage share, to avoid double-counting
the persisted SessionMeta.contextSummary is capped and holds no per-item detail since it is synced and written to disk; per-item detail is fetched on demand and never persisted
a hover-triggered summary refresh only broadcasts/syncs when the summary actually changed
resetting a session's Claude conversation (workflow fresh-start step) stamps contextResetAt; readings older than that render as stale until the next turn reports

Lines does not set autoCompactEnabled and has no control over the CLI's own background auto-compaction; the hover card's auto-compact row is a straight passthrough of the CLI's own settingSources-resolved setting, shown even when off

Lines never fires compaction itself — only a manual button and a passive warning badge, since it is irreversible, lossy, and billable; this is distinct from the CLI's own background auto-compaction, which Lines does not control

the manual button's disabled state always carries a specific reason (turn running, a workflow step's approved output is being consolidated, no session yet, no reading yet, or the SDK explicitly reported the compaction failed) via one shared contextCompactBlock predicate
the unsupported latch requires an explicit SDK compact_result:'failed' — a turn settling with neither a boundary nor a status verdict is inconclusive and leaves the button enabled

the unsupported latch is scoped to the CLI conversation that produced it: cleared on resetClaudeSession, on bridge restart, and when adopting a synced session, so it never survives past the process/conversation that saw the failure

a workflow step parked waiting-approval does not block the manual button — every step hand-off reads the on-disk transcript (withoutCompactSpans), never the CLI's live context; only a live advance (WorkflowState.advancing) blocks, since it is about to prompt the next step

a compaction over a parked or failed step runs as an ordinary 'running' turn, so its status is snapshotted (LiveState.compactResume) and restored on every path that ends the turn — the result settle branch, abandonCompaction (stop, dead query), and reconcileWithWorker re-deriving the park from stepStatuses after a bridge restart — so the session never strands on 'done' or loses a failed step's banner

while a parked step compacts, WorkflowEngine holds approve/force-advance/retry and queues a typed prompt instead of pushing a second turn under the in-flight /compact; a queued prompt drains into the same step (never advances) once the compaction settles
a compaction is invisible to every workflow turn scan (consolidateStepOutput, lastAssistantText, summarizeTurn, retryTurn) via withoutCompactSpans, but never stripped from permission bookkeeping
architecturalRules: the bridge-worker protocol gained a generic ask/askResult request-response method rather than a one-off message type, so future control requests do not require another PROTOCOL_VERSION bump (which restarts the worker and drops in-flight turns)
the worker returns raw SDK JSON from ask; all normalization lives in server/src/contextBreakdown.ts as pure, defensively-coerced functions, keeping the worker's import graph unchanged
the existing cumulative fields (lastTokens, totalTokens) are untouched; this feature adds a parallel occupancy reading rather than altering the billing one
compactContext is a dedicated SessionManager method, not a call to prompt() — a compaction carries no 'user' transcript event and must not auto-name the session or touch the queue
one shared predicate (contextCompactBlock) backs the server-side guard, the button's disabled state, and its tooltip

naming: transcript event kind 'context-compact', payload ContextCompactData, SessionMeta.contextCompact — all contextCompact-prefixed, distinct from the unrelated compactionLevel (transcript display density)

the browser's buildTranscript mirrors withoutCompactSpans: events inside an open compact span are dropped from the rendered transcript, not just hidden by the marker pair — except a failed result, which closes the span like a 'user' event does

LiveState.compactResume (the status a compaction covered) is deliberately not a SessionMeta field — per-process scratch, never synced or persisted, so a bridge restart loses it cleanly and reconcileWithWorker re-derives the park from WorkflowState.stepStatuses instead of trusting a resurrected copy

features.name: Conversational workflow/step editing (in-process MCP tools)
features.purpose: Expose workflow/step list/read/create/update/delete as in-process MCP tools (mcp__lines__*) so a session can discuss and edit its own workflows in conversation instead of only via the WorkflowEditor modal; writes are permission-gated, reads are not, and the codex door (/lines-mcp), which has no approval card, serves the reads only.
businessRules: mutations address a workflow by id, or by a name unique among owned workflows; a name match against another user's published workflow is refused as read-only, never silently forked
create_workflow/update_workflow/save_step are rejected before WorkflowEngine.save() on a shared workflowValidation.ts failure, with one actionable error string
update_workflow's steps argument replaces the whole list, no patch-by-index

resolveWorkflowRef should still run before saveWorkflow for the better, candidate-naming error message; WorkflowEngine.save() itself throws ForeignWorkflowError for an id it classifies as foreign, as the guard of last resort
list/read tools cap results at 100 rows (default 50)
a bridge gone mid-call answers after MCP_TOOL_FALLBACK_MS (30s) with an error result rather than parking the turn indefinitely

"foreign" is own-beats-shared: an id present in both the own and shared maps (a stale shared snapshot of the user's own row, or the same id republished under a second identity) is writable, not foreign

every workflow/step read tool reports createdAt/updatedAt as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM local-time strings, not raw ms epochs; stepVersionsView stays numeric because the browser's version popover needs ms for relTime
a workflow's createdAt is stamped once on first save and never restamped; a fresh (empty) id always mints a new one, so duplicate()/create_workflow can never inherit the source's birthday
a step's createdAt is the lineage's creation, not the mint time of the version being read; every version of one step reports the same createdAt, and that version's own mint time is its updatedAt

creation time only ever moves earlier, never later, everywhere it merges (earliest/LEAST) — idempotent and order-independent across peers, so a client or blob that omits createdAt can never erase a known one

a write runs only where an approval card gated it: the codex door (POST /lines-mcp) has no card on its path, so it serves LINES_READ_ONLY_MANIFEST and dispatches with allowWrites: false, while the Claude door keeps every write behind its card (allowWrites: true)
architecturalRules: tool names/descriptions/schemas live entirely on the bridge (mcpWorkflowTools.ts) and are hot-reloadable; only the workflow-agnostic conversion (workerMcp.ts) and protocol shape (workerProtocol.ts) sit in the worker's minimal import graph
PROTOCOL_VERSION bumped 2->3 for the optional push.tools field, so a bridge/worker skew is a loud mismatch instead of silently tool-less sessions
RPC_FALLBACK table excludes canUseTool on purpose - the SDK parks it with no deadline since a permission request must wait for a human
workflowCommands.ts imports UserContext type-only to avoid a runtime cycle with userContext.ts

shared/workflowValidation.ts is re-exported from shared/types.ts as that file's last statement, an intentional import cycle safe only while workflowValidation.ts never reads types.ts bindings at its own top level
the web WorkflowEditor draft (useWorkflowDraft.ts) was not migrated onto shared/workflowValidation.ts in this change; the two validators can drift

createMcpDispatcher's allowWrites has no default — every caller states it, so a caller that forgot to think about it gets no writes — and a write is refused in the dispatcher as well as left out of the read-only manifest, since a client can call a tool it was never listed; LINES_READ_ONLY_MANIFEST is built from the same READ_TOOLS specs as LINES_TOOL_MANIFEST

features.name: Brand logo assets
features.purpose: Renders the Lines brand mark across the tab-bar header, browser tab favicon, desktop notification icon, and the animated boot splash; there is no wordmark anywhere, baked or DOM.
businessRules: the header, favicon, and notification icon all use the same mark art now - no separate lockup - logo-mark.png for the header, logo-mark-solid.png/favicon.png for the other two
favicon.png and logo-mark-solid.png are the same art at two paths because index.html needs a /public URL while alerts.ts wants a Vite asset import
the header is height-driven (height 24, width auto) inside a plate with padding 4 and borderRadius 6
alt="Lines" on the header is the only accessible name for the brand

the boot splash is static HTML in index.html outside #root, one persistent element that React never renders or remounts, so its loop does not restart between boot steps or machine switches; lib/splash.ts only changes the caption and its state (shown, finishing, finished, leaving, hidden)

the splash is skipped before first paint (web/public/splash-guard.js, loaded synchronously from index.html — a file, not an inline script, because the CSP allows no inline script) when Clerk is configured and the route is /welcome or /join/:code or there is no signed-in Clerk cookie; splashSkippedAtBoot exposes this; a wrong guess for a signed-in user is corrected when the app's first claim shows the splash again; builds without Clerk always keep it
the splash layer scrolls only while shown (connecting help panel); in finishing, finished and leaving it clips, so the hand-over scale and the app mounting beneath cannot produce scrollbars

each boot step holds the splash with its own caption (Starting Lines, Signing you in, Finding your machines, Connecting to <machine>, Loading your sessions and projects, Opening your session); the splash has no header

the app is not rendered until the mark has finished drawing onto the static logo; it then mounts hidden under the splash, the splash fades out, and the app fades in the moment the splash is gone, with a 4s fallback if an expected app never mounts
when the app opens on a session with no transcript loaded, the splash waits for it (capped at 6s) once per page load; a machine switch remounts the app and replays the sequence

the What's new card can hold the hand-over: holdApp keeps the splash at the finished mark and suspends the 4s fallback while the card shows in the splash slot, the mark and card are centred as one group and glide when the card changes size, and the release runs the usual fade (see whats-new)
architecturalRules: the white plate in ProjectTabs is load-bearing: logo-mark.png is transparent with no background of its own, so without the plate the art would sit directly on the dark header; the plate also supplies the header's corner rounding since that asset carries no baked mask

logo-mark-solid.png/favicon.png bake their own rounded-rect corner mask (RGBA), unlike the header asset, because nothing downstream - the favicon <link>, the Notification icon - can round them at render time
link.type must track the real bytes: index.html declares image/png and restorePlain resets to image/png after render installs a data URL
committed PNGs are cropped derivatives of a single 1254x1254 RGB-on-white source that is not in the repo; a future re-crop or re-tone must start from that source, not from the committed derivatives
the splash mark is a hand-built SVG in index.html, separate from the PNG assets, so changing the mark means changing that markup too

features.name: Multi-root projects
features.purpose: Let one project tab span more than one folder, so every session created in it can read and write in all of them with the same auto-approve behavior as the primary, and the file tree, @mention, and /find see every root.
businessRules: the primary path is the project's sole identity; extra roots widen what its sessions may read/write, but every session's cwd stays the primary
writes in an extra root auto-approve in auto mode exactly like the primary; the sensitive-path override (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env) still wins regardless of which root a path resolves under
one root belongs to exactly one project; roots may not nest within a project
an empty roots list escalates every file tool - the guard fails toward prompting, never toward silently trusting nothing
@mention's feature provider stays primary-root-only; only the file provider is multi-root
removing a root only narrows what the project's sessions may reach; nothing on disk is touched, and the learned project key for that path is kept
architecturalRules: roots are resolved at use time from the project record (rootsForCwd), never snapshotted onto SessionMeta, which is synced and must keep its existing shape
additionalDirectories is omitted (not []) for a single-root project, so a single-root session's serialized query options stay byte-identical to before this feature
the guard's three exported functions take roots: string[], not an optional 5th parameter after cwd
projects.json stays local-only (never synced); only the resolved project-key map is synced
deliberately does not reuse resolveProjectKey for root membership - that key's --show-prefix keeps monorepo siblings apart, the opposite of what one workspace tab needs

features.name: Multi-repo commits
features.purpose: Group a multi-root session's folders into git commit units by work tree (not by project), give a workflow step's {diff} a per-repo section, and add a {roots} token so a step can scope every git command with -C <repo root>, since additionalDirectories never moves the Bash shell out of the session's primary cwd.
businessRules: commit units come from git rev-parse --show-toplevel, never from resolveProjectKey, whose --show-prefix component deliberately keeps monorepo siblings apart
two roots that resolve to the same work tree are one commit unit; two separate work trees are two
a root that isn't inside any git work tree is never a commit unit
{roots} is not a hand-off token: a template using only {roots} with freshStart on still gets the normal {previous}/{diff} auto-prepend
a single repo produces no '# repo:' header in {diff} - existing single-root workflows see byte-identical prompts
the MAX_DIFF_CHARS budget for {diff} is shared across every commit unit, not multiplied by the repo count, with unused share redistributed to repos that overflowed theirs
architecturalRules: repo-grouping/diff logic (git.ts) stays pure git, with no prompt formatting; {roots}'s rendering lives in workflows.ts
the shared git() helper now has a timeout, since this feature multiplies git calls on the step-entry path the user waits through at every approval gap
diffBaselines is additive alongside the deprecated diffBaseline inside the synced WorkflowState; writers only ever set diffBaselines, the legacy field is read-only
MAX_UNTRACKED (new-file cap per diff) is per repo, not per workflow

features.name: Git worktrees
features.purpose: Run a session in its own linked git worktree instead of sharing one checkout with every other session in the project; attribution to the parent tab without widening what the session's roots may reach. A per-session worktree starts detached and gets a lines/<title> branch once the session's auto-title resolves, so nothing is ever renamed.
businessRules: attribution, not capability: a worktree session's project tab widens, its roots never do — projectRoots must never return a worktree path
one path, one owner, and no nesting, extending the same rule multi-root-projects applies to roots
a per-session worktree starts detached; its branch is cut once the session's auto-title resolves and is never renamed after; a worktree the user named explicitly gets its branch immediately
every branch Lines mints on its own initiative is namespaced lines/… (LINES_BRANCH_PREFIX); a branch the user typed into the create form is untouched
removal is always explicit; git branch -d only when asked and only for a branch createdByLines; never -D
removal is refused while any non-archived session's cwd is inside the worktree, unless force
deleting or archiving a session never touches its worktree — the record renders 'orphaned', one click from Remove
git is the source of truth; Project.worktrees is a cache reconciled on openProject; a worktree adopted from outside Lines never gets createdByLines
explicit create fails on a taken path/branch; the per-session auto path uniquifies (-2, -3…) instead
a managed worktree (under WORKTREE_ROOT) is never added to the recent-directories list, since opening it as its own project tab would double-count every session in it
architecturalRules: runGit (throws, stderr in the message) is for mutating git only; the existing git() (swallows every failure to '') stays read-only
Lines' own worktree operations go through worktreeCommands, never Bash, so assessToolCall never sees them; the two new BASH_RULES entries govern only an agent running git itself
WorktreeDeps (run, repoRoot, ensureParent) is the one seam every command function takes, mirroring GitRun in worktrees.ts
defaultWorktreePath groups by repo basename under WORKTREE_ROOT, not full repo path, so a name collision is resolved by the existing uniquifier
SessionManager.onAutoNamed is a callback wired in userContext.ts, not a direct call from sessions.ts into worktreeCommands.ts, since that layer needs a whole UserContext

features.name: Documentation reader
features.purpose: In-app reader for a project's docs/** markdown corpus: a doc tree, an index.json-driven feature-card home, full-text search, and cross-links that navigate inside the reader instead of opening the source-file preview.
businessRules: an index entry whose doc is missing from the bundle still renders as a card with a 'no doc' badge; a bundle doc no entry claims lists under 'Other documents'; a missing/unparseable index degrades to a plain document list
a markdown link target always resolves to kind: 'doc' and opens inside the reader even when the target isn't in this corpus, surfacing a 'not in this corpus' panel instead of a source-preview 404
a link that escapes the docs root, or isn't markdown, opens the existing file-preview modal instead
no project open, or no docs/ folder in the active project, shows an empty state instead of an error boundary
the reader's Open source button opens the file preview with raw: true, so it shows the markdown source rather than the rendered preview
architecturalRules: one bundle request (GET /docs?path=) powers the tree, cards, search and cross-links; no per-file fan-out and no separate search route
/docs sits inside the same corsFor() + resolveWorkspacePath gate as /file, /tree and /find
collectDocs never follows symlinked files or directories, closing an exfiltration path a prefix-based containment check would otherwise miss
pure doc logic (link resolution, title/summary extraction, search ranking) lives in shared/types.ts so node:test can cover it
Markdown gained one optional onLinkClick prop instead of being forked; absent, every transcript call site keeps the existing openFilePreview behavior
the three global modals (MonacoPreviewModal, LoginModal, GuardAllowlistReviewModal) are mounted at the App root instead of inside Shell, so they still work on /docs

features.name: Hosted machine access
features.purpose: The whole path from a browser anywhere to the agent on the user's own machine: ephemeral local ports, the browser-bridge contract, the outbound relay, device pairing, and the UI gate that picks which machine you are talking to.
businessRules: fromAgent only accepts a frame from the socket the hub currently calls its agent; a superseded (or half-dead) bridge that keeps writing cannot inject state into a live browser channel or close a channel now owned by the bridge that replaced it
attachAgent terminates (not just closes) the predecessor it supersedes, so a takeover cannot leave the loser's socket lingering OPEN on the relay

the per-agent re-verify tick and health/ping interval both bail out the instant their own socket is no longer the hub's agent, so a superseded socket's still-running timer can never drop the hub — or evict the browser channels — out from under the bridge that replaced it
a duplicate agent attach for a device (attachAgent superseding a live one) logs distinctly from a first attach, naming the running attach count

the relay's public health endpoint (GET /) keeps its exact unauthenticated shape; presenting the correct x-relay-secret (constant-time compared) additionally returns hubs, a per-device summary (deviceId, online, channel count, agentAttaches, lastAttachAt) for triage — agentAttaches climbing on an otherwise-idle paired device is the tell for two bridges fighting over one identity

the bridge rejects a duplicate open for a channel id it already serves (logging a warning) rather than building a second RelayChannel — a relay that replays open on attach re-delivers ids already held, and building a second link means a second full hello down a socket that never reconnected; the current relay closes channels on attach instead, so this is a guard
RelayClient.connect() closes any pre-existing socket (and drops its channels) before dialling a new one, so one RelayClient instance can never hold two live sockets for the same device

every bridge takes this machine's single-instance lock (~/.lines-app/bridge.lock, pid+startedAt+instance+deviceId) unconditionally, relaying or not, claimed atomically ('wx'); on collision a live instance:'desktop' holder is preempted (SIGTERM, cross-checked against its own published runtime file first) since the tray is the only supervisor that can stand down and re-arm, any other live holder gets a bounded ~2s retry window (for a tsx watch successor meeting a still-exiting predecessor) before the new process exits EXIT_BRIDGE_LOCK_HELD (78) naming the holder

LINES_ALLOW_MULTIPLE_BRIDGES=1 is the deliberate escape hatch that skips the single-instance lock entirely (no read, no write), for tests and any intentionally-run second bridge; it must never be set in a real deployment

RelayClient no longer resets its reconnect backoff on 'open' — only a socket that survives RELAY_STABLE_MS does, on close, since a supersede close always follows a successful open and the old reset let two bridges fight at the retry floor forever; SUPERSEDE_LIMIT consecutive supersedes with no stable socket escalates the re-dial cap to SUPERSEDE_CAP_MS, resetting the moment a dial lands a stable link
register is unauthenticated - the machine has no user yet and a code is worthless until claimed; re-registering an already-claimed AND UNREVOKED device is refused (409) rather than silently re-bound
re-registering a REVOKED device clears its stale userId/revokedAt and issues a fresh code - otherwise a revoked machine could never be claimed again, since claim and verify both refuse a revoked row
claim/verify answer the same 'unknown or expired code' for absent, expired, and revoked, so a distinct 'expired' reply can't confirm a guessed code had once been real

revoking a device tombstones it (revokedAt) rather than deleting the row, so it stays an audit trail; it stops the device reconnecting AND ends a live connection within RELAY_REVERIFY_MS, since the relay re-checks each attached device's claim on a timer rather than only on attach

the re-verify tick is asymmetric with attach on purpose: attach fails closed on a refusal OR an outage, but a live device is dropped only on an explicit 403 - treating a storage blip as a refusal would kick every user off their own machine
the relay pings its attached agent and terminate()s one silent for ~2 missed pings; without it a half-open socket leaves the device looking online forever and the browser spinning with no hello
the bridge terminates its own relay socket after LINES_RELAY_IDLE_MS of silence and re-dials - also the macOS-sleep fix, since the wall-clock tick fires late on wake

POST /v1/devices/unpair is authenticated by the device secret (the machine holds no user token) and must stay internet-reachable, unlike verify; every failure answers the same opaque 403 and it returns no pairing code, leaving register as the one code-issuing path
GET /v1/devices never returns secretHash
if storage is unreachable the relay refuses the device rather than admitting it
the desktop shell re-registers an unclaimed device on a timer and on demand to keep a valid code on screen with no app restart, relying on register's re-issue (not 409) behavior for an unclaimed row

the desktop shell also re-registers on an unexpected 1008 (debounced 30s, guarded on having no code) so a machine revoked from the browser shows a fresh pairing code unprompted, and offers 'Unpair this machine...' while paired as the escape hatch that needs no browser
pairing a new machine only becomes the active one automatically if none was active before - silently moving a working session to a different computer would be worse than an extra click
revoking is described in the UI as what it does: stops a machine reconnecting, does not sever a connection already open

a guest row in DevicesSection shows Leave (red, IconLogout) instead of Revoke, since a grantee cannot revoke an owner's grant; Leave calls leaveShare then disconnectMachine (the link is held open in the background and would otherwise keep retrying a grant that no longer exists), clears the remembered device id if it was the active machine, and reloads the list - see session-collaboration for the route

the header's MachineSwitcher (multi-machine-client) is a second machine-switch surface beside Settings → Machines, reusing the same rememberDeviceId+switchDevice pair DevicesSection's switchToDevice uses, so the two can never pick a machine differently
the Machines settings section does not render in a local build - a one-row list of the machine you're already on is noise

the stuck-connecting screen offers a way out after 6s - switch to any other paired machine (overriding chooseDevice's remembered/most-recent pick, which is what chose the unreachable one) or pair a new one; unpair sits last, behind the collapsed Details toggle and an inline confirm; waiting alone never resolves it, since the socket reaches the relay fine and simply finds no agent attached
DownloadDesktopApp renders nothing when no build has been published, since a button pointing at nothing is worse than none
stream deltas are the only droppable traffic: never persisted, and the browser refetches the transcript on reconnect, so losing one costs a partially-typed token rather than state
above the high-water mark a link sheds stream deltas but still receives every critical message
above the hard limit the link is closed outright, which is safe because hello is a complete state snapshot and a reconnect resyncs whatever was missed
thresholds (4MB/32MB) sit far above any loopback burst, so local dev never reaches them
an absent hello.bridge means a bridge older than the field, which counts as skew

hello also carries an optional worker: WorkerStatus, and workerStatus broadcasts later transitions; neither bumped APP_PROTOCOL_VERSION since both are additive and an older client tolerates their absence
ephemeral by default; LINES_WORKER_PORT/LINES_BRIDGE_PORT pin a port only when explicitly set, which Tilt does so its readiness probes have fixed targets

LINES_INSTANCE separates concurrent installs — the desktop shell sets 'desktop', a dev checkout (Tilt included) leaves it unset ('default'); Tilt sets nothing itself since web/vite.config.ts resolves /__bridge from the same variable
the worker rejects any connection that cannot echo the published token, checked before the newest-bridge-wins takeover so a local process cannot evict the real bridge by connecting
a discovery file naming a dead pid is removed on read, not merely ignored
PORT belongs to the storage server alone now; bridge and worker no longer read it
a browser connecting while no bridge is attached is told deviceOffline immediately rather than left on an indefinite spinner

a bridge attach (restart, re-dial or takeover) closes every channel on the device: owners with 1012 so the browser redials quickly and runs a fresh e2ee handshake (the old session died with the old bridge socket, so a replayed open is unusable), guests with 1008 so they re-run the /client gate; only the owner's token is replayed, and only to a bridge that proved that owner's claim — see session-collaboration
newest bridge wins, so a reconnecting bridge can take over from a half-dead predecessor the relay has not noticed
the relay persists nothing and logs no payload
with RELAY_URL unset nothing dials and the local-only setup is unchanged
a browser may only reach a device it owns or holds a grant on (see session-collaboration); if storage cannot verify a device's secret the relay refuses the connection rather than admitting it

a browser socket carries a monotonic generation stamp; a frame arriving on a socket whose generation is no longer current is dropped rather than applied — switchDevice closes the old socket but does not detach its message handler, so a late frame from the previous machine could otherwise reach applyServerMessage after clearBootstrap()

machineOffline is surfaced by ConnectionBanner after bootstrap too, not only by the pre-bootstrap ConnectingMachine screen — relay-up-but-machine-gone otherwise rendered as a healthy 'connected' UI in which every action silently went nowhere

the gate never connects to a machine this browser was not shown: on a first visit (no remembered device id) it renders ChooseMachine — the whole list, with health, platform, last-seen and an owner badge — and connects only after an explicit pick, even when the account has exactly one machine

chooseDevice's remembered/most-recent heuristic resumes a choice rather than making one, so a remembered machine that has since been revoked puts the list back up instead of silently falling through to a different computer

a machine's name is the hostname it registered with, stored in plaintext and shown to everyone it shares a session with; PATCH /v1/devices/:id lets the owner rename it, which is the user's only control over what that hostname leaks

DeviceGate dials the remembered machine optimistically (bootDial) before the device list has loaded, since rememberedDeviceId() is a synchronous localStorage read the socket need not wait behind a network round trip; the dial is dropped if the list lands without that id in it, so the gate-never-connects-to-an-unshown-machine rule still holds once the list is authoritative

/client holds a browser for up to OWNER_ATTACH_GRACE_MS only when hub.ownerId is still null in this relay process (waitForAgent) — closes a race where a browser reconnects, after a relay restart, faster than its own bridge finishes verifyDevice, which used to refuse the machine's own owner 1008 and cost a 5s backoff per attempt; a running machine with an attached bridge pays nothing, and the hold never widens access, only delays a classification

a connect never waits on Clerk without a deadline: openSocket races getToken({skipCache:true}) against TOKEN_TIMEOUT_MS (10s), then the cached getToken() against 5s; if both fail it schedules the ordinary RECONNECT_DELAY_MS retry instead of dialling — a hung mint used to leave a link with no socket and no retry timer, an endless spinner
one connect in flight per link (connectingSince); wake, online, retry and Reconnect now all funnel into openSocket
browser storage calls carry a 10s token deadline and a 15s AbortSignal, so the device-list splash step cannot spin forever

every relay client refusal is logged and recorded with its reason (bad-token/no-token/not-owner-no-grant with ownerId/storage-unreachable/bridge-too-old), as are waitForAgent outcomes and agent refusals (unauthorized vs unreachable); a per-device event history (50 x 1000 devices, LRU, no payloads or tokens) survives the idle-hub sweep and is served only in the secret-gated GET / as events

the browser keeps a localStorage diag ring (lines.diag) of connect-path events, echoed as [diag] console lines; ConnectingMachine's slow help (portalled into the boot splash) shows a plain hint, with the link phase and Send diagnostics/Copy (and Unpair) behind a collapsed Details toggle, and an unsent stall is uploaded once on the next hello
POST /v1/diagnostics stores nothing: it sanitises the report (scalar fields only, bounded, token query params redacted) and writes one [diag] userId=… line to storage stdout

connect deadlines: an encrypted socket has HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS (20s) from open to a ready channel, then HELLO_TIMEOUT_MS (60s) to deliver hello with no pong check in that window, and the post-hello PONG_TIMEOUT_MS is 30s; expiry closes and redials (diag handshake-timeout / hello-timeout), and none of the timers run down while the relay says no bridge is attached (tracked per socket)

the bridge binds 127.0.0.1 unless LINES_BRIDGE_HOST names 0.0.0.0 or :: (127.0.0.1 and localhost mean the default; any other value is refused, logged, and loopback used) — every local caller (the page, the codex MCP child, the OAuth redirect) dials 127.0.0.1 by number

a direct socket is admitted only from this machine's own page (a loopback origin from a loopback peer), from an origin listed in LINES_BRIDGE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, or as a non-browser client (no Origin) on loopback; Origin null (sandboxed frame, file://) is refused like any stranger; refusals are 403, decided in verifyClient before the socket exists, so a refused page never gets a hello

on a loopback bind a Host header that does not name this machine (localhost exactly, or a loopback IP literal) is a DNS-rebinding page and gets 421, on plain HTTP and the WebSocket upgrade alike; a missing Host fails closed; a wildcard bind skips the check
LINES_BRIDGE_DIRECT=0 refuses every direct WebSocket upgrade; the desktop app sets it in relay mode, where its window reaches the bridge through the relay; plain HTTP routes are unaffected
the bridge's WebSocketServer caps one inbound frame at MAX_FRAME_BYTES (64 MiB) rather than ws's 100 MiB default
the loopback port stays reachable by any local process, and a non-browser client there needs nothing more on a desktop install (no Clerk gate); Lines assumes a single-user machine

every path that installs a context's storage token (hello, in-channel auth refresh, the relay's token push) goes through setClerkToken, which refuses a token whose sub is not the context's user; the single-tenant 'local' context takes one only under LINES_DEV_SUPERVISED=1 (the dev relay with auth off), never on a desktop install
tokenRefreshAction: a guest's refresh is ignored, a relayed owner's accepted on the relay's word, a direct socket's re-verified through Clerk where CLERK_SECRET_KEY is set and ignored otherwise

a guest's Clerk token never reaches the host's bridge: the relay forwards token null on a guest open, keeps only the owner's token for a re-push (setToken ignores anyone but ownerId, the attach re-push is filtered to ownerId) and drops a guest's {type:'auth'} frame after a full JSON parse — stripped at the relay because the bridge is code the host runs

the bridge sends its device secret in the x-lines-device-secret header, never the URL; the relay still reads the deprecated secret query when the header is absent and logs neither form, so the relay must deploy before a desktop release whose bridge sends only the header

APP_PROTOCOL_VERSION is 6 (host-issued guest grants) and the relay's COLLAB_MIN_PROTOCOL defaults to 6, so a guest reaches only a bridge that admits guests on grants it minted; an older bridge keeps serving its owner

every id that becomes a path under ~/.lines-app passes isValidStoreId: a relay channel whose attested user id or grant host id is malformed is closed 1008 before any context exists, userStoreRoot and UserRegistry.get throw on one, a malformed session id has no transcript and deleting it is a no-op, and loadTranscript for a session the context does not know answers empty
the bridge makes ~/.lines-app 0700 at startup whoever started it (Tilt and a terminal start it without the desktop shell), and creates transcripts and rewind sidecars 0600
architecturalRules: only the secret's hash is stored, never the plaintext, so a database compromise cannot yield anything that impersonates a device
the relay holds no database credentials and never queries Postgres directly - it asks storage, the only process with DB credentials at all

the /client gate has two branches, both failing closed at the earliest point: the owner check (hub.ownerId === userId) is unchanged and never consults storage; anyone else must hold a grant from POST /v1/devices/authorize (see session-collaboration)

POST /v1/devices/verify is machine-to-machine with no Clerk token, so it is gated by a constant-time-compared RELAY_SHARED_SECRET instead, and excluded from storage's public router in a hosted deployment even with the secret guessed; unset, storage refuses verification with 503 rather than falling open
device identity (mint, hash, register) lives in server/src/device.ts, shared by the desktop app and the CLI pairing script, so the two cannot drift on the credential format

Clerk token providers are installed during render, not inside useEffect - child effects (DeviceGate) run before parent effects (AuthedConnect), so an effect-based registration meant the device list's first fetch and the first socket connect both fired with no token attached
switchDevice closes the existing socket and clears bootstrapped before reconnecting, rather than waiting for the old one to drop - in-flight messages on it belong to the old machine's bridge
the socket URL is built with URL/searchParams, not concatenation - the relay matches its endpoint path exactly and a concatenated token could produce a non-matching path
BrowserLink covers only what the bridge genuinely calls; every addition is one more thing an alternative transport must implement
close() must move readyState off LINK_OPEN synchronously, so broadcast does not re-close the same wedged link on every message
removal from ctx.sockets is owned solely by the 'close' handler, including on the hard-limit path
a per-socket 'error' listener is mandatory: an unhandled 'error' on an EventEmitter throws and takes the bridge down; a plain-object link avoids the footgun entirely
linkSendAction is pure and exported so the policy is testable without a socket
APP_PROTOCOL_VERSION is bumped only for browser<->bridge changes; the bridge<->worker PROTOCOL_VERSION is a separate contract on its own numbering
hello.bridge is optional in the type, because a hosted web app will meet bridges older than itself
the helpers live in workerProtocol.ts, not a module of their own: port discovery is part of the bridge<->worker contract, and a separate file would widen the worker's tsx-watch restart trigger
APP_ROOT is defined in workerProtocol.ts and re-exported by store.ts, so the worker can reach it without importing the bridge graph
publishing is atomic (temp + rename) and 0600; watchRuntimeInfo watches the directory, not the file, because rename replaces the inode
timers/watchers are released via WorkerClient.dispose() rather than unref(), which would make a timer invisible to node's mock timers

the bridge's token is published but not enforced on browser connections (a browser cannot set WebSocket headers); the upgrade check (verifyClient: this machine's own pages by default) and, where CLERK_SECRET_KEY is set, the Clerk gate guard that path, and /__bridge exposes only the port

connectionPolicy.ts is pure and dependency-free; verifyClient is its one piece of glue, shared by the bridge and its socket test so the test exercises the code that runs; the policy is decided before the socket exists rather than in handleConnection
the bind is IPv4 on purpose: every local caller dials 127.0.0.1 by number, so Tilt's probe and ws.ts name 127.0.0.1 rather than localhost, which may resolve to ::1 first
setClerkToken is the single writer of ctx.clerkToken, so the token-subject rule cannot be honoured on two installing paths and missed on the third
a live ws socket and node's mock timers cannot be mixed; tests compress the client's intervals instead

the relay client is a peripheral, never a supervisor: relay health must never restart the bridge and absolutely never the worker, which would turn a relay blip into a reconcile, an interruptedAt stamp and an auto-continued turn

the payload is opaque - the relay routes on the header and never parses the message, so end-to-end encryption can encrypt payload alone with no codec rewrite; the one exception is a guest's frame toward the bridge, parsed for its type so an auth refresh can be dropped — it reads nothing the relay could not already see, and an owner's frame is never looked at
frames are forwarded synchronously inside the message handler; an await per frame would let two race and reorder a stream
a dropped relay socket must synthesize close for every open channel, else ctx.sockets keeps dead links and broadcast serialises into them forever
RelayChannel is a plain object, not an EventEmitter, so it cannot inherit the throw-on-unhandled-error hazard

the relay is NOT the auth edge: the attested userId is a routing hint, and owner authority on a relay channel comes from a static key the machine pinned itself at enrollment (see end-to-end-encryption). The Clerk token still is not re-verified on a relayed channel — that part stands, and it is authorization for storage sync rather than for driving the machine; whose token it is, though, is checked on every path (setClerkToken). A guest channel is encrypted too, against the machine key from the invite link, and reaches handleConnection only on a grant the bridge minted (see session-collaboration)
relay/ shares no types with the app and the bridge does not import the relay package; frame shapes are duplicated in relayClient.ts on purpose
reconnect uses exponential backoff with jitter, since a flat retry turns one relay restart into a synchronised stampede

terminate() on supersede is deliberately aggressive rather than a graceful close-and-drain: a superseded bridge has no readers left, so draining it only leaves a noisy half-open socket around longer — the trade-off is a louder log during a genuine flap, which is a feature during triage

the bridge closes its own pre-existing socket (and drops its channels) at the start of connect(), before dialling — belt-and-braces alongside the single-flight retryTimer, so RelayClient itself can never be the source of two live sockets for one device
the single-instance lock file lives beside device.json under the same APP_ROOT rather than a new path resolver, reusing the existing app-data-root convention (see app-data-root.md)

stale-lock detection is process.kill(pid, 0): ESRCH means nothing holds the pid, so the new process takes the lock; any other outcome (including EPERM, another OS user's live process) is treated as held

only instance:'desktop' is preemptible, and only after cross-checking the pid against readRuntimeInfo('bridge', 'desktop') — the lock file's word alone must never be enough to SIGTERM a pid, since pids are reused
armLockRelease (process.on('exit', releaseBridgeLock)) is registered only after a successful claim, so a refused start never touches the incumbent's lock file
the supersede circuit breaker lives entirely in RelayClient, never in index.ts or the lock — it only slows its own retry and never restarts or blocks anything else

hello.local is a property of the link, not the app: true only for a socket that is both unrelayed and on loopback, since the bridge can be opened to every interface on purpose (LINES_BRIDGE_HOST, for LAN testing) and then a LAN socket is as remote as the relay for anything that opens a window on the host's screen. Absent means not local, so it fails closed

waitForAgent's timeout is deliberately not unref()'d — unlike WorkerClient.dispose()'s timers, it is cleared the instant a bridge attaches and is bounded at a few seconds, so unref()ing it would let an idle event loop drain before the deadline and the promise would never settle
HubRegistry.sweep() also skips a hub with a browser parked in waitForAgent (hasPendingClients), so the 60s idle sweep cannot drop a hub out from under a waiter before its bridge attaches

features.name: Workspace reads over the WebSocket
features.purpose: File contents, directory listings, the docs bundle, @mention search, attachments and chunked media previews (image, video, audio, pdf) travel over the authenticated WebSocket instead of bridge HTTP routes, removing the Clerk token from query strings and leaving the bridge with no file-serving HTTP surface. One kind, writeFile, lets the owner save an edit to an existing text file.
businessRules: status keeps using HTTP codes because the client already maps 403/404/413/415 to user-facing messages
a request made while disconnected rejects immediately; in-flight requests reject on close rather than hanging
find stays all-or-nothing across roots: a partial result reads as 'no match here' and would silently hide a folder
attachments are capped at the same 2MB as the old /file route
grep is all-or-nothing across roots like find; sessionSearch clamps every session id through sessionInReach
media serves only browser-renderable extensions (415 otherwise), clamps each request to 1MB, returns 413 over 200MB and 400 for an offset outside the file
media is pulled one chunk at a time so live frames interleave on the shared socket and relay instead of queuing behind one large frame

the owner's file, media and writeFile reach any path on the host (resolveFilePath: their own disk over their own authenticated socket, the agent's reach); a guest of either scope stays clamped to their session cwds; tree, docs, find, grep, sessionSearch, sessionDiffFile and attachment stay root-scoped for everyone
writeFile is owner-only, enforced in handleFileRequest and the handler: every file kind rides the readFiles cap, so a View or Full guest would otherwise write to the host's disk

for a guest, every read, write and media request is served from where its path really lands: inside a granted root both as written and once symlinks are followed, then read or written at that resolved real path (grantedReal), gated again there; a link that can't be followed is 403. The owner's single-file routes skip the root check but still touch only the real path they checked
writeFile writes only existing regular text files, and answers 413 over 2MB, 415 on a NUL byte, 400 without content

an attachment is served only to a connection that reaches its session (sessionInReach): a session-scope guest reads its own sessions' attachments and no others'; the session is read off where the file really is, so a link planted in the attachments directory, or from one session's folder into another's, is refused
grep never searches through a symlink that leaves its root (git lists a symlink by its own path, and its index can name a file under a directory since swapped for a link)
writeFile with a stale expectedMtimeMs answers 409 with the current mtime and writes nothing; absent expectedMtimeMs writes unconditionally
a save made during a running turn in the session cwd is attributed to the agent by the session diff
architecturalRules: handlers are pure {status, body} functions in their own module rather than http.ServerResponse writers, so they can serve a relay channel and are testable without a socket (index.ts listens on import)
fileResponse is settled in ws.ts before applyServerMessage and returns early; the store never sees it
replies go to the originating link, never via broadcast, since two tabs each have their own in-flight reqIds
corsFor, httpUserId, WEB_ORIGIN and withAuthToken are deleted rather than retained: each was a second auth path to keep in step with the socket's
attachment blob URLs are revoked on unmount, else every re-render leaks a blob for the life of the page
media is its own FileRequestKind rather than a new body on file, so version skew is safe: an old bridge answers 400, shown as 'update the bridge'
media blob URLs are revoked on unmount and the chunk loop stops after the in-flight request; SVG renders via , never inline
writeFile is its own FileRequestKind, so an old bridge answers 400, shown as 'restart or update it'
writeFile writes a sibling temp file, chmods it to the original's mode, then renames over the realpath target, so a failure never truncates the file and a symlink stays a symlink

containment is one implementation: realPathOf/isRealInside are exported from server/src/autoGuard.ts and used by resolveWorkspacePath, the attachment route and grep, so the routes follow links exactly the way the auto-mode guard does (the route-local realInsideGrant is gone)

a route touches the resolved real path it checked (grantedReal), never the path as named, which would follow its links a second time after the check and let a link swapped in between redirect the access
grep pays for a realpath only on candidates that are a symlink or sit below a linked directory (isLink, linkedDirs memoized per directory), since it walks thousands of files
resolveFilePath is for single-file routes only; pointing tree, find or grep at it would let the sidebar and search walk the whole disk

features.name: Desktop app
features.purpose: The menu-bar app that supervises the bridge and worker as local children, owns this machine's pairing state and tray UI, and the packaging that turns it into an installable macOS .dmg that runs away from a repo checkout.
businessRules: right-click shows a native context menu in every shell window; link actions copy or open externally, never in-window
a restart is refused while any session is running, waiting-permission, or waiting-approval, since a restart kills bridge and worker together under one atomic update
closing the window does not quit the app, and must not kill an in-flight turn

an update installs only from ready and only on a signed build (CAN_SELF_INSTALL); a browser restart is refused while a session is active, the tray and notification restart warns first, and nothing restarts the app on its own

in hosted mode (the default; local mode needs LINES_LOCAL_MODE=1) the shell serves no local UI - it registers this machine's device identity, spawns the bridge with the relay/storage/device env, and shows a pairing code window only if the machine has not been claimed yet

childEnv sets LINES_BRIDGE_DIRECT=0 in relay mode, so the bridge accepts no direct socket at all (the window reaches it through the relay, and a socket on the bridge's port drives the agent), and LINES_BRIDGE_DIRECT=1 in local mode, whose window is a loopback page that dials the bridge directly

~/.lines-app is 0700 and both log generations 0600: ensurePrivateAppRoot runs at every start before anything writes beneath it (best-effort), and appendLog creates the log 0600 in a 0700 directory — transcripts, the device secret, e2ee keys, MCP credentials and logs all live there

the window's permission handler is an allowlist on the app's own origin: the microphone (and only it) for media, APP_PERMISSIONS (notifications, clipboard-sanitized-write, fullscreen, openExternal) for the rest; a third-party page the window wanders onto gets nothing, where Electron's default grants everything

the local-mode UI server sends the hosted page's headers (nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy) and localModeCsp(): the hosted policy with this machine's loopback and the configured storage/relay origins added to connect-src, images only from the page's own origin, data:/blob: and Clerk's avatars
an upload is refused unless R2_RELEASE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is an absolute https URL: the update feed derived from it is what the shipped app trusts, so it must not be rewritable on the wire

a relay open alone is not proof of pairing - the relay accepts the socket before asking storage whether the device is claimed, so Connected lags the raw socket by RELAY_SETTLE_MS and a 1008 close reads as Not paired rather than an indefinite Connecting
a pairing code never requires an app restart to refresh, on a timer or on demand
device registration failing at boot is not fatal - RelayClient retries the relay forever, so a machine that registers late still comes up once storage is reachable again
hosted is the default; local mode requires LINES_LOCAL_MODE=1 and web/dist is not shipped
a missing or too-old Claude Code refuses the turn with an actionable message in both the browser and the tray
LINES_CLAUDE_PATH is exclusive: when set, no other location is tried

updates download in the background (autoDownload) and are handed to Squirrel.Mac at once (autoInstallOnAppQuit); the user restarts into them from the tray, the notification, the manual-check dialog or a browser, or they install on a normal quit; a download or staging failure for a known version falls back to available and the download page

a bridge child refuses to start if another live process already holds this machine's single-instance lock, unless that holder is instance:'desktop' (a previous tray bridge) — in which case ours preempts it instead; this is a second guard beneath the shell's own requestSingleInstanceLock, for a respawn racing a not-yet-exited previous bridge or a bridge started by hand alongside the packaged app; without it two bridge processes can share one device.json and the relay ends up superseding one of them, which is visible in every connected browser as a flicker until it does

when a different installation (a dev checkout, most commonly Tilt) holds the lock instead, the tray's own bridge stands down rather than fighting for it — no bridge or worker spawns at startup, or the running bridge is not respawned after exiting/being preempted — until the lock clears, and the tray reports this plainly ('Paused — another bridge owns this machine') rather than 'Connecting…' or a silent retry loop

the worker is never part of a stand-down: only the bridge collides on the machine lock and the relay device identity, so a worker mid-turn is left alone when a sibling process collides on a resource the worker doesn't touch
a release is refused when desktop/package.json's version is already published, unless --force (or the workflow's force input) is passed — artifacts are immutable at the edge
npm run release -w desktop is an alias of ship; the upload-only step is upload
npm run ship -w desktop deletes desktop/release/ before every build
