npm run ship -w desktop runs the root typecheck and the server and relay suites before packaging, with no skip flag; only the release workflow sets LINES_SHIP_TESTED=1, because its guard job already ran them on the same commit
the desktop release pipeline is manual workflow_dispatch only — no tag convention, no release on push to main
an update notification fires at most once per version (in-memory dedup), not once per state transition, so the 6h re-check does not re-nag for the same version
buildHello's update field is owner-only; a guest never learns about a pending update on a machine they don't own

every update check outcome has a permanent tray row (checking, disabled-and-why, available, failed, last-checked, or never-checked) — none of the old silent failure modes (a rejected check, no feed URL, a dev build, an updater that would not start) can read as up to date anymore

a failed automatic check retries once after 5 minutes, and again on waking from sleep if the last check is over an hour stale — covers a login-time network race and a setInterval a laptop's sleep starved
the tray states the running version from the same value (APP_VERSION) the updater compares the feed against, so the two can never disagree
a manual 'Check for updates' always answers with a dialog, including 'up to date' — it must never look like it did nothing

hosted mode's 'Open Lines' opens a native window at config.webUrl by default; the choice between that and the browser persists in ~/.lines-app/desktop.json, and 'Open in Browser'/'Open Desktop Window' is always the other row, one click away
the desktop window has its own cookie jar, separate from Safari or Chrome — signing in in a browser does not sign in the window and vice versa; dev and packaged runs share one jar

nothing but the app itself ever loads in the chrome-less window; a navigation stays in-window only as the app origin itself, a dedicated identity host, a scoped OAuth entry path (github.com's /login/oauth/ only), or the continuation of a flow already off-app — everything else, including any other github.com link, opens in the real browser
the pairing window navigates nowhere at all, not even to the app's own origin - clicking the pairing card's link opens the real browser and leaves the code on screen

an off-app window always has a way back: a 'Back to Lines' pill is injected into any page the window lands on outside the app origin, and the tray's 'Open Lines' reloads an existing window back to the app instead of just showing it as-is
desktop.log stamps every line with an ISO time, re-cuts child output into whole tagged lines, and rotates once to desktop.1.log past 5MB

the shell logs power transitions ([power] suspend/resume/lock-screen/unlock-screen), relay link changes ([relay-status]), child spawn/exit with uptime, and device registration outcome (never the pairing code)

the app window's console is mirrored to the log as [renderer] — only [diag]/[ws]/[e2ee] lines plus warnings/errors — along with did-finish-load (URL without fragment), render-process-gone and unresponsive; observed from the main process, so the window keeps its no-preload/no-IPC contract

the tray's Collect diagnostics… zips both log generations, run/*/*.json with token deleted, the bridge lock and a summary.json into ~/.lines-app/diagnostics via /usr/bin/ditto; device.json is never copied

ship.mjs stamps desktopPending in changelog.json into a new desktop release when it commits a version bump, in the same commit; the release workflow's guard job fails if desktopPending is non-empty because CI cannot commit the stamp (see whats-new)
architecturalRules: context menu hooked inside attachNavigationGuards so every window, including popups, gets it without a preload
loginShellPath() resolves the login shell's PATH once for both children, because a GUI-launched macOS app inherits a minimal PATH that breaks the agent's shell-outs
children are spawned with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, since process.execPath inside Electron is the Electron binary and would otherwise relaunch the app
the worker is never auto-restarted on crash - its live queries are gone, and a silent respawn would look like a healthy session that lost its turn; the bridge is restarted freely
the desktop app and Tilt share the same LINES_INSTANCE/port-discovery contract, so a dev checkout and an installed app never collide
device identity lives in server/src/device.ts, not duplicated in the shell, so it and npm run pair -w server cannot drift on the credential format
ROOT resolves to process.resourcesPath when packaged, the repo root otherwise, which is the one branch letting a dev checkout and an installed app share this file

an unsigned bundle (electron-builder identity: null) has no _CodeSignature/CodeResources, which macOS reports as "damaged" with no Open Anyway path — releases are Developer ID signed and notarized with the hardened runtime, and ship.mjs passes forceCodeSigning so a missing or untrusted certificate fails the build instead of shipping unsigned
the agent SDK ships unbundled because sdk.mjs resolves through createRequire(import.meta.url)
the SDK's -darwin-arm64 platform package is deleted; every query passes pathToClaudeCodeExecutable so its resolver never runs
the bridge and worker bundles must be ESM — server and shared use import.meta.dirname, which is undefined under CJS
the version floor is ours or nobody's — the SDK performs no version handshake at all
releases use a second public R2 bucket, because public-read is a bucket-level setting

the bridge lock lives beside device.json under the same APP_ROOT, reusing the existing app-data-root path helpers rather than adding a new resolver; a stale lock is detected via process.kill(pid, 0) (ESRCH means take it), and LINES_ALLOW_MULTIPLE_BRIDGES=1 is the deliberate escape hatch that must never be set in a real deployment

foreignBridgeLock/BRIDGE_LOCK_FILE/EXIT_BRIDGE_LOCK_HELD are duplicated in main.ts rather than imported from server/src/index.ts, the same precedent APP_ROOT already sets in this file — EXIT_BRIDGE_LOCK_HELD=78 is a contract between the two files, changing it in one without the other silently breaks the stand-down trigger

enterStandDown is the only path that clears bridge/worker handles and arms the recheck timer; both the startup check and spawnChild's exit handler funnel into it rather than each duplicating the tray-copy and recheck logic

every send across the shell↔bridge IPC channel (updateStatus, relayStatus, updateRestartRequest) is guarded on connected with a no-op error callback, not sent bare - the bridge exit handler never nulls the child handle before respawning, so a non-null handle is not proof of a live channel, and Node's ChildProcess/process.send throws synchronously into a closed one, which is uncaught and fatal to the shell
a local release and a CI release both run desktop/scripts/ship.mjs — the same code path, so they cannot drift into two procedures
ship.mjs derives LINES_UPDATE_FEED_URL/LINES_DOWNLOAD_URL from R2_RELEASE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL rather than taking them as separate inputs
release-desktop.yml's guard job runs on ubuntu-latest (1x billing) so a stale version or type error is cheap; release runs on macos-latest (10x billing, arm64, a standard runner)
autoUpdater.logger is wired to the shell's log file before every guard in startUpdateChecks runs, so the reason a check never happened is captured too, not just the reason one failed
UpdateStatus is deliberately not widened with a last-checked timestamp — the browser can neither trigger nor act on a check, so that state stays shell-local rather than crossing the wire protocol

updateTray() only calls setContextMenu/setTitle when a signature of the rendered template actually changes, since it runs every 2s and would otherwise reinstall a byte-identical NSMenu tens of thousands of times a day and could swap the menu out from under one the user has open

the desktop window gets no preload and no IPC; every BrowserWindow (main, pairing, and any popup allowed through setWindowOpenHandler) is routed through attachNavigationGuards, which evaluates one ordered decision function (navigationVerdict) against will-navigate and setWindowOpenHandler and hands anything not in-app to shell.openExternal, logging every blocked/dropped navigation and every non-trivial allow

will-redirect is deliberately unhandled — every OAuth 302 leg arrives that way, and guarding it would mean enumerating hosts no allowlist can enumerate; will-frame-navigate is likewise not added since web/src has no iframes and it would double-handle the main frame
the 'Back to Lines' pill is injected via insertCSS/executeJavaScript rather than an inline style or IPC, so a page's CSP cannot strip it and the window keeps its zero-privilege, no-preload contract
the dock tile is shown iff a BrowserWindow exists, in hosted mode; local mode keeps a permanent tile as before
shell-owned state under ~/.lines-app is named for the shell, never for its content — desktop.json follows that rather than server/src/store.ts's content-named convention (device.json, projects.json)

localModeCsp() copies deploy/docker/web-nginx.conf's policy by hand, adding only loopback and the configured remote origins to connect-src; nothing checks the two agree, so a change to one belongs in the other
ensurePrivateAppRoot() runs in start() before loadPrefs() and the first shellLog, the first write beneath APP_ROOT, so the directory is 0700 before anything lands in it
relatedDecisions: CAN_SELF_INSTALL is on: from 0.2.44 updates install in place; 0.2.43 and earlier only check, so their users install the first self-installing build by hand once; a packaged app outside Applications offers once to move itself there, since Squirrel.Mac cannot replace a copy on the DMG or a read-only one
electron is pinned exact so electron-builder can resolve its version from a hoisted workspace
arm64 only; x64/universal is a one-line mac.target change
production-deployment's VITE_DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_URL is now set once, to the stable alias, rather than per release
the R2 release credentials now live in two places (VPS lines.env and GitHub Actions secrets) — same token, wider blast radius

features.name: Recipes
features.purpose: Publishable, versioned prompt documents with tags, screenshots, an author and a public run count; browse everyone's published recipes and run one (standalone, inside a chosen workflow, or as a synthesized workflow), including bundles of recipes.
businessRules: a RecipeContent carries exactly one of prompt or members; a bundle's members must all be leaves and publishing a bundle requires every member already published
bundle members are unversioned - the newest version of a member is always the one that runs; reproducibility lives in the synthesized workflow's frozen inline step prompts instead
run counts increment once per recipe at trigger time, only after the first prompt is successfully injected; a bundle and each of its expanded members count separately
tags are freeform, server-normalized and deduped on every save, capped at 6, and may be empty; tag filtering is client-side over the wholesale shared pull
a run always spawns a new session; a multi-recipe run cannot also specify an existing workflowId

R2 is optional - unconfigured R2 answers 503 on upload and the recipe still saves without a screenshot; a public base pointed at the S3 API endpoint instead of a public r2.dev/custom domain uploads successfully but never renders, which the storage server warns about at boot

a run containing someone else's recipe (a leaf, a bundle member or the bundle itself) uses only FOREIGN_RECIPE_MODES (plan, default; anything else becomes default), stops after every step, cannot run inside one of the user's workflows, and sets the session's permissionCeiling so an approved plan resumes in default rather than auto

the run modal shows every prompt that will run and requires a confirmation; the bridge refuses a foreign run unless runRecipe.confirmedPrompts equals its own expansion's prompts in run order, so a recipe changed after the user read it does not run

someone else's recipes carry no trust mark and are confirmed per run, never trusted once (trustRecipe refuses them); an own recipe this machine has not verified is refused, directly or as a bundle member, until reviewed — under LINES_E2EE_STRICT=0 an unsigned or forged one still runs

Duplicate carries the original's mark (a copy of a stranger's recipe arrives foreign, held back until reviewed); restoring an unverified version is disabled because a restore is re-signed by this machine

setSharedRecipes drops any row claiming the current user, and storage takes ownerId from the row owner on /recipes/shared and ownerId/id from the row on /recipes/:ownerId/:id/versions — a row claiming the reader would otherwise be re-published under their name and run without the foreign confirmation
addRecipeVersions adopts only the requested recipe's history, and an unverified own version never displaces a trusted copy of the same number with different content

a recipe image URL must be under this deployment's bucket (R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/recipes/, no '..'); PUT /recipes skips any version with an off-bucket image, and with no bucket configured no image URL is accepted
the /recipes/stats ETag is computed over the rows the caller can see (own stats and published recipes'), as its answer is
architecturalRules: RecipeEngine is a standalone class, not folded into WorkflowEngine, since a recipe has no step/handoff/pin semantics
all bundle/tag invariants are enforced only inside RecipeEngine.saveRecipe - storage treats data as an opaque JSON blob apart from the image-URL check on PUT /recipes
a multi-recipe run's synthesized workflow is saved, never ephemeral, because every WorkflowEngine lifecycle method re-resolves the def by id and silently no-ops if it is missing
RecipeEngine.expandForRun is the only place bundle expansion happens; the client always sends refs, never a pre-flattened list
an off-bucket version is skipped, not rewritten (the blob carries its author's signature, and an edited copy would stop verifying for everyone) and not a 400 (a whole history is pushed at once)
the foreign- and unverified-recipe rules are decided in recipeCommands.runRecipe, never trusted from the modal; confirmedPrompts is compared with the bridge's expansion, never used in its place
the run cooldown is stamped only after every refusal, so a corrected retry is not swallowed as a double-click

features.name: Production deployment
features.purpose: Runs the server side of a hosted install (relay, storage, static web bundle, static marketing page) as containers behind Traefik, with per-hostname TLS. Excludes the bridge and worker entirely - the agent runs on each user's own machine.
businessRules: the web build stage also bakes VITE_DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_URL; unlike the other three VITE_* args it may legitimately be empty (no desktop release yet), so its build-time assertion only fires when the value is set
VITE_DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_URL is set once, to the stable R2 alias (Lines-latest.dmg), not per release — a desktop release republishes that key so web never needs a rebuild in lockstep
storage never gets a published port or Traefik exposure beyond its one router; only relay and the browser's device calls reach it, everything else is internal-network only
migrations run via `docker compose run --rm migrate` before the first `up` against a new database, using the direct (:5432) connection string

the same ordering applies to every later schema change, not just the first bring-up: migrate deploy must run against the live database before a new storage image serves traffic, or the new code 500s with a Prisma unknown-column/table error (P2021) against the old schema

the relay's health endpoint (GET / on the relay's own host) accepts an optional x-relay-secret header; a request presenting the correct RELAY_SHARED_SECRET gets a hubs array (per-device attach counts/timestamps) alongside the ordinary health body, used to triage a duplicate-bridge or flapping-relay-link report without touching Postgres — see hosted-machine-access

the deploy SSH key's VPS-side authorized_keys entry forces /root/deploy-lines.sh regardless of the command CI sends — that key can run nothing else on the box; the script takes three stdin lines (GHCR token, GHCR actor, image tag)

check-migration-safety.sh gates on added migration files (--diff-filter=A) between the push's before/after SHAs; editing an already-applied migration to add something destructive bypasses it — accepted because Prisma migrations are append-only by convention

images are pinned to the pushing commit's SHA: build pushes :latest and :<sha>, deploy-lines.sh exports TAG=<sha> from the third stdin line, and compose.yml reads ${TAG:-latest}; rollback is `TAG=<old-sha> docker compose --env-file lines.env up -d` with no rebuild, and an old two-line stdin caller still works and falls back to latest

Monaco's four editor surfaces are React.lazy-loaded rather than statically imported from the entry chunk, so their chunks are never named in index.html and carry no SRI hash — same-origin script-src is what still gates them; deliberate, since bundling Monaco into the entry chunk delayed first paint on every screen, including ones with no editor on them

the production database is hosted Supabase; any standalone Postgres is a drop-in alternative with DATABASE_URL and DIRECT_URL set to the same string and no pgbouncer param, including the optional bundled postgres service under the db compose profile
web and landing answer /download with a 302 to the runtime DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_URL (compose passes VITE_DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_URL, defaulting to /), so download clicks are counted from the access log
neither origin serves analytics JS or third-party embeds; growth metrics are the nginx access log (?ref= tags, /download 302s) plus read-only SQL

the CSP enforces (Content-Security-Policy, no longer Report-Only): rendered agent markdown could otherwise exfiltrate through an image URL, so img-src allows only 'self', data:, blob:, img.clerk.com and ${CSP_IMG_SRC} (the recipe bucket, from R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL via compose); trial a policy change as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first

R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL must be a bare origin (no path) for the CSP, since a CSP source with a path matches only that path; storage refuses to store a recipe image anywhere but under it, so the policy and the data agree

script-src and frame-src include https://challenges.cloudflare.com (Clerk's sign-up captcha); media-src is 'self' blob:; frame-src also allows blob: for the PDF preview; Clerk telemetry is off since connect-src does not allow its collector
a pk_live Clerk instance loads clerk-js from clerk.<its domain>, which neither Clerk wildcard matches: add that host to script-src and CSP_CONNECT_SRC before switching, or sign-in stops loading
no 'unsafe-inline' for scripts, so index.html's pre-paint splash guard is web/public/splash-guard.js, reading the per-build Clerk key from a data-clerk attribute

/html-preview.html and /html-preview.js are the one permissive route (sandbox directive, default-src *, unsafe-inline/eval, frame-ancestors 'self', no X-Frame-Options): the file viewer renders agent-written HTML there, safe because the sandbox directive forces an opaque origin; every other header stays and desktop local mode serves the same policy

every response carries HSTS (max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, no preload), a Permissions-Policy granting only microphone=(self), and no nginx version (server_tokens off); storage disables Express's x-powered-by

every table has row level security enabled with no policies and never FORCEd (20261006000000_row_level_security): Supabase's anon/authenticated roles (which hold no grants on these tables today) see nothing, while storage, connecting as the owning role, is unaffected; a DATABASE_URL naming another role needs BYPASSRLS, and a new table enables RLS in the migration that creates it

PUT /recipes skips (never rewrites, never 400s) any version whose images are not under ${R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/recipes/ (isServedRecipeImage) and reports how many it skipped; /recipes/stats's ETag covers only the rows the caller can see; /steps/resolve answers the caller's own versions and anyone's published ones, leaving out what they may not see exactly as a missing row, with refs type-checked and ownerId taken from the row

this release's migrations (row_level_security, mcp_env_names_only, share_grant_ids) run in the pipeline's migrate step before up -d; the env scrub is an UPDATE that discards stored values, which check-migration-safety.sh does not look for, so it passes the gate and cannot be rolled back

this project's Supabase migration history has gone missing before, so run prisma db pull --print (and migrate status) before migrate deploy — including before pushing a migration, since the pipeline runs migrate itself — and migrate resolve --applied any already-live migration first

deploy order for this release: storage with its migrations, then relay and web, then the desktop release — the released bridge sends its device secret only in a header the relay must already read, and guests reach a host only once its desktop bridge speaks protocol 6
architecturalRules: npm ci is scoped by --workspace rather than --omit=optional, since --omit=optional also drops @rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu (an optional dependency on the same platform-binary mechanism as the Claude SDK's native binary) and breaks vite build
the relay's Traefik router carries no StripPrefix middleware - relay/src/index.ts matches url.pathname exactly, so a rewritten path closes the socket with 1008

storage's public router excludes /v1/devices/verify, /presence and /authorize by rule, on top of each route's own shared-secret gate - defense in depth: a network-level exclusion and an application-level check, either could fail without the other

the deps layer's inputs are normalized by deploy/docker/normalize-manifests.mjs in a manifests stage: every version becomes 0.0.0 (manifests plus the lockfile's top level, root and workspace entries, by exact key), and scripts and desktop's build block are dropped, so version bumps and script edits no longer invalidate deps or force a new ~230 MB layer onto the registry and VPS; safe because npm ci runs --ignore-scripts and every @lines/* spec is "*" (the script exits 1 otherwise); any stage that runs a workspace script or reads its version must COPY that workspace first
the build job's services leg builds relay and storage together so both images share one deps blob; in separate jobs each would rerun npm ci on a deps miss and the VPS would pull two ~230 MB layers
the storage image installs openssl explicitly - node:22-slim ships without libssl and Prisma's query engine otherwise falls back to a guessed build and warns at every boot
the four VITE_* build args exist in two places kept in sync by hand: GitHub Actions secrets (CI image build) and lines.env on the VPS (manual build only) — nothing checks the two agree

nginx's envsubst filter is ^(CSP_CONNECT_SRC|CSP_IMG_SRC|DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_URL)$, and the image defaults DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_URL to / and CSP_IMG_SRC to empty, because an unsubstituted ${...} is an unknown nginx variable that fails the config at start

every nginx location that sets its own add_header (/assets/, /index.html, /sw.js, /html-preview.html, /html-preview.js) repeats the whole security header set, since add_header is inherited only by a block that declares none; a header added at server level goes into each of those blocks too

the optional postgres service publishes no port and sits only on the internal lines-db network shared with storage and migrate; their depends_on is required: false so Supabase deployments start without it, and POSTGRES_PASSWORD is not ${...:?} because compose interpolates profiled services too

features.name: Session collaboration
features.purpose: Invite another signed-in user into one session, or onto a whole machine, so they can prompt the same running agent, with live presence and attribution, without ever getting a copy of the host's data. Inverts the app's single-owner assumption: access becomes a capability set enforced by a compiler-checked default-deny table instead of a boolean owner check. The host's machine admits each guest itself, on a grant it minted and handed over in the invite link, over a channel encrypted end to end; the relay can narrow that grant but never widen it.
businessRules: four presets (view, prompt, collaborator, full); only full grants setPermissionMode, manageSessions (archive/unarchive/complete) and deleteSessions; without setPermissionMode a guest's requested session and workflow-step permission modes are clamped to the host's new-session default

a machine-scope guest with createSessions sees the host's workflow library read-only; other guests see only the workflows their visible sessions use; a guest with manageWorkflow runs their own workflow by sending it inline with createSession (self-contained, validated, stored as a session snapshot, never added to the host's library); its refs resolve to their exact pinned versions only, the guest's browser refuses to send it while their own machine holds any of it back unverified, and the host refuses a definition still carrying an untrusted mark

never grantable at any preset: settings, guard allowlist, project/worktree management, login/logout, device unpair, workflow/step/recipe authoring, installUpdate, pickFolder, minting/moving/revoking guest grants, trusting synced content or a signing machine
a machine-scope grant covers every session on the machine and outranks a session share on the same machine
several session shares on one machine intersect to the narrowest capability set, never the union
revoking a share, or unpairing/deleting the device, tombstones every grant on that device in one transaction

DELETE /v1/shares/:kind/:id is otherwise always owner-scoped (a grantee can revoke nothing) with one exception: kind === 'self' lets a guest tombstone their own grants on a machine (deviceId in the URL, grantee taken from the caller's own auth, never a parameter) via revokeGrantsForGrantee, which is userId-scoped in every where clause so it can never widen past the caller's own access; it never touches the Device row or another guest's grant, 404s when nothing matched, and is reached from Settings → Machines' Leave action (DevicesSection) via web/src/lib/shares.ts's leaveShare

a guest never gets a UserContext of their own and never sets clerkToken or triggers syncNow; nor does their Clerk token reach the host's machine at all (the relay strips it from open, keeps none for a re-push and drops a guest's auth refresh; a guest link relays none)

a guest's file access is clamped to the cwds of their granted sessions; the ~/.claude/plans auto-approve exception is owner-only; an attachment is served only for a session in the grant's reach, judged from where the file really lands
the relay's bridge-too-old check for a guest (guestNeedsNewerBridge) applies only while a bridge is attached, so a sleeping host reads as offline, not as a revoked grant

a guest channel is dropped, not replayed, when its device's bridge re-attaches, since the new bridge's protocol is unknown until its hello arrives; the guest's browser reconnects and re-runs the /client gate

revoking from the share modal ends the grant on the machine at once (revokeGuestGrant) and closes the guest's sockets there; failing that, the relay's sweep closes a live guest channel within GUEST_REAUTH_MS (60s) of storage's no, and the machine's reconciliation drops the grant within GRANT_RECONCILE_MS (60s) of being online with its owner's token
a promptNeedsApproval guest's prompt lands queuePaused on the owner's existing queue, no new state machine
presence and attribution identity always come from the connection's attested identity, never a client-supplied field
a historical row or the owner's own prompt with no recorded actor is attributed to the session's host

the collaborator address book (ShareContact) is decoupled from grant state on purpose — revoking a share or letting an invite expire never removes the remembered address; removing a contact is a hard delete, not a tombstone, and only clears the suggestion, never a grant

a queued prompt may be edited in place by its author or the machine owner (prompt cap, not interrupt); editing never clears queuePaused, and an edit by someone other than the author is recorded (editedAt/editedBy) but still flushes attributed to the author

switchProvider sits at MESSAGE_AUTHZ cap 'interrupt' (the most destructive cap the table has), and also requires the setModel cap and refuses an actor with promptNeedsApproval -- both checked inside SessionManager.switchProvider itself, since one MESSAGE_AUTHZ row can only express one cap

a guest is admitted only on a grant the host's own bridge minted (server/src/guestGrants.ts), presented as the first sealed frame {type:'guestGrant', tokens} of a channel encrypted against the machine key from the invite link; the relay's attestation only narrows it (guestAccessFor: a capability needs both sides, promptNeedsApproval holds if either asks, session scope on either side means the sessions both name and never createSessions, nothing left is 1008)

the grant token is 256 random bits, stored on the machine only as a sha256 hash (~/.lines-app/guest-grants.json, 0600), answered to the owner's socket alone (guestGrantMinted), and travels only in the invite link's fragment (#grant=…&key=…&device=…) and inside the encrypted channel; storage keeps only the grant id
an unredeemed grant expires with its invite (GRANT_CLAIM_TTL_MS, 7 days); the first account to redeem binds it, so a forwarded link stops there; a redeemed grant lasts until revoked

several grants for one guest on one machine combine to the widest (combineGrants; promptNeedsApproval only if every grant asks) and are then intersected with the relay's attestation, which storage computes as the narrowest, so a guest never gets more than storage currently allows

creating an invite needs the machine online, relaying and opened through the owner's account (the 'local' context cannot mint): ShareModal mints first, then createInvite with grantId, and revokes the grant if the invite fails; preset changes and revokes go to the machine too (updateGuestGrant/revokeGuestGrant, closing the sockets admitted on them), with a warning when its link is down

adoptJoinGrant binds a stashed grant only to the machine the link named and for that invite's code, never over a different key already pinned for that machine; tokens are kept per device, several each; JoinPage adopts after the claim, or after a failed claim when the device list already shows the machine as shared with them

a relaying bridge reconciles its grants every GRANT_RECONCILE_MS (60s) against the grant ids storage lists for the device (GET /v1/shares, grantTracking: true); it only removes, treats an error or a server without grantTracking as 'cannot say', and spares grants younger than GRANT_RECONCILE_GRACE_MS (10 min)

a guest starts sessions only inside one of the host's open project roots (guestCwdAllowed, symlinks resolved on both sides) and never in a new work tree; a guest's permission answer drops alwaysAllow and allowAsRead (permissionAnswerFor), and the card hides both buttons
the relay gate refuses a guest on storage's no and on no answer ('unreachable', logged storage-unreachable); the sweep closes a channel only on an answer, and runs one sweep at a time

COLLAB_MIN_PROTOCOL is 6: a bridge older than that admits guests on the relay's word, so the relay puts no guest through to it; a share made before host-issued grants has no token and is refused by a protocol-6 bridge until the owner sends a new invite link
architecturalRules: MESSAGE_AUTHZ is an exhaustive Record keyed on ClientMessage['type'] so an unclassified message is a compile error, not a review gap
SocketAccess lives on the sockets Map's value, never on BrowserLink, which stays a minimal structural contract
the relay's owner fast path never touches storage

the relay holds no database credentials and forwards the attested grant without interpreting capabilities (the sweep only compares it with storage's fresh answer); the only app message it parses is a guest's frame type, to drop a token refresh

admission is the host bridge's: a guest channel reaches handleConnection only through the channel gate's admitGuest, and handleConnection checks the grants again (none, or grants for a different host than the relay names, is 1008); the relay's attestation stays in the path only to narrow
grants live in ~/.lines-app/guest-grants.json as token hashes behind an injectable GuestGrantStore, so the policy is tested from a temp directory
storage keeps grant ids, never tokens, and nothing it says can create or widen a grant; liveGrantIds reads GET /v1/shares unsigned and soft-failing, since an answer can only drop grants
guestGrantMinted is handled point to point in ws.ts, like fileResponse, and never reaches the store
a guest channel's refusal text avoids the phrase 'end-to-end encrypted channel', which arms the client's owner-enrollment gate; a guest needs the link, not an enrollment

SecureChannel handles inbound frames one at a time so a later frame cannot overtake the grant; one handshake per channel and no enrollment on a guest channel, since a guest channel accepts any client key
parseShareCaps denies by default on anything not an explicit true
presence is bridge-local and ephemeral, never rides SessionMeta, needs no relay or storage support
resolvedActor sits alongside resolvedBy, never folded into it
a peer's prompt bubble stays right-aligned like the owner's; authorship is carried by avatar/colour, not by side
personMeta's palette is deliberately disjoint from agentMeta's

features.name: Multi-machine client
features.purpose: Hold a live link to more than one machine at once, but show exactly one machine's sessions at a time, chosen from a header switcher, so a browser holding a shared machine's link never has to merge two sets of owner state. Replaces web/src/ws.ts's single module-level socket with one MachineLink per machine, and rewrites three reducers (hello merge, draft pruning, auto-select) that were correct for one machine and destructive for two; a fourth (the hello reducer's owner-state fields) is scoped per machine behind a MachineView and projected onto the globals only for the primary.
businessRules: the primary machine's connectionStatus/machineOffline/bootstrapped/protocolSkew/bridge/workerStatus/storageStatus/updateStatus are the only values the global banners read

a hello's owner-state fields (projects, projectKeys, recentDirs, workflows/steps/recipes and their shared/pinned/stats variants, models, usage, openaiUsage, auth, openaiAuth, access, guardAllowlist, guardReview, memoryReview, mcpConnections, mcpReview) land in that machine's own MachineSlice.view and reach the global store fields only when the hello came from the primary machine; a non-primary hello, repeated or not, is inert against them

the four auto-open modal flags (loginModalOpen, guardReviewOpen, memoryReviewOpen, mcpReviewOpen) stay global but are gated on fromPrimary too, so a background machine can never raise a dialog about an account the user is not looking at

setPrimaryMachine spreads the new primary's MachineSlice.view over the same global fields the hello reducer writes (one projection, used by both) and recomputes activeProject against it, so a machine switch swaps projects/library/usage/account atomically with no round trip; it also clears selectedSessionId when the previously selected session's sessionMachine stamp is not the new primary, and no-ops entirely when the requested id is already primary

the sidebar's three groups (Sessions, Shared-with-me, Archived) and the project tab's status dot are scoped to sessionsOnMachine(sessions, sessionMachine, primaryDeviceId ?? ''); the store still holds every linked machine's sessions (message routing via sessionMachine, and alerts, need all of them), so this is a display-only scope

maybeAlert (web/src/lib/alerts.ts) is deliberately NOT scoped to the primary machine — a session finishing on a background machine still chimes and notifies, which is the point of keeping that link open; the header switcher badges the machine a notification came from
a shared machine connects automatically up to LINK_CAP; an idle non-primary link disconnects after IDLE_DISCONNECT_MS
sessionMachine is per-client in-memory state, never persisted or synced
auto-selecting a freshly created session additionally requires the creating frame to have come from the primary machine

a resumed tab probes every link it holds a socket for (visibilitychange when visible, pageshow with event.persisted, debounced) and redials only one that fails the probe; a link with no socket (idle-disconnected) is left alone so a tab switch cannot defeat IDLE_DISCONNECT_MS

a wake also revives the primary link when it holds no socket, no pending retry and no connect in flight (shouldReviveIdle) — the primary is never idle-disconnected, so that state is a connect that died before creating a socket; non-primary socket-less links stay down per IDLE_DISCONNECT_MS

Web Push (see web-push-notifications) follows the same not-scoped-to-primary rule as maybeAlert: each bridge keeps its own last-seen status per session and pushes for the sessions it hosts, and a device registers its subscription with every owned machine, not only the primary

a double-click on the header switcher toggles to the previously active machine (recorded by rememberDeviceId when the active id changes), only while that machine is still listed and is not the active one; the control shows a count badge, not a dot, for sessions needing the user on other machines
a notification click (page-level or Web Push) routes through openSessionFromAlert, which switches the primary machine (via alertTarget) when the session isn't hosted there before selecting it
architecturalRules: every cross-machine merge/prune/select rule, plus the MachineView projection and sessionsOnMachine, lives in web/src/lib/machines.ts as a plain function, unit-testable without a socket, a store, or React

MachineView's fields are named identically to their global store counterparts, so `...slice.view` is itself the whole projection; the hello reducer and setPrimaryMachine spread the same object rather than hand-listing fields twice, which is what keeps the two from drifting apart
prunableDraftIds/pruneDrafts/pruneDraftAttachments take the ids to delete, not the ids to keep
MachineLink owns every piece of per-socket state that used to be a ws.ts module global; socketGeneration now holds per link
useSessionMachine/useSessionMachineHealth must be wrapped in useShallow or zustand v5 re-renders without end on their freshly built return object
web/src/lib/machines.ts is imported directly by a server/-side test file so it can run under node:test without a browser

lifecycle listeners (visibilitychange, pageshow[persisted]) are registered exactly once, from wireConnectivity() in ws.ts, never from a component effect; the wake probe judges liveness against its own stamp (awaitingProbeSince) and its own timeout, never PONG_TIMEOUT_MS, so the heartbeat's stall-forgiveness (re-baselining lastPongAt on a late tick) cannot extend it

MachineSwitcher renders only when SHARING_ENABLED (a local build has one machine and no grants); it replaces the header's brand/tabs separator dot on desktop (icon-only, no machine name, so it does not compete with the project tab ScrollArea for width) and is the same icon-only control on a phone, placed beside the burger instead of the dropped brand/tabs separator

features.name: Transcript live-update performance
features.purpose: Why a live turn or a session switch used to freeze the UI for a beat, and the three independent fixes: batching WebSocket transcript events into one render per frame, keeping rebuilt transcript items referentially stable so memoization and diff caches survive a rebuild, and windowing a long transcript's initial mount. A fourth fix: gate the initial loadTranscript send and its reconnect retry on link health, and show a reasoned loading state instead of the plain empty-state copy while it's outstanding. A fifth: page the transcript load (tail first, then byte-bounded background backfill of older history) so the first paint no longer waits on the whole file.
businessRules: a live turn's transcript renders at most once per animation frame, not once per WebSocket event

a hidden tab accumulates its transcript backlog without rendering at all (no animation frames fire while hidden) and commits it as a single render on refocus, rather than replaying the whole backlog as N sequential renders

a long session's initial mount renders only its last ~40 top-level items; the rest backfill on idle, or immediately on scrolling near the top, with a 'Show earlier messages' button as the always-available affordance
windowing applies to workflow sessions too; the progress bar and stepper jump-to-step both stay correct against a clipped list (see transcript-rendering.md and workflow-step-lifecycle.md)
loadTranscript is re-sent on every reconnect (gated on health.connected, not merely !loaded), since a send while the link is down is dropped rather than queued
the loading placeholder only replaces the transcript when nothing is cached to show (!loaded && !events?.length); a reconnect reload with cached events keeps the transcript on screen
the loading reason's precedence is link, then bridge attachment, then worker health, matching the machine-health banners' own order

a transcript load is paged: the tail page paints first and older history backfills in the background, one byte-bounded page in flight at a time, on every device, until the cache reaches transcriptFloor
a loadTranscript with no page still returns the whole file and a transcript reply with no page is complete, so old clients and old bridges keep working with no version-skew error path
a tail page whose prevSeq is newer than the last cached seq replaces the disjoint cache instead of leaving a hole
a page is aligned back to a user event, but extension stops at 4x PAGE_BYTES so one huge turn cannot defeat paging
architecturalRules: contract: nothing outside applyServerMessage may read `transcripts`/`lastEventAt` and assume it's settled — every non-'event' message flushes the pending buffer first (flushPendingEvents at the top of applyServerMessage), so a new message handler that reads transcripts without going through applyServerMessage's switch breaks this silently

case 'event' only pushes into a per-session pending buffer and schedules a flush via requestAnimationFrame; it performs no `set()` itself — the buffer, the scheduled-flush handle, and flushPendingEvents all live inside the store's `create` closure since they close over `set`

the buffer's flush replicates the prior per-event dedupe (one Set<seq> per session per flush, built once instead of a linear scan per event) and the prior 'a complete SDK message supersedes the stream deltas that built up to it' rule, applied once over the whole batch at its last complete message's index rather than once per event — this must keep producing the same resulting array the old per-event path would have, since it's the only place that rule is expressed

a setTimeout fallback for the flush arms only when requestAnimationFrame is unavailable; it must never arm merely because the tab is hidden, since a hidden-tab timer firing would defeat the backlog-until-refocus behavior that's the point of batching on rAF in the first place

reconcileItems (transcript.ts) is what makes a rebuild cheap for React, not buildTranscript itself — buildTranscript's own cost was measured at 3-5ms even on a 5540-event/14MB real session, so it was never the dominant cost of a session switch; see transcript-rendering.md's reconcileItems rule for the exhaustive list of fields it must compare

the tail window and the markdown highlight deferral (Markdown.tsx) are the two changes that actually addressed the measured session-switch cost — a 278-row folded session can hold ~90 full Markdown documents, each a synchronous remark/rehype/rehype-highlight parse, all committed in one pass on ErrorBoundary remount (App.tsx keys SessionView by selectedSessionId); windowing bounds how many of those mount at once, and the highlight deferral cuts the cost of each one that does

the sidebar's own re-render cost (SessionRow memoization, archived-session pagination — session-and-project-ui.md) is a second, independent contributor to 'switching sessions feels slow' that has nothing to do with the size of the session being switched to — it re-rendered every row on every selection change regardless

pageTranscript lives in its own pure module because index.ts listens on import; the backfill driver lives in SessionView and transcriptBackfill.ts rather than the store, since ws.ts already imports the store
the backfill in-flight guard is shared module state keyed by `before`, used by both the background driver and the jump/reveal requestRest fetches so they cannot race

features.name: Session change tracking
features.purpose: A per-session git baseline captured once at creation, per-turn attribution of which changed files belong to this session (mechanism-agnostic, via git snapshot windows), and a read-only review UI that lists every changed file and diffs it on demand, without routing diff content through a model.
businessRules: one baseline per session, captured once at creation, never recaptured or overwritten
baseline resolution order is session baseline, then workflow baseline, then a synthesized HEAD flagged synthetic
a pruned snapshot ref falls back to HEAD and is flagged stale rather than silently rendering as no changes
a path is ambiguous only when every source that saw it is an overlapped turn window; a direct tool_use claim always wins
sessionDiff/sessionDiffFile require the session itself to be inside the connection's grant, not just the readFiles capability
no MAX_DIFF_CHARS-style cap applies on this path, since nothing here reaches a model
workflow {diff} behavior is unchanged: WorkflowState.diffBaselines is still written and read exactly as before
architecturalRules: diff assembly (baseline resolution, attribution, bucketing) lives on SessionManager, not in fileRoutes.ts, which stays a thin permission clamp
git.ts stays pure git with no prompt formatting; parseNameStatus/parseNumstat are exported pure functions
per-turn attribution is a transcript event ('files-changed'), never a SessionMeta field, and is deliberately never rendered as a transcript card
handleFileRequest and its ROUTES map are async; every pre-existing handler still resolves synchronously

features.name: Session rewind
features.purpose: Recover a session whose context overflowed mid-conversation by truncating its transcript from a chosen sent message on, re-pointing the CLI conversation at the truncated history in place (SDK forkSession), and either discarding that message or handing its text back to the composer to edit and resend.
businessRules: truncate-in-place only: no branching, no alternate-history tree; the discarded tail is recoverable only by hand from the sidecar file
never auto-resubmits; Edit only prefills the composer, the user must send it themselves
a started workflow does not block a rewind — rollbackToTranscript keeps WorkflowState in sync with whatever the truncated transcript still shows
cumulative session spend and per-step spend are deliberately not rewound — that money was really spent
Edit reloads attachments from disk only when edit: true was requested; a plain Delete never pays that read

the confirm dialog states plainly what is lost: the message is deleted either way (only Edit keeps its text, in the composer, not the transcript), everything after it is deleted too, and it is irreversible with no refund; a first-prompt rewind with no anchor also says Claude's memory of the session is cleared completely; a started workflow names the step it parks back on
Copy of the message's own text is never gated by rewindBlock

rewinding above a provider switch restores the model and, when the switch recorded its abandoned resume pointer (ProviderSwitchData.fromSessionId), forks and resumes that conversation for real; a switch recorded before that field existed degrades to the right model with a fresh conversation, never the wrong model with a stale pointer
architecturalRules: fork-then-truncate ordering: forkSession is awaited eagerly inside rewindSession, before any local mutation, so a fork failure leaves Lines' own transcript untouched
rewindSession broadcasts transcriptTruncated itself rather than the index.ts WS handler, so it is ordered before any event a rewind listener emits while settling (e.g. a workflow park marker)

RewindListener mirrors TurnCompleteListener's shape — one optional hook SessionManager calls, registered once by WorkflowEngine's constructor — rather than adding a SessionManager -> WorkflowEngine dependency edge
store.truncateTranscript invalidates the transcript cache rather than trimming the cached entry in place, since entry.lines/entry.parsed are handed to live readers by reference

the dropped tail is archived to a transcripts/<sessionId>.rewind-<ts>.jsonl sidecar before the live file is rewritten (archive-then-truncate); no read path or cleanup job consumes these files, and they accumulate with repeated rewinds
the rewinding in-flight claim is taken synchronously before rewindSession's first await, mirroring the compacting guard
RewindPrompt's attachment rehydration reuses SessionManager.reloadAttachments, extracted out of lastPromptForRetry so both paths reload identically

the rewind target's era (model + resume pointer) is resolved from the transcript's provider-switch markers before any anchor scan runs; both the Claude-uuid and codex-turn-id scans are bounded below by the era's floor so an anchor is never borrowed from a conversation the fork target has never seen

features.name: Background tasks
features.purpose: Track live SDK background tasks (a backgrounded subagent or Bash command) per session as server-side state, exempt a session that owns one from idle-query recycling (previously a silent data-loss bug), and surface them as state on the tool card that launched them (falling back to a standalone transcript row only for a genuine orphan) plus a composer Stop path distinct from interrupt, a live strip, and a sidebar row.
businessRules: the live set is never restored from a persisted SessionMeta.backgroundTasks on load — a background task belongs to a specific CLI process, and a value surviving a restart in sessions.json describes a process nothing here has a handle on any more

background_tasks_changed is the only thing that may put an id into the live set (strengthened from “is the only writer”); everything else — init, closeQuery, handleWorkerEnded, resetClaudeSession, task_notification, and stopBackgroundTasks — may only take ids out, so membership is monotone toward empty between level emissions. A missed bookend now fails as a premature empty (self-corrected by the next level emission) instead of a permanent non-empty (observed wedged for 661 events in one real session, clearable only by a CLI restart)

a background-task-only system event (background_tasks_changed, task_notification, task_progress, task_updated) never heals a stale session status back to 'running' in handleWorkerEvent — those events outlive the turn that started them, so treating one as proof a turn is live on a session that had already settled wedged the status permanently (no second result was ever coming), which also made the session wrongly read as interruptible for recycleIdleQueries and reconcileWithWorker
a settled session that still owns a live background task is never recycled by recycleIdleQueries — closing its query would kill the CLI child and the task with it, silently

stopBackgroundTasks(sessionId, taskId?) stops one task, or each live task when no id is given, and then removes the stopped ids from the set itself, optimistically — the user's manual escape hatch for a task the CLI has already forgotten (previously it deliberately left the set alone; a still-alive task now just flickers back on the next background_tasks_changed, which is accepted as better than an unrecoverable wedge)
a result arriving while background tasks are still live still settles the turn normally (done/error) — the turn lifecycle is unaffected by background work outside it
a queued prompt can still flush into a session while a background task runs — the CLI handles a new foreground turn concurrently with a background one
the composer's Send action is never blocked by a live background task; only Stop's target message (interrupt vs stopBackgroundTasks) changes based on whether a turn is also live
the sidebar's background-work row is not actionable and is checked after waiting-permission and the interrupted-turn state, both of which do need the user
the finish chime/notification is suppressed while backgroundTasks is non-empty; it fires normally for the eventual notification turn once the set has emptied

a task that vanishes silently (no task_notification, no further background_tasks_changed naming it) is not self-healing under this invariant — the user still needs to click Stop; fully self-healing that needs per-task timestamps plus a timer, out of scope here

an event proving a main-thread turn (assistant, stream_event, non-replay user, no subagent parent) on a settled session with no bridge-started turn does heal the status to running and re-opens a parked workflow step — unlike the background-task-only system events above
architecturalRules: SessionStatus is deliberately not overloaded to represent background work — a separate SessionMeta field keeps the turn lifecycle (workflow advance, queue flush, turn-complete accounting) byte-identical
BackgroundTaskInfo[] is a record, not a bare count, since the SDK's level payload already names every live task; one field so the two can never drift
all writers of LiveState.backgroundTasks go through the single private setBackgroundTasks helper, which owns the compare-then-upsert — no call site broadcasts on its own
adding stopTask to BridgeToWorker is a protocol bump (v4 -> v5), unlike an added field on an existing message, which is safely ignorable by an old worker
worker.ts stays thin: it records the background_tasks_changed/init payload and forwards it in hello, but does not interpret it, the same convention busy already follows
the transcript's openTasks map is keyed by taskId rather than a single slot like openCompact, because background tasks can overlap

run_in_background is absent from every real backgrounded call's input observed in practice, so the taskFlags clock-icon flag is fed from ToolBlock.background at the TaskHeader call site instead of from parseTaskInput's own input.run_in_background alone

task_progress/task_updated/thinking_tokens/status(no compact verdict)/hook_started/hook_response system events are broadcast but no longer written to the transcript file (EPHEMERAL_SYSTEM_SUBTYPES in server/src/sessions.ts) — roughly half of every transcript file's lines, and nothing reads them back on reload

features.name: Turn interjection
features.purpose: Release a queued prompt into the turn that is already running ("Send now") instead of waiting for it to settle, using the SDK's undocumented priority steering knob.
businessRules: sending happens from the queue row, never from the composer — typing while busy still queues
an interjection never opens a turn and is never a rewind anchor
it runs attributed to the item's author, not whoever pressed the button
a promptNeedsApproval guest cannot release their own item
items with attachments are refused in v1
refused during compaction, interrupt, rewind, workflow advance, or a closed link, leaving the item queued to flush normally
releasing one item never releases the rest of the queue, and never clears queuePaused unless the queue empties
interjected work bills to the original turn's result, so a step's cost includes it
no MIN_INTERJECT_VERSION: priority 'next' and an absent priority measured identically
architecturalRules: separate TranscriptEvent kind ('interject') rather than a flag on 'user', so every turn-boundary scan keyed on kind === 'user' stays correct untouched
the push reuses the queryTokens entry instead of re-resolving a token, because pushWithToken closes the query on a mismatch
no new SessionStatus value and no new SessionMeta field
priority rides inside the opaque push.message, so worker.ts and PROTOCOL_VERSION are untouched
the {ok:false, code} union mirrors compactContext so a lost race reads as 'still queued', not as an error
the CLI behaviour and the priority:'next' choice come from a measurement (server/scripts/spike-interject.ts), not an inference from the SDK's types

features.name: Quick file open (Cmd+P)
features.purpose: Jump to any project file from anywhere in the app via Cmd/Ctrl+P, reusing the @mention file ranker in a floating palette.
businessRules: Cmd+P searches only the active project's roots (rootsForCwd), not every open project tab
a hit always opens in the preview overlay, never a files-mode tab, regardless of which sidebar mode is active when the palette opens
a .md/.markdown hit or tree open renders in Preview with a Preview/Raw header toggle; other files and .mdx open in Monaco with no toggle, and the mode is not persisted

a .html/.htm file opens in Preview with the same toggle (.xhtml stays source); the preview runs scripts in an opaque-origin sandbox and can load network assets, relative assets and links do not resolve, and if the shell does not answer within ~3s a hint says to update or use Raw
the preview shows the file tree only for a file inside an open project's root that is not HTML; a file outside every root, or any .html/.htm file, fills the whole preview
relative links in the rendered file resolve against its own directory and open in the same preview; relative images are not resolved

the preview is editable on your own machine (Raw/Monaco only, guests read-only): Cmd/Ctrl+S or Save, no autosave; closing the preview or opening another file asks before discarding, and the tab warns on close or reload while any edit is unsaved

save state shows in the host's header beside its own buttons (dot + 'Unsaved changes', Discard, Save; on a conflict 'Changed on disk', Reload, Overwrite) and a dirty files-mode tab shows a dot; Discard reverts in place so it is one undo away
hideIgnored defaults to on and is local-only (not part of synced settings)
non-ignored files fill the capped candidate list before ignored ones, so a large gitignored tree cannot starve the palette or find-in-files
architecturalRules: the palette is a global overlay mounted in App.tsx alongside MonacoPreviewModal/LoginModal, not scoped under any route, so the shortcut works from the docs reader too
hideIgnored is a single store field read by both surfaces (palette, sidebar tree) rather than two independent toggles

save controls are portalled into the host's header via FileActionsSlot, never stacked over the editor: the editor subtree keeps one shape, since wrapping it on the first edit remounts Monaco and drops focus mid-keystroke; Monaco stays uncontrolled after mount and Discard edits it in place

the HTML reaches the preview frame by postMessage from the web app (read via the file route), never uploaded; /html-preview.html is the only route with a permissive CSP, safe because the CSP sandbox directive gives an opaque origin, and the iframe sandbox must never gain allow-same-origin, allow-top-navigation or allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox

features.name: MCP connections
features.purpose: Add a third-party MCP server from Settings, see its live per-session connection status, and authorize it via OAuth without needing a running turn — synced across machines like the guard allowlist, with credential values (HTTP header values, stdio env values) that never leave the machine that holds them: only their names travel.
entryPoints: server/src/sessions.ts applyMcpServers (a connection edit reaching live queries)
businessRules: header and stdio env values never sync and never reach a browser; only headerKeys/envKeys (names) travel on the wire, values stay in the local mcp-secrets.json and mcp-env.json (0600); a synced connection arrives without them until entered on that machine

env values are write-only in the UI like header values: a saved one shows as an empty box that says it is saved, an empty box on save keeps the stored value, removing a variable drops its value, and a name normalizeConnection would skip is refused in the form (isMcpEnvName) rather than lost
envValuesHeld (which envKeys this machine holds a value for) is set only on what the bridge sends its own browsers, never in the synced blob, and never taken from a client or a remote row
accepting a remote list never takes a credential value from it, and a values-only difference is not a divergence (sameConnection compares env names)

storage keeps names only: PUT /mcp-connections drops header and env values whatever a bridge sends (answered as usual, not 400, so an older bridge keeps syncing) and GET serves a values-free copy of any row still holding them
every MCP file (connections, sync, secrets, env) is written 0600 and tightened to 0600 at startup
scrubbing storage is not un-leaking: an API key synced in a stdio connection's env before names-only sync should be rotated
the Lines in-process server always wins a name collision in the worker's mcpServers merge; a connection named 'lines' is refused at validation (reserved-name)
a remote connection list is never applied automatically; a divergence is always shown as an explicit added/removed diff
divergence detection is a set difference over full connection content (ids included), never an updatedAt comparison
push to storage is suppressed while a review is pending
a disabled connection is kept but contributes nothing to serverConfigs() — no session sees its tools while it's off
alwaysLoad is left unset on every generated server config, so a connection's tools defer behind tool search by default
only mode: 'url' elicitations render a card; mode: 'form' is declined without ever reaching the user
an elicitation whose query has already died resolves 'expired' with no injected model prompt
authorizing a server, editing/removing a connection, and reading MCP status are all owner-only, permanently
OAuth's redirect URI is always http://127.0.0.1:<bridge's bound port>/mcp-oauth/callback, so authorizing only works from a browser on the same machine as the bridge
the OAuth callback route's state parameter is the only credential on it: single-use, TTL-bounded, timingSafeEqual-compared; a provider response with no state is refused outright
a dead session's pending OAuth handshakes are forgotten on worker onEnded, since the PKCE verifier died with that CLI process

review() re-sanitizes the pending list (via sanitizeConnections) on every call and recomputes the diff off that sanitized list, rather than trusting what reviewRemote staged — the pending blob round-trips through mcp-connections-sync.json, which loadMcpSync validates only on updatedAt
architecturalRules: validators live in shared/types.ts so the web client runs the exact same rules before sending a connection to the bridge
connection edits are intent messages (add/update/remove/review), never a whole-list save
the connection list is not part of UserUiSettings/pushSettings() — server-authoritative, security-relevant state stays out of the whole-blob save
mergeMcpServers lives in server/src/workerProtocol.ts (not worker.ts) so it is importable and testable without a live query

MCP_AUTH_METHODS/mcpAuthSupport/McpAuthApi are defined once in workerProtocol.ts (the worker's one importable local module) and re-exported by mcpAuth.ts, so the canary test and the call site cannot disagree

Query.mcpAuthenticate/mcpSubmitOAuthCallbackUrl exist in the SDK's runtime bundle but not in sdk.d.ts; every call goes through mcpAuthSupport(q), and mcpAuth.contract.test.ts fails in both directions on an SDK upgrade (methods gone from the runtime, or methods appearing in the typings)
adding a params field to the ask BridgeToWorker message, and adding new AskMethod values, are not protocol bumps — an older worker that doesn't read/implement them falls through to its default case

McpConnections is a structural copy of GuardAllowlist (server/src/autoGuard.ts): same file split plus two local-only credential files (mcp-secrets.json for header values, mcp-env.json for stdio env values — its own file because an older build reads the secrets file's shape directly), same review lifecycle, same onChange/onReview wiring

names-only is enforced at the validator: normalizeConnection reduces any env map to envKeys, so every shape built from canonical rows is value-free by construction; blob() is built from those rows, never from list(), so one machine's envValuesHeld cannot reach another

withoutMcpValues runs on both sides of the storage boundary: outbound before req signs, so the signature verifies after storage's own filtering; inbound after verification, so a legacy row hands this machine names only; a row the migration scrubbed fails verification and is replaced by the bridge's own names-only push

the load migration moves inline env values into mcp-env.json before rewriting the connections file without them, and skips that rewrite if the move did not land, so a failed write costs a retry, never the key
findPermissionRequest's request-vs-resolution predicate is toolName || elicitation, not toolName alone, since an elicitation request legitimately carries no tool name
the OAuth callback route is added to the bridge's existing bare http.createServer via a path-prefix check, not a new server or port, since the redirect URI has to be a fixed, publishable value

features.name: Settings → Updates pane
features.purpose: Show the version of every moving part (web, bridge, worker, desktop app, Claude Code CLI) in one place in Settings, with a permanent desktop download link.
businessRules: versions shown are web, bridge, worker, desktop app, and Claude CLI only

the desktop row's badge and button variant come solely from updateStatus.state === 'available' (the desktop shell's own feed verdict) — no client-side version-string comparison exists anywhere in the pane

the download button always renders whenever a desktop build has been published, regardless of update state — being current does not hide it, only DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_ENABLED being false hides the whole row

the download action is a plain link to DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_URL, the manual path for a shell that cannot install the update itself; once the shell reports ready the row offers Restart to update (installUpdate), disabled while restartBlocked, which the bridge re-sends as sessions start and finish
an unknown version renders as a dimmed em dash rather than an omitted row, so the pane's shape never changes
hello.claudeCli never carries the CLI binary's absolute path — publicClaudeCliStatus builds the wire object field by field rather than spreading the bridge-local status
hello.claudeCli and the worker's hello.appVersion are both optional, so neither bumps a protocol version

both CLI probes are self-healing: a working answer is cached for the process lifetime, but a missing/outdated verdict is only trusted for RETRY_FAILED_AFTER_MS (10s); the bridge re-probes on a 15s interval and broadcasts a 'cliStatus' message to every context only when the combined answer actually changes, so installing a CLI clears the pane and the model picker without a restart
architecturalRules: ClaudeCliState/ClaudeCliStatus are declared in shared/types.ts and re-exported from server/src/claudeCli.ts, so the browser can read the shape without importing server code
the worker's appVersion is a package version, distinct from the protocol version already on its hello — the worker outlives bridge restarts, so the two can legitimately differ
__LINES_VERSION__ for the web bundle mirrors the existing bridge/worker/desktop-shell define idiom rather than introducing a VITE_ env var
CodexCliState/CodexCliStatus follow ClaudeCliStatus's precedent exactly: declared in shared/types.ts, re-exported from server/src/codexCli.ts, path stripped before hello/cliStatus

features.name: Manual reasoning-effort selection
features.purpose: Let a user or workflow step pick how hard a model thinks, not just which model runs: a control beside the model picker in the composer, on a workflow step, as a new-session default, and as a global effort for plan-mode turns specifically.
businessRules: absent means the provider's own default everywhere; never a sentinel and never null on the wire for Claude — codex alone still receives an explicit null when nothing is chosen, meaning 'ask codex for its own preset', not 'the user chose nothing', and a user-chosen value must never itself be sent as null
no 'minimal': measured directly against a live codex app-server, a turn sent with it fails outright even though OpenAI's own config reference lists it, so both providers' offered lists are low..max

plan mode has its own global effort (UserUiSettings.planReasoningEffort), mirroring codex's own plan_mode_reasoning_effort config key, overriding the session's own effort only while that session is in plan mode
a workflow step's effort is absolute, not additive: a step with none clears the session back to the provider default rather than inheriting the previous step's
no cross-provider refusal: unlike setModel, changing effort never strands a conversation
a stored effort the session's current provider does not offer is dropped at push time rather than sent, reachable via a pre-first-turn provider switch
effect lands on the next turn, never the running one
A per-run override's effort is absolute: null means Auto even when the step sets an effort, and an absent field uses the step's value.
architecturalRules: the worker's ensureSession returns an already-live query early and discards the options of every later push, so an effort change on a live Claude session marks the query stale (SessionManager.staleQueries) rather than editing options in place; pushWithToken drops it there on the next push, reusing recycleIdleQueries' three exemptions (busy, background tasks, MCP OAuth hold) for free

codex's effort rides collaborationMode.settings.reasoning_effort, which is already built and sent on every turn for plan mode, rather than the typed turn/start.effort field — one code path instead of two dials with no documented precedence

setReasoningEffort reuses the setModel ShareCaps capability rather than minting a new one (effort is strictly weaker than model choice), but stays a distinct ClientMessage since setModel carries a cross-provider refusal verdict effort has no analogue for
effortSelectData is the single entry point every effort Select goes through, mirroring modelSelectData/renderModelOption, and always leads with an explicit 'Auto' row rather than an empty value
workflow steps validate a chosen effort against Anthropic's list only, since a step naming an OpenAI model is already refused outright

features.name: Cross-provider model switching
features.purpose: The deliberate, lossy way past setModel's cross-provider refusal: drop a session's stranded conversation, summarize it with a one-shot helper query, and seed the other provider with the hand-off.
businessRules: the switch is lossy by design: the summary is capped to roughly six bullets under 120 words, and the transcript's provider-switch marker is the only durable signal that everything above it is invisible to the model below, rendering even when the summary failed

providerSwitchBlock does not refuse on a live turn or on a workflow session in any state, unlike rewindBlock -- a live turn is stopped first, and a workflow session's own advancing/advanceOnComplete state is what actually blocks

the switch is one-shot on a workflow session: the next step still runs on the model that step names; providerSwitched only stops that step from parking as an authoring mistake, it does not make the switch sticky for the run

CLI availability on the target provider is checked before anything destructive -- the single highest-severity ordering property in the feature; any later refusal must go above resetClaudeSession, never below it
a guest whose prompts need approval is refused outright, since the seed prompt bypasses that staging entirely
architecturalRules: setModel's refusal stays strict and untouched; switchProvider is a second, more deliberate entry point rather than a flag that loosens the first one
helper queries run in an empty scratch directory, never the session's cwd, so a project's auto-memory or AGENTS.md cannot leak into a narrow summary
switchingProvider is claimed before the stop, not merely before the summary, and folded into isBusy/canInterject/maybeFlush alongside the existing rewinding/compacting guards
forkCodex takes an optional explicit threadId, used only when a rewind crosses back into a codex era the worker holds no live binding for

features.name: End-to-end encryption
features.purpose: Make the hosted server untrusted: a browser and a machine agree on keys out of band and authenticate each other directly, so the relay carries ciphertext it can neither read nor forge, and storage holds blobs it cannot author. On by default: every relayed channel must authenticate from a machine's first launch — an owner's against a pinned key, a guest's against the key in their invite link plus a grant the machine minted — and sync refuses unsigned blobs or holds unsigned items back for review.
businessRules: every relayed owner channel must authenticate from a machine's first launch, enrolled device or not — there is no plaintext owner path; before enrolling, the only thing a channel can do is enrol

that requirement is machine-wide, never per-device: per-device is no protection, because an attacker simply declines to enrol and takes the unencrypted path; every browser enrols once (the desktop's own window automatically, others via EnrollGate with a tray or CLI code)
an enrollment code is single-use, expires in 15 minutes, and minting a new one invalidates the outstanding one
20 characters of a 32-symbol alphabet is 100 bits, which is what makes a typed code safe against an attacker who can watch the exchange; a short code would need a PAKE, which is deliberately not here
the browser's private key is non-extractable in IndexedDB — a later XSS can use it but cannot carry it away
no key material is ever uploaded, and the storage schema must not gain a public-key column: a key the server can rewrite is a key an attacker with the database can rewrite
revocation works from the tray and the CLI with no browser, because key pinning plus a lost device would otherwise be unrecoverable

a relayed guest channel is end-to-end encrypted against the machine key its invite link carries and admitted only on a grant this machine minted, presented as the first sealed frame ({type:'guestGrant', tokens}) — never on the relay's word, which now only picks which check applies; a guest channel can never enrol a device

a guest gets the grant this machine issued, narrowed by the relay's attestation — the relay can take access away, never give it; a guest client older than APP_PROTOCOL_VERSION 6 sends plaintext and is refused, and the relay does not put a guest through to a bridge older than 6

signed sync covers the blobs /settings, /guard-allowlist and /mcp-connections, and every workflow, step and recipe per item (each row keeps its own JSON whole in a data column); /memory, /project-keys and sessions carry no signature yet

blob sync is strict by default: unsigned, forged, signer-changed and rolled-back blobs are all refused, and LINES_E2EE_STRICT=0 (recovery only) accepts unsigned ones with a warning; a refusal is re-pushed signed on the same sync pass
blob signing keys are trust-on-first-use then pinned; a changed signer is refused and surfaced, as SSH treats a changed host key

a workflow, step or recipe this machine did not sign is kept and shown, never dropped, and held back from running until reviewed (UntrustedMark: unsigned, forged, unknown-signer, foreign); under LINES_E2EE_STRICT=0 unsigned and forged items still run but keep their mark, so this machine never re-signs them as its own

items get no trust-on-first-use: only this machine's own key is trusted, and another machine only by an explicit trustSigner after the user compares its 64-bit SHA-256 fingerprint (xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx, rendered as an enrolled browser's) with the one that machine shows in Settings → Sync; a fingerprint that is not the key's is refused, and revoking holds back again what only that machine vouched for

approving a held-back item (trustSyncedItem) approves its reviewed digest only — not the machine that signed it, not a later change, not another copy of the same version; a stale digest is refused, and revoking a machine leaves item approvals standing
neither an edit nor a copy clears a mark: an edited held-back item stays held back and a copy carries its original's mark; an edit made here to a trusted machine's item becomes this machine's own

a mark is this bridge's verdict: never pushed, stripped from every pulled row, only ever added by a client message (a copy), and re-decided by settledHold on every load and pull so a decision made under LINES_E2EE_STRICT=0 or before a revoke cannot outlive it
this machine's sync-signing fingerprint and the account's trusted machines are owner-only (hello.syncSigning, the syncSigning broadcast); a guest's view has neither

an enrollment code handed to a page travels in the URL fragment, never a query string, and is consumed and stripped on read — a query string reaches the server, which is the party the code exists to exclude; the query form is still accepted on read only because an older desktop build's QR emitted it

a machine's own desktop window is handed a live code (appUrlForOwnWindow) rather than asked to type one: the shell and the bridge are already the same trust domain, so hand-enrolling the machine against itself was a step with no security value

the connect-time EnrollGate states the exchange as numbered steps, because step one happens on a different device from the one the user is looking at, and it is not a dead end — it also lists the account's other machines and offers pairing a new one
architecturalRules: attested.userId is a routing hint, not an authorization decision — this replaces the former rule that the relay is the auth edge
WebCrypto primitives only (ECDH P-256, HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM, ECDSA P-256): zero dependencies, and non-extractable browser keys
the construction follows Noise IK's shape, written longhand so it is auditable in one file — do not invent a variant; follow Noise IK precisely or get the change externally reviewed
the crypto layer wraps a byte channel, not a WebSocket, so a WebRTC DataChannel can be slotted underneath with no protocol change
guardRelayChannel sits between RelayClient and handleConnection: the bridge's message switch must not grow a crypto branch
