no relay channel is handed over in the constructor: an owner's after its handshake against a pinned key, a guest's after its sealed grant redeems; the deadlock that once forced a plaintext guest's handover there (the bridge speaks first) is gone because a guest's browser now opens with e2eeHello against the invite link's key
one handshake per channel and no enrolment once one has begun — a guest channel takes any client key, so a second e2eeHello would let the relay swap itself in as the admitted guest
SecureChannel serializes inbound frames through one promise chain, so a guest's later frame cannot overtake its grant and an owner's frames cannot reorder past the counter check
handleConnection re-checks the gate: a guest with no grants, or grants for a host other than the one the relay names, is closed 1008; the host a guest reaches is named by the grant
a guest refusal never contains 'end-to-end encrypted channel', the phrase the client keys its owner EnrollGate on

MachineLink.pinned is fixed when the socket opens with a pinned key and never cleared, unlike expectsSecure: a pinned link never sends or applies a plaintext app frame (only the relay's deviceOffline/deviceOnline), and e2eeReady before the link's own handshake finished closes it; the guest grant is written right after e2eeConfirm
plaintextFrameAllowed is a pure function in web/src/lib so the server's test runner can cover it
item signatures bind kind and account (one machine key signs for every account on it, and some items carry no ownerId), sign ownerId, and exclude createdAt (storage injects it) and the local mark

signForPush never signs a marked row (laundering); unsigned/forged rows travel unsigned, another machine's or another user's are not pushed; counters for a batch are reserved in one store write and an unchanged row re-sends its cached signature

ItemTrust (sync-trust.json, per account, 0600, never uploaded) is read on every call rather than cached, because both engines and the command layer hold one; fingerprints are computed on the bridge, never taken from disk or the wire
a refused client reconnects silently (no heartbeat, no auth relay), which is the only window in which enrollment is possible
enrollment re-dials the link by name (reconnectMachine), never the primary: on the connect-time gate the primary is a different machine or unset
base64 inflates payloads ~33%, so broadcast backpressure thresholds were raised by a third; isDroppable still runs pre-serialization

features.name: Mobile client
features.purpose: Drive real sessions from a phone: the existing UI adapted in place with Mantine breakpoints, hover-gated actions made reachable by touch, a bottom-sheet permission prompt, and a push-only service worker for installability and notifications.
businessRules: phone is Mantine's default sm breakpoint (48em); no custom breakpoints were added

the sidebar is a real drawer on a phone and closes when a session is picked or created; createSession also synchronously focuses a hidden keyboard-primer input so iOS keeps its keyboard up across the round-trip to the new session's composer

full-screen modals and bottom sheets never size from 100dvh/--lines-viewport, which is not reliably the screen height in a standalone iOS home-screen app: they size against the fixed Mantine overlay inner (the screen) and pad by env(safe-area-inset-*); the full-screen modal rule is global, not phone-only, so an iPad home-screen app gets it too
sidebar width is clamped against the viewport on every read, so a width saved on a large display cannot cover a 390px screen
on a coarse pointer, hover-revealed actions are shown outright — they were unreachable on touch, and inline styles beat any CSS override
dismissing the permission sheet denies: a swipe is a decision, and the safe reading is no
the file browser, workflow editor and diff modals are deferred behind BestOnDesktop; the file palette is simply absent, since its only entry point is a keyboard shortcut

installable with a push-only service worker (web/public/sw.js, no fetch handler and no cache) — see web-push-notifications; offline caching buys nothing for a live WebSocket client, and an SW-cached bundle against a newer bridge would trip the skew path in the one case a reload cannot fix

no full-height surface uses 100vh: on a phone vh is the large viewport (measured as if the browser toolbars were hidden), so a 100vh shell puts the composer under Safari's toolbar — everything uses --lines-viewport, which is dvh-based like Mantine's own AppShell

the shell subtracts the on-screen keyboard too: iOS shrinks only the visual viewport, so dvh does not move and the composer ends up under the keyboard; trackKeyboardInset measures the difference from visualViewport and publishes --lines-keyboard, while Chrome's interactive-widget=resizes-content shrinks the layout viewport so the same measurement reads ~0 and the two never stack

inputs are 16px on a phone because iOS Safari zooms the page in on focus below that and does not zoom back out on blur, leaving the app permanently magnified; Mantine's default is 14px so every field tripped it

the header's trailing controls fold into the Clerk account menu on a phone (or one overflow menu, for a build with no Clerk key), and the brand mark is dropped, since burger + brand + tabs + five controls exceed 390px and the tabs are what gets squeezed out; the machine switcher moves beside the burger instead of dropping out

icon-only controls get a 32px floor on a phone from a rule on .mantine-ActionIcon-root; a 44px minimum across buttons, menu items, inputs and segments was tried and made every control shout, and Mantine's own sizes already clear 32px for anything with a label
the composer's text is 15px, and 16px on iOS where the zoom rule applies — @supports (-webkit-touch-callout: none) is the platform test, so Chrome on iOS keeps the floor too
a bottom sheet is sized by its content (size="auto"), never by a share of the screen: a sheet pinned at 80dvh is the same height whether it holds four controls or one

the composer's permission mode is its own Menu on the row (SEGMENT_MODES, same three modes and order as the desktop pills), separate from the Options icon button; the Options sheet no longer carries the mode control

the phone project-picker button is sized and left-aligned to its own label instead of stretching to fill the header, and the composer has no corner radius or left/right/bottom border on a phone, so it reads as a strip spanning the screen

a bottom sheet's top clearance is padding on .lines-mobile-sheet-inner (--lines-safe-top plus a gap), not a content max-height, so its title and close button clear the Dynamic Island; a full-screen modal's content is the fixed inner minus --lines-keyboard with the bottom inset as padding (dropped while the keyboard is up) and its header padded by --lines-safe-top, with no inline height or header padding-top on a phone; PermissionPrompt's sheet carries .lines-mobile-sheet and .lines-mobile-sheet-inner

the transcript ScrollArea sets scrollbars="y" and styles.content.display="block": Mantine's default display:table content wrapper grows to its widest non-shrinking child, which let one nowrap row widen the whole scroll column past 390px

the desktop-update pill (UpdateBanner) shows on a phone only for a staged (ready) update, compact (Update ready · Restart); an available update, whose only action is the macOS download link, stays hidden there
architecturalRules: adapt in place, never fork a mobile shell: a second transcript renderer either is the same code or drifts and re-loses the batching, windowing and referential-stability work
PermissionPrompt's phone branch is presentation only — one component, one approval path, because two answers to 'may this run?' is a security bug rather than a layout one
Transcript.tsx takes layout props only
lib/layout.ts and lib/pointer.ts stay separate: a node:test imports the pure rule, so it must never reach matchMedia
a fixed width above a leaf icon becomes maw / min(Npx, 100vw - 2rem)

a phone-only branch that owns state mounts that state above the branch — HeaderActions is one component rather than three because a settings modal rendered inside the overflow menu is unmounted by the very click that opens it

features.name: Voice input
features.purpose: Dictate into the composer via a local whisper.cpp transcriber on the bridge, so audio never leaves the machine hosting the session and the provider only ever sees text.
businessRules: transcribe needs the prompt capability, not a session grant — dictating is exactly as privileged as typing
installWhisperModel is owner-only, permanently — it writes into the host's app data folder
an English-only model is always run with -l en and never asked to translate, regardless of the language or translate flag requested
a named non-English language (or translate) with only the English-only model installed is refused rather than silently mistranscribed
one transcription and one model download run at a time per bridge
recordings longer than VOICE_MAX_SECONDS (90s) auto-stop and are transcribed as caught
Send while recording or transcribing finishes the recording and sends once the transcript is spliced in; a failed or empty transcription sends nothing and leaves the prompt as it was

dictation in a card field (an Other… answer, a plan-comment note) only fills or appends text; it never picks, advances, saves or submits, shows only with the prompt capability, and ends when its field closes
only one Other… answer records at a time; the other questions' mics are disabled
a model download is refused while LINES_WHISPER_MODEL pins a single external model file

an iOS home-screen app re-prompts for the mic on every recording (WebKit drops the grant once tracks stop, no per-site setting); the stream is not held open between recordings because that keeps the mic indicator lit
architecturalRules: one useVoiceDictation serves every mic; the composer and the cards differ only in what onText does with the transcript
voice input is not a ProviderCapabilities field — the prompt reaches either provider as plain text either way
insertAtCaret is the one place text is spliced into a MentionValue and its ranges remapped; mention completion and voice insertion both call it
the model a recording uses is decided twice by the same rule (pickWhisperModel server-side, whisperModelFor shared) rather than the client asking the bridge
a downloaded model is only renamed into place after its byte count matches the announced content-length and its header carries ggml's magic number
relatedDecisions: local whisper.cpp over a hosted STT API: private, no API key, same code path on browser, phone and desktop
the dictation language decides the model rather than offering a model picker
auto-download deferred no further than the model: the binary is bundled on desktop but still a manual brew install elsewhere

features.name: Smart turn routing (JEV)
features.purpose: Before each turn, optionally ask TypeSafe's JEV classifier which of an allowed set of models and reasoning efforts that turn should run on, per a plain-language rule; off by default, applied silently in auto mode, or held for the user to accept/decline in ask mode. A workflow step's own rule overrides the global one while it runs.
businessRules: the TypeSafe key is per user and local-only: stored in typesafe-key.json (0600), never synced, never echoed or logged; env TYPESAFE_API_KEY is no longer read; set/clear are owner-only
off never calls JEV, and off is the default: no session is routed and no prompt text leaves the bridge until a user opts in
plan mode is never routed — the global plan-mode effort keeps winning
a routing rule never crosses providers: every model in RoutingRule.models must be on the rule's own provider, or the rule is treated as absent
model and effort picks are gated independently by their own confidence, so one can apply while the other is skipped
a pick equal to the session's current setting is a no-op: no query recycle, no lastRouting update
a manual model or effort change pauses routing for that session until the composer badge resumes it or the next workflow step starts
a step's own routing rule overrides the global rule for its provider while that step runs
no LLM fallback: no stored key, non-2xx, malformed body or timeout all leave the turn on its current settings
only the turn's own prompt text (capped) plus a few plain-line signals are sent to JEV — never the transcript, never tool output
architecturalRules: the hook lives in SessionManager.pushTurn, the single async point every turn passes through, after the intoLiveTurn early return and before the codex branch and pushWithToken
the step rule reaches SessionManager through an injected StepRoutingProvider callback registered by WorkflowEngine, the same injection style as TurnCompleteListener
heldTurns is bridge-memory only; a restart loses it and boot reconcile clears the matching routingSuggestion
a held turn's release goes back through pushTurn, not straight to pushWithToken, so the CLI check and token refresh run fresh
routing's own setModel/setReasoningEffort calls never set routingPaused — the pause is set only from the client-message handler path
server/src/jev.ts only calls the official TypeSafe endpoint, hardcoded as a source constant rather than read from env
sameContent (workflow versioning) compares routing via a stable key-sorted JSON serialization

features.name: Web Push notifications
features.purpose: Alert the user about a session (done/needs permission/needs approval) while the mobile client is backgrounded or closed, using Web Push so the bridge — not the suspended page — wakes a push-only service worker to show the notification.
businessRules: subscriptions are bridge-local, stored per user in push-subscriptions.json (mode 0600), and never synced

the device mints its own VAPID keypair with WebCrypto and keeps it in localStorage, since one browser subscription is tied to one application-server key and every bridge the device registers with has to sign with that same key

registerPush/unregisterPush need { needs: 'owner' }: a guest's narrowed access would otherwise be bypassed by a subscription covering the whole machine, and the bridge also POSTs to whatever endpoint the client supplies
the bridge accepts only https: endpoints on fcm.googleapis.com or hosts ending in .push.apple.com, .push.services.mozilla.com, or .notify.windows.com — an SSRF guard on that POST
not scoped to the primary machine, like maybeAlert: a device registers with every owned machine, and each bridge pushes for the sessions it hosts
no push for a session adopted from sync (adoptSynced), since that broadcast means the session ran elsewhere and was just reset to idle here

no alert between workflow steps: isAlertTransition is false for a done whose workflow is started, whose current step still reads running, and which is not the last step — an advance follows silently and a park re-alerts as waiting-approval; see workflow-step-lifecycle
a push and an in-page alert for the same session share tag: sessionId, so they collapse into one notification on a device that would otherwise get both
the owner hello carries pushAvailable: true; the client only sends registerPush to a machine that said so, so an older bridge is never asked to handle an unknown message type
push only reaches iOS/iPadOS from the home-screen app (display-mode: standalone), iOS 16.4+, with the permission prompt triggered by a tap; Settings shows an Add to Home Screen hint otherwise
sw.js's push handler always calls showNotification, even on unparseable payload data, because iOS may revoke a subscription that receives a push with no visible notification
a bridge restart's in-memory last-seen-status map starts empty, so a session that settles immediately after restart does not push — accepted, to avoid a duplicate push on the next real transition
architecturalRules: sw.js handles only push and notificationclick — no fetch handler, no cache — which is what keeps the pre-existing no-service-worker reasoning intact: with no fetch handler a worker can never serve a stale bundle against a newer bridge

PushNotifier is modeled on SpendHistory: one instance per UserContext, backed by a single JSON file loaded at construction and rewritten on change, with the sender function injected so tests never touch the network
the alert transition rule (isAlertTransition/alertBody/ALERT_STATUSES) lives once in shared/types.ts, and both the page's maybeAlert and the bridge's PushNotifier call it

alertTarget is a plain function in web/src/lib/machines.ts, imported directly by server/src/machineMerge.test.ts under node:test, the same pattern every other multi-machine merge/prune/select rule in that file follows

notify() prefers registration.showNotification when a service worker is registered and falls back to the page-level Notification constructor only when there is none, including inside the desktop Electron window, whose service-worker notification support is unverified

features.name: Landing page
features.purpose: Provider-neutral marketing page (signed-out in the app, and a standalone static build on the apex): a hero cycling through the supported coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) that leads with the Mac download beside Get started, with a self-hosted demo loop, then illustrated sections for how it works, features, security, where your data goes, ways to run it and getting started, in the app's monochrome theme.
businessRules: the landing page paints immediately, never behind the boot splash: index.html loads web/public/splash-guard.js (a file, since the deployed CSP allows no inline script), which hides the splash before first paint for landing routes and signed-out visitors, and the root route renders LandingPage directly while Clerk is still loading for a guest, at the same tree position it keeps once signed out, so it does not remount
generic claims say coding agent or list providers; strings that are truly provider-specific (Claude CLI status, Claude sign-in, SDK internals) stay provider-specific
supporting another provider in the copy is one new AGENTS entry, kept local to LandingPage because shared/providers.ts is capability data, not marketing copy
the closing panels say at least one of Claude Code or Codex must be installed on the paired machine

download first: the hero leads with the Mac download, then Get started, with Sign in in the header; with no build published the hero falls back to Get started and Sign in and the account panel spans the closing row alone

Notarized by Apple holds only from desktop 0.2.43, so the configured download link must serve the stable Lines-latest.dmg alias or a signed versioned build; the version shows only when the link names one

encryption copy says end-to-end encryption is on by default, that every browser enrols once with a code from the machine, that a guest connects with the key in their invite link, and that the relay carries traffic it cannot read or forge; it never claims everything is encrypted or zero-knowledge

privacy copy uses only the approved lines in the feature doc (agent runs on your machine; repos and full transcripts live on the machine and are never stored on Lines servers; live traffic between the machine and every browser on it, the user's or a guest's, is end-to-end encrypted, with the relay still seeing which device connects, when and how much; session list, workflows and memory sync to storage in plaintext; the bridge dials out and listens on the machine alone, so no port is open to the network; prompts go to the provider under the user's own account); 'your code never leaves your machine', 'transcripts and files never leave your machine', 'zero-knowledge' and 'we can't see anything' are banned
the Where your data goes section mirrors PRIVACY.md and links to it; a change to what is stored or relayed updates both together
shared links carry ?ref=<channel>, and the nginx access log is the only channel attribution
copy says works with Claude Code and Codex and never implies an Anthropic or OpenAI partnership or endorsement
the Mac panel points Windows and Linux users at running from source

the phone remote leads: the hero subtitle names the push to your phone and the From anywhere group is the first feature group, in the first wide tile; Plan & control (focus mode, inline plan comments, Approve or Refine with comments) takes the second wide tile, then Run agents, Review and Automate; the recipe library stays out of the hero until it has public content
architecturalRules: the rotating word sits on its own line with every word stacked in one grid cell and centred independently, so a short word leaves no gap and a long one never re-wraps the heading; mid-sentence placement shifts the surrounding text on every swap
the visible heading is aria-hidden and a VisuallyHidden sibling carries the full sentence naming every agent, so assistive tech never hears the words cycle
under prefers-reduced-motion the rotator renders the first word and starts no timer, with the CSS animation disabled as a second guard; the interval is cleared on unmount

hero words are split into letters: the outgoing word dissolves letter by letter, then the next forms; each letter paints its slice of one word-wide brand-colour gradient (AgentRotator measures width and offsets) that drifts slowly, with a solid-colour fallback where background-clip text is unsupported
the illustrations are decorative aria-hidden inline SVG using Mantine colour variables, so they follow the colour scheme; the card text carries the meaning

the app theme is monochrome (mono primary as a light/dark virtual colour, softened neutral dark scheme); status hues are muted OKLCH ramps on one shared lightness curve, with teal and cyan spread apart so done, needs answer and needs approval stay distinct, gray without its blue tint, and dark-scheme light-variant badges re-pointed in index.css to a translucent tint with hue text; the old sandstone and slate palettes are removed and needs-approval is cyan
header anchors scroll smoothly only while the landing page is mounted and never under prefers-reduced-motion
the header is a three-column grid with the action pinned to column 3, so the nav does not move while Clerk resolves the signed-in/out action
no analytics script and no third-party embed on either build: the app origin holds the end-to-end encryption keys, so measurement is server-side only (access log, /download redirect)
the download button links to /download in production builds, which the serving nginx 302s to DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_URL so every click is logged; dev builds link to the DMG directly
DemoVideo plays muted, looping and inline from a same-origin file; under prefers-reduced-motion it shows the poster with controls and never autoplays; it renders nothing if the file fails to load
og:image and og:url are absolute linesapp.cloud URLs, set identically in web/index.html and web/landing/index.html

the header action column holds a GitHub icon link beside Sign in / Open app, a plain link with no star-count fetch, since that would be a third-party request from the origin holding the encryption keys
the header Download button shows from md up only, since below that the row crowds and a phone cannot install it; the hero carries the download at every width

features.name: Find in files (Cmd+Shift+F)
features.purpose: Search the contents of every file in the active project from the sidebar search's Files scope, with results beside a main-pane file preview at the matching line.
businessRules: searches only the active project's roots, sharing hideIgnored with Cmd+P and the file tree
files over 1 MB and binary files are skipped; results are capped by files, matches and time and marked truncated
grep is all-or-nothing across roots: one root out of reach is a 403
an invalid regex is a 400 with an invalidRegex body; a bare 400 means an older bridge
results are shown only while they match the current query, roots and flags
a hit on a markdown file opens Raw at its line, not Preview, because a hit carries a line; picking another hit returns to Raw, and the toggle choice is not persisted

the preview is editable and saveable from its header, beside the close button (owner only, Raw only); picking another file's hit, closing the preview or search, or leaving the Files scope asks before discarding unsaved changes
after a save the current query re-runs if the saved file is among the hits, since line numbers may have shifted
architecturalRules: reuses the file-request handler, so auth, relay encryption and root containment are inherited
server search and web highlighting share buildMatcher
search yields to the event loop between batches of files
non-ignored files fill the candidate cap before ignored ones

features.name: Find in sessions
features.purpose: Search session transcripts from the sidebar, replace the session list with matching snippets, and jump to and highlight the hit in the transcript.
businessRules: searched text is prompts, interjections, assistant text, key tool-input fields and tool results; thinking, compacted spans and ephemeral system events are excluded
every session id is clamped through sessionInReach and the route needs the readFiles capability
Cmd/Ctrl+F opens session search and replaces browser find-in-page only while a project is open on a non-phone client
Esc closes the search from anywhere unless another handler took it, a Mantine overlay is open, or focus is in Monaco
old results are never shown while a new search loads
a jump into history not yet fetched triggers one loadTranscript for everything older than the first loaded event, then completes when it lands
architecturalRules: search is an overlay state over the session list, not a sidebar mode, and is never persisted
a hit's row is found from item keys that embed the event seq; items carry no separate seq
text highlighting uses the CSS Custom Highlight API, leaving the markdown tree untouched
search runs on the bridge because the transcript only mounts its most recent rows

features.name: What's new
features.purpose: Show a first-open-after-update card listing every user-facing web and desktop change since the versions this browser last saw, with the app loaded behind it, plus a permanent history in Settings.
businessRules: two tracks, web (__LINES_VERSION__) and desktop (bridge.version from the first hello), each with its own localStorage marker (lines.seenWeb, lines.seenDesktop); either one past its marker shows every release in between
a missing marker is written silently and shows nothing; markers only move forward
nextSeen caps at the newest release the bundle knows, so desktop notes stamped after a web deploy still show on a later load
decided once per page load, so a machine switch never reshows the card; guests never see it
desktop notes wait in desktopPending until ship.mjs stamps them with the version it bumps; the CI guard fails on a non-empty desktopPending

only user-facing feat or noticeable fix commits get an entry, one short user-worded line each; web/ paths go to the web track with a web/package.json patch bump, desktop/ server/ shared/ paths go to desktopPending
architecturalRules: the app mounts and loads behind the card; holdApp suspends the splash fallback timer so an open card is never faded away
the splash centres mark and card as one group while held and glides on size change; the layer clips outside shown, so the list scrolls inside the card
compareVersions lives in shared/changelog.ts and is re-exported from server/src/claudeCli.ts
changelog.json is read by web/vite.config.ts at config time and baked in, so the web image must copy it
